title: Curie architecture atlas
subtitle: The production loop, its swappable seams, and the distance between current state and vision.

architectureGroups.label: Channel surface
architectureGroups.subtitle: 3 implementations · 1 planned
architectureGroups.description: One stable channel role in the architecture. Slack, Discord and email have shipped implementations; the built-in email provider currently refuses inbound work because sender authentication is unverifiable. Teams remains planned. Implementation inventory is separate from supported adoption paths.

architectureGroups.label: Sandbox substrate
architectureGroups.subtitle: 2 proven implementations
architectureGroups.description: The stable substrate role beneath sandbox lifecycle. Kubernetes and Docker prove that the same boundary has multiple implementations.

architectureGroups.label: Bot capabilities
architectureGroups.subtitle: 1 shipped example, 2 patterns
architectureGroups.description: Reasons to buy rather than architecture peers of the worker or the runner. Each one is a bundle, an eval set, and an operating pattern that rides the isolated runtime. Expand to see the individual capabilities.

architectureGroups.label: Deployed agent
architectureGroups.subtitle: Identity, bundle, deployment
architectureGroups.description: One agent as an install sees it. An agent may be authored elsewhere; what Curie adds is an identity, a bundle it can deploy, and a channel to answer on. Expand to see the three parts.

overview.title: The request-to-reply loop
overview.description: Read left to right. Every colored connector is a seam: green is proven, yellow is clean but unproven, red is intertwined, and blue is planned.

stages.label: External surfaces
stages.description: A person, repository, or operator starts work.

stages.label: Ingress + API
stages.description: Authenticate, bind the agent, and turn the event into work.

stages.label: Queue + worker
stages.description: Claim delivery, lock the conversation, and resolve the run.

stages.label: Sandbox + runner
stages.description: Start or resume an isolated, steerable ACI session.

stages.label: Harness + MCP + model
stages.description: Run the multi-turn model loop, call hosted MCP tools, and produce side effects.

return.label: stream result, request approval when needed, then reply to the originating surface

rails.label: Approval loop
rails.description: Pause, authorize, and resume a live turn.

rails.label: Evidence plane
rails.description: Traces, telemetry, eval cases, scores, and results surround every run.

rails.label: Substrate
rails.description: Kubernetes is the production baseline; Docker proves the same sandbox boundary locally.

maturityRubric.label: Proven
maturityRubric.definition: Multiple real implementations have exercised the same boundary.

maturityRubric.label: Clean, unproven
maturityRubric.definition: One real implementation sits behind a credible boundary, but a second implementation has not tested the shape.

maturityRubric.label: Intertwined
maturityRubric.definition: A swap still requires coordinated knowledge or changes across implementation owners.

maturityRubric.label: Planned / reserved
maturityRubric.definition: The intended line is documented, but there is not a real implementation to score.

documentationDrift.title: ADR-0144 predates explicit namespace adoption
documentationDrift.claim: The draft ADR says there is no adopt flag and an operator must add created-owner labels manually.
documentationDrift.current: Explicit --adopt records the prior namespace contents and retains that namespace during teardown. Automatic adoption of an empty namespace can still assign deletion ownership.

documentationDrift.title: ADR-0144 predates the live schema assertion
documentationDrift.claim: The draft ADR says rollback has no override when the API pod cannot report its schema.
documentationDrift.current: The CLI accepts an operator-observed live schema revision while still enforcing the compatibility window before Helm mutates the release. Schema-gated dry runs also reject uncatalogued target applications without probing the live database, and every schema refusal includes its next step. A refused rollback also names history builds whose retained manifests declare a window containing the live schema. A dry run names only catalogued versions because it reads no retained manifests.

documentationDrift.title: ADR-0144 predates the quiesce-write fence
documentationDrift.claim: The draft ADR says the worker ignores a refused quiesce write and can strand its owned marker during cleanup.
documentationDrift.current: The worker checks the fenced write result, refuses the stale hook, and clears only the authoritative owned marker.

documentationDrift.title: ADRs 0125 and 0126 predate the installation level workspace gate
documentationDrift.claim: ADR 0125 specifies a nullable per-deployment repository; ADR 0126 replaces it with deployment workspace_enabled as the coding capability gate.
documentationDrift.current: The worker deliberately ignores that legacy deployment bit as a coding gate. The worker wide coordinator switch controls availability, while server scoped selection, the repository allowlist, and operator source bindings control workspace authority.

documentationDrift.title: ADR 0144 predates the resumable upgrade driver
documentationDrift.claim: The draft leaves resumable checkpoints, convergence, canary proof and interrupted-phase recovery open.
documentationDrift.current: The CLI now resolves and pins a target chart, validates its version and schema metadata before mutation, owns a namespaced checkpoint through resource version compare and set, resumes nine phases, proves exact convergence, runs a target version canary, and records the observed known good version. This does not establish the distributed execution lease proposed by the ADR. Failed phases now exit nonzero with their structured report. Interrupted rollback selection preserves a confirmed recorded target, and failed apply recovery conservatively checks live workload image maps. Cold release plans defer stock runner rebinding until target runner compatibility is observable. Apply now rebuilds retained repository runners before Helm and reruns after a pre-Helm build failure. Draft ADR 0230 proposes the shared lifecycle record but is not implemented.

documentationDrift.title: ADR 0173 predates implemented runner layering
documentationDrift.claim: ADR 0173 states that runner layering has no implementation.
documentationDrift.current: Bundles can build and select a layered runner with platform base validation. The release workflow now publishes the first party factory layer, and the renderer records layer and platform base digests.

documentationDrift.title: ADR 0184 predates supervised stream retention
documentationDrift.claim: The Draft context says no production code runs XTRIM or XDEL on the consumed streams.
documentationDrift.current: The worker constructs and supervises StreamRetention, whose trim_settled pass runs XTRIM MINID below every consumer group settlement floor after the lag window. This does not establish the proposed Postgres receipts or counted-backlog changes. ADR 0237 retains ordinary hook receipts in Valkey, separately from the proposed Postgres receipt migration.

documentationDrift.title: ADR 0203 predates argument-bound permission grants
documentationDrift.claim: Its context describes post-approval grants as tool-name scoped rather than argument scoped.
documentationDrift.current: Permission grants require canonical equality with the approved argument object. The model-free action executor and automated remediation admission, independent reads and breaker paths are now implemented; qualified installation authority remains a separate gate.

documentationDrift.title: ADR 0144 predates the final roll hold hook
documentationDrift.claim: The draft says only a clean drain extends the pause to the roll hold.
documentationDrift.current: A clean drain leaves a 300 second lease; attest and migration renew it, and the final pre-upgrade hold hook alone extends it to the roll hold.

documentationDrift.title: Approval interface predates bare-name boot refusal
documentationDrift.claim: The approval interface says alias gates silently arm nothing and produce a warning.
documentationDrift.current: Unknown bare operator names and CLI aliases now raise ApprovalPolicyError and refuse runner boot.

documentationDrift.title: Controller guide predates scoped refusals and restart recovery
documentationDrift.claim: The chart guide treats any current forbidden-NetworkPolicy line and historical restart or lease failure as fatal.
documentationDrift.current: Current cluster-scope list/watch refusals and restart-count growth are fatal. Namespaced refusals and previous-container failures remain diagnostic, and a recovered current container can prove serving health.

documentationDrift.title: ADR 0220 context predates implemented identity links and resolution
documentationDrift.claim: ADR 0220 says no link table, resolver or creation flow is implemented.
documentationDrift.current: Migration 0107 and the current models implement tenant-scoped identity namespaces and links, with ordered Slack principal resolution through exact active links. Migrations 0120 through 0122 add team sync state, agent access policies and directory identity; the scoped directory API, one-time connect and invocation and approver team enforcement are implemented. The schema still accepts provider_event_verified and admin_mapped verification sources, and agents without a team still use binding allowed_callers and native Slack sets or exact email lists.

documentationDrift.title: ADR 0220 describes an email authentication path that is currently refused
documentationDrift.claim: ADR 0220 section 4 describes authenticated aligned DMARC sender checks as the current email path.
documentationDrift.current: The email adapter refuses every inbound message with authentication_unverifiable before body fetching when its provider declares no sender verification. AgentMail, the only built-in provider, declares none, so no email starts a turn or resolves an approval. Governed-domain IdP email links remain planned.

documentationDrift.title: Forge interface predates the Cloud unconfirmed refusal
documentationDrift.claim: The interface says rediscovery drops every unverified publication before matching.
documentationDrift.current: Bitbucket Cloud refuses unverified open matching publications as unconfirmed; other providers and completed unverified matches remain excluded.

documentationDrift.title: ADR 0143 predates moved-base first publication
documentationDrift.claim: The accepted ADR describes one exact deterministic approved commit and recovery against its recorded expected parent.
documentationDrift.current: For the first nonempty publication only, the Job can replay the approved patch onto a descendant of the immutable approved base. The API proves the revision marker, one parent and both ancestry relations to the current selected-branch tip, then records the actual parent under fenced settlement. Later revisions keep exact prior-head parent proof. The ADR has not been amended to describe this first-publication exception. Each ancestry relation is now one forge is_ancestor request. GitHub answers from one three-dot compare status rather than a bounded parent walk.

documentationDrift.title: ADR 0195 predates current-attempt check ordering
documentationDrift.claim: The accepted ADR says any concluded non-passing required check on the tagged commit is contrary evidence and refuses release authorization.
documentationDrift.current: The authorizer orders attempts of each required name by completed_at, otherwise started_at, and judges only the latest attempts when every attempt is orderable. A later successful rerun can supersede an earlier failure or cancellation. A current failure or skip still blocks, and missing timestamps retain conservative evaluation of all attempts. ADR 0247 adds two inheritance paths under that same rule: a tree-identical parent, including a merge's second parent, is tried before the version-only walk, and registering only this release's schema window as the ancestor's candidate stays inside the walk. ADR 0195's frozen text still says any concluded non-passing required check refuses and that a second parent is never the proof. ADR 0247 amends the second-parent exclusion for identical trees and restates that a concluded non-passing own check refuses, without describing latest-attempt ordering.

documentationDrift.title: ADR 0249 names migration 0136
documentationDrift.claim: ADR 0249 says migration 0136 replaces the deadline checks and is the realizing migration.
documentationDrift.current: The deadline ceiling change is migration 0140, which revises 0123. ARCHITECTURE.md records ADR 0249 as enforced by migration 0140. This tree has no migration 0136.

documentationDrift.title: Chart values comments still cap delivery at three hours
documentationDrift.claim: charts/curie/values.yaml says the delivery budget must be between 60 and 10800 seconds, the runner ceiling must be at most 10800 seconds, and values.schema.json enforces those maxima. It also says a rollout at the 10800 second maximum takes about three hours per pod.
documentationDrift.current: values.schema.json allows both fields up to 43200 seconds, and the worker rejects only a budget above 43200. The shipped defaults remain 10800 seconds. The comments describe the old maximum.

documentationDrift.title: Factory bundle guide understates the platform deadline ceiling
documentationDrift.claim: The factory bundle README still says the maximum execution duration is 10800 seconds.
documentationDrift.current: The platform permits 60 through 43200 seconds under migration 0140. The bundle review hook uses execution_seconds and execution_deadline returned by get_issue, so a 10800 second quickstart default is not the platform maximum.

nodes.label: Slack
nodes.subtitle: Surface today
nodes.description: The original production channel. Bolt Socket Mode handles ingress; Slack Web API renders replies and approval cards. Progress rendering helpers exist, but deliberate progress delivery is disabled. It is no longer the only registered production kind. A streamed reply edit is cut to the 4,000 byte chat.update limit at a line break with a visible note. One installation can route several separate bot applications. Final replies and the stored progress outbox use stable delivery identity, and the receipt shown at turn end follows the installation mode. A long final answer is partitioned into sequential keyed continuation messages under a 4,000-byte edit limit instead of being cut, and a verbatim answer is one rich text section of text and literal link elements per partition, so the approved characters and line breaks stay exact without a code box (ADR 0250). A part Slack refuses as msg_too_long is resent as smaller parts, each with its own key. A smaller part that is also refused is replaced by a notice so the reply still completes.

nodes.label: Discord
nodes.subtitle: Shipped surface
nodes.description: Out-of-process Gateway adapter. Mentions in a bound parent channel create a public thread and placeholder; later thread messages continue the same conversation. v1 supports text, mentions, threads, and streamed edits. It does not implement buttons, DMs, attachments, or interactive approvals, and a Discord failure never falls back to Slack. The adapter now uses the shared telemetry bootstrap and redacting JSON logger for its own package plus discord.py, uvicorn, and httpx. OTLP export is supported, although the adapter still authors no spans or instruments.

nodes.label: Email
nodes.subtitle: Shipped surface
nodes.description: First-party AgentMail adapter with a scoped HTTP channel edge and threaded reply delivery. Current AgentMail inbound messages cannot establish sender authentication Curie can verify, so every message is refused with authentication_unverifiable before body fetching, starting a turn, or resolving an approval. Historical accepted deliveries can still receive one threaded reply per turn.completed. Delivery state is local SQLite with one serialized writer. Terminal completion rows compact oldest first under a derived cap without evicting unresolved or leased work, and an oversized database has an offline copy and VACUUM recovery command. Transport failures and all 4xx discovery refusals enter bounded backoff. Provider, channel, and egress credentials may come from per-field existing Secrets without chart ownership of their values. An external collector requires a narrow chart-declared egress peer.  The adapter uses shared telemetry and credential redaction, including OTLP export and startup-failure logs, without a generic environment-injection surface. Provider dialing stays within configured egress CIDRs while TLS verifies the provider hostname. Sustained discovery failure makes readiness fail after a bounded interval and appears in status; liveness stays independent and the Service retains reply delivery to the unready adapter. A refused provider TCP connection is classified separately during thread witness and send, returning a retryable 424 without treating it as a deleted thread or a completed delivery. An approval can be requested through email under the accepted route decision. Scoped approval-resolution authorization and email card delivery are implemented, but current inbound provider replies are refused before that resolution path. A live single use reference identifies the pending approval, while the platform checks the sender against binding callers and listed approvers. Requests go to existing thread participants; the adapter does not invite an absent approver itself. Replies in a thread with a pending approval do not start ordinary turns. Helm upgrades roll this component's consumers when a consumed chart-owned Secret value changes. Foreign Secret contents rotated in place require a separate rollout. Accepted ADR 0220 plans exact-address identity links supplied by the IdP only for governed domains, with separately verifiable sender authentication required before resolution. Governed-domain email links remain planned, and the current AgentMail authentication refusal remains. Accepted ADR 0228 is implemented: the neutral adapter keeps the channel protocol, delivery state, inbound gate, the rebuilt intake path and approvals by email, while a versioned MailProvider selected by CURIE_MAIL_PROVIDER lists, reads, replies, finds reply markers, maps failures to neutral kinds and reports the sender verdict. AgentMail is the built-in provider and declares no sender verification, so it still refuses every inbound message; a conformance kit gates out-of-tree providers. When an agent has an invocation or approver team, email callers resolve only through an exact IdP email link before the team membership check.

nodes.label: Curie CLI
nodes.subtitle: Agent-facing control
nodes.description: Drives skill, local, and cluster loops. The local/cluster message verbs can replace Slack ingress and reply transport without changing the worker path. Operators can mint and rotate row-scoped channel tokens, while status and doctor expose bounded completion-outbox and mail-delivery health without identifiers. The checkout-only release-accept evaluator reads a private evidence ledger and fails closed unless one unchanged candidate has seven days of accounted canaries and every recovery criterion. Push delivery diagnosis distinguishes configured, reachable, observed, and verified states instead of treating repository binding as delivery proof. A bare curie doctor discovers the platform API from cluster state, cluster up --dev preserves recorded comms and sealing values, and release builds embed the exact source commit used to resolve installer artifacts. Plain cluster up, apply, and diff retain installed typed mail settings, external Secret pairs, paired worker adapter credentials, and installed local inference. Explicit namespace adoption records prior labels and objects, and cluster down retains the adopted namespace. Hosted connector deploys wait for current revision readiness; skill and local connector startup share one configurable bounded deadline. Explicit source decisions take precedence without replaying stale inline credentials. Offline dry-run plans do not read an installed release. Cluster up and apply wait for the installed Helm target workloads to converge; cluster status returns failure with redacted generation, replica, image and hook diagnoses when the target is unhealthy. Cluster upgrade resolves the selected release chart or explicit local/ref target, pins it to the requested version, validates declared chart version and rendered target schema metadata before mutation, and requires explicit forward-only admission for pending contract or irreversible migrations. One namespaced ConfigMap owns the operation and its durable nine-phase checkpoint through resourceVersion and holder compare-and-set. A resumed upgrade proves exact target images, generations, replicas, hooks, queues, and manifest state, then runs a target-version canary and records known-good from the observed release version. The CLI rollback catalog for v0.9.0 spans migrations 0001 through 0044; it is distinct from that release's API image serving compatibility window of 0044 through 0044. The 0.9.2 and 0.9.3 release identities each carry the exact 0045 through 0045 schema window because no migration landed between them. CI refuses a new migration unless the release windows advance consistently. The restore and upgrade drills exercise stable installation survival and recovery. Sibling tag image reports require a unique serving Node inventory binding and conditional Node read; this does not prove mutable tag freshness. An explicit cluster context pins every Helm and kubectl child. Channel token operations refuse failed release discovery instead of guessing a Secret name. Retained up escapes literal dotted object keys, while upgrade preserves scalar types through JSON values. Ambiguous 0.8.8 and 0.8.9 rollback identities require retained schema metadata. Local commands and ladder runs honor explicit Compose project and endpoint settings. The 0.10.0 and 0.10.1 release identities share schema window 0045 through 0058. A bundle deploy leaves the platform release alone unless a connector secret name is new or its value changed. Worker status and doctor report a paused fleet's remaining quiesce TTL, and the example sre-bot provision-observability verb records a receipt naming the Grafana connector Secret without the token. The historical v0.11.0 release uses API schema 0070; the historical release windows remain separately recorded for upgrade admission. The 0.11.2 release identity carries schema window 0070 through 0070. Upgrade refuses absent or partial caller credential pairs before mutation, including dry run, same version verification, and resume; upgrade does not generate a missing pair. Budget updates preserve unspecified values. Factory rendering selects the published runner layer and emits a strict version 2 receipt with required bundle_dir, rendered, runner_image, and runner_note fields. The runner fields accept string or null, unknown fields are rejected, the schema ID ends in /v2.json, and its index version is 2.0. The App completion path explicitly selects factory polling without requiring a webhook secret. Operators can control memory writes and guidance. Factory render receipt schema v2 requires nullable runner_image and runner_note fields. Local and cluster Console login commands discover the installation credential and mint a subject-bound single-use login code. Cluster up retains recorded runner environment and credential references; cluster upgrade deletes removed runner layers instead of setting them to null. nodes.label: Forges
nodes.subtitle: Trackers + code hosts
nodes.description: Webhook and outbound commit polling converge on the API git-flow engine. Dev pushes build and evaluate; production pushes promote. Repository binding is not delivery proof: pushes arrive through either an operator-created webhook or configured commit polling, and Curie reports only observed configuration rather than claiming that exposure proves delivery. The platform also clones managed workspaces and publishes through an approval-gated path that never leaves write credentials inside the sandbox. One scoped thread and repository own one fenced pull request lineage. Human issue comments, pull request review comments, and submitted reviews are admitted only for the currently open bound pull request after fresh provider reads confirm the immutable repository, installation, pull request, binding generation, and exact head. Accepted feedback enters a durable outbox for the original scoped thread; stale heads, terminal pull requests, unavailable provider truth, and authority mismatches start no model turn. Signed labelled issue events now admit one canonical factory WorkItem, while relabel, unlabel, issue comments, and review events retain distinct authority checks. Factory status and final outcome comments use the GitHub issue as their operator surface. Because GitHub does not redeliver a failed webhook, the API reconciler also polls bound repositories for factory labelled issues with no WorkItem and admits them with a request identity derived from the labeled event. Factory state labels moved to the curie-factory prefix. Covered factory publication turns can compare a proposed title and body against a fresh API side pull request read without any GitHub credential entering the sandbox. Factory intake now defaults to outbound polling with optional webhook delivery. The platform reads the issue through a scoped capability with its own fresh App token; the factory sandbox needs no GitHub read credential. Factory review admission retains the issue cancellation lock until the revision request and delivery settlement commit together; nested dispatch commits use savepoints. GitHub and GitLab provide tracker and code-host roles. Jira Cloud provides the tracker role; Bitbucket Cloud and Data Center provide code hosts. Roles remain separate when work tracking and source hosting differ. GitHub publication discovery filters one raw response page at a time and retains only owned matching publications, keeping pagination memory bounded by a page plus matches. Feedback-only repositories also poll conversation comments on owned open pull requests without admitting new issue work. Factory CI now defaults to 3600 seconds from push, still capped by the execution deadline and preserving explicit operator values. GitHub reads base-branch ruleset and branch-protection required-check names. A required name absent from the published head stays pending until the deadline, then ends ci_unverified and names the missing trigger without applying it. Transient rule-read failures can time out; permanent unreadability refuses immediately. Other code hosts declare required-check reads unsupported rather than simulating them. Code hosts answer ancestry with one is_ancestor request. GitHub uses one three-dot compare and only its status. A cancelled GitHub Actions run is ignored when a later run with the same key and head has a newer start, or a higher check id when the starts match. A cancellation with no newer same-key run still counts. Operator-configured GitHub labels, at most ten names for one exact repository, are applied once to an open non-draft factory pull request. A forge or marker error leaves the publication in place, and publication does not apply labels to start a required check.

nodes.label: External hook
nodes.subtitle: HMAC-triggered turn
nodes.description: A named, HMAC-authenticated API hook creates a quota- and body-bounded webhook-sourced turn whose authenticated payload is escaped and delimited as untrusted prompt content. For alert-driven coding, an operator-owned source binding extracts a configured workload fact and maps it to an allowlisted repository plus recorded revision. Missing, ambiguous, malformed, or unauthorized mappings refuse before workspace selection, and payload URLs never choose the target. Declared cron schedules ship; deploy wiring for declared generic webhooks remains planned. A hook may explicitly request tool_access=read-only. Its receipt proves the queued policy only; an operator must establish compatible worker and runner artifacts because the API does not discover homogeneous fleet enforcement. An authenticated hook may select a preposted reply context under the signed request contract. Signed ingress now repeats authentication under a dedicated live SQL source gate. Configured policy or durable operation history refuses the ordinary path before delivery effects. Hook-specific signing, source control, broker metadata and atomic protected admission primitives exist, but protected provisioning, worker consumption and qualified runtime execution are not wired into this route. Protected admission recovery rereads concurrent commit observations within a 32-attempt bound while retaining stable orphan refusal. Ordinary hook enqueue atomically retains a bounded receipt beside its permanent Valkey claim, preserving the original stream ID, conversation and selected tool policy after stream trimming. Faithful completed retries can return that receipt without the original queued turn. Mismatched, malformed or orphan receipt metadata refuses with 409. Legacy claims without receipt metadata still require the original queue entry.

nodes.label: Console UI
nodes.subtitle: Operations surface
nodes.description: A real API-backed console for fleet, runs, metrics, cost, logs, versions, evals, approvals, and memory. Approval resolution uses the authenticated Console session subject rather than a caller-supplied actor. Usage and Settings remain honest stubs. An external API requires an explicit proxy target; chart rendering refuses a disabled in-chart API without that target. Agent cards and the Overview card show each agent's runs, tokens, and cost from the metrics summary, and show unknown cost when the model has no price. Console session creation and reads have separate shared Valkey budgets. The browser now authenticates only with the HttpOnly Console session cookie. A single-use CLI-minted login code is exchanged for that session; protected views mount only after the session probe succeeds, and a protected request returning 401 returns the UI to sign-in. Browser configuration and API requests no longer carry the platform administrator key. Cookie-authenticated mutations require a matching origin. Its other session-authenticated API calls are ordinary control-plane traffic; the map draws only the trace and metrics read path, which belongs to the telemetry seam, and attributes no seam to the generic traffic. The read-only Factory view displays work item lanes, stage progress and cost. The backend implements generic OIDC authentication; complete console SSO entry remains separate work. Accepted ADR 0220 keeps future people, teams, links and sync-status administration read-only, with identity and membership changes made in the IdP. These administration views and the one-time IdP account-connect confirmation remain planned.

nodes.label: Dispatcher
nodes.subtitle: Ingress · dedupe · placeholder
nodes.description: Before Socket Mode, a bounded startup preflight waits for API health and verifies configured Slack destination capabilities. The live dispatcher then normalizes Slack events and Block Kit text into QueuedTurn, carries adapter scoped file references without downloading their bytes, records adapter owned refusals, deduplicates ingress, posts the placeholder, and appends to the run stream. If posting the placeholder fails, the dispatcher keeps the claim and still enqueues the turn with a null placeholder, and the worker posts the answer as a fresh thread reply. Bot authored thread messages are admitted only for explicitly trusted bot and channel pairs. Approval clicks become independently signed, approval bound chat principal attestations; an exact record miss is treated as another release owning that approval, never as authority to mutate it. Its single Deployment replica uses a Recreate rollout so Socket Mode never runs two clients on one app token; Slack retries delivery across the reconnect gap. One installation can now run several declared Slack identities and route each event through its owning application. A binding caller list is checked before a placeholder or turn is created. For a threaded mention, a bounded lookup verifies this bot authored the root and quotes it as untrusted context with slashes neutralized; that context grants no new routing authority. Configured and connected Socket Mode identity counts are measured independently of the process heartbeat. Helm upgrades roll this component's consumers when a consumed chart-owned Secret value changes. Foreign Secret contents rotated in place require a separate rollout. Repeated native Socket Mode session failures are counted in a bounded window and escalate to the supervisor; isolated reconnects can recover without escalation. Caller admission now honors the agent's invocation team through the API and reuses a cached decision only under a currently verified identity fence generation for the same caller and signed transport evidence. Socket Mode counts frames per configured identity with hello, disconnect, events_api, interactive, slash_commands and other types, and forwards SDK session lifecycle logs through the service logger. Slack identity labels admit at most 16 valid slugs per process before folding into other. Mentions in explicitly configured delivery-canary channels are counted and dropped after envelope validation, before relevance, principal lookup, approval handling, admission or dedupe: no API read, placeholder or queued turn is created. Frame counts expose received traffic; a delivery-canary count proves only that the configured mention reached that identity, separately from process heartbeat and connected-identity counts. The mutation that publishes the identity fence keeps its writer session isolated until settlement.

nodes.label: Port adapter service
nodes.subtitle: Third-party channel edge
nodes.description: The accepted placement for a generic third-party adapter kit: a deployed service, not a bundle-loaded plugin. Slack, Discord, and email already ship as first-party surfaces. The generic adapter manifest, install flow, service discovery, and conformance kit remain unbuilt.

nodes.label: Channel HTTP edge
nodes.subtitle: Generic ingress + egress
nodes.description: The API mints row-scoped channel tokens and platform-owned QueuedTurn records; every mint increments the row generation before signing, so reminting immediately revokes the prior token. A separately scoped adapter principal can rotate its own credential, mint channel tokens only for bindings it serves, list approvals on those routes, and resolve eligible explicit-user approvals. Discord and email already consume this HTTP edge. Worker-side HttpReplyAdapter posts the four versioned reply events to each binding's server-controlled endpoint, while the reserved built-in cluster-message relay returns CLI-driven replies through the API. TurnIn carries Attachment references onto the queue. Non Slack references are resolved at the binding's attachment endpoint through ChannelPortFileClient with the adapter egress credential; Discord and mail still emit no references. In a disconnected cluster relay, adapter selects reply delivery while optional ReplyHandle.identity selects the named Slack binding; unknown identities refuse. Approvals and publications persist the named Slack relay reply_identity separately from reply_adapter. The reserved cluster-message adapter still selects delivery; default identity and non-relay selectors normalize to null.

nodes.label: API
nodes.subtitle: Control plane · git flow
nodes.description: Owns agents, versions, deployments, multi-surface channel bindings, approvals, state, connector rendering, managed repository workspaces, bundle validation, git flow deploys, and read proxies. An opt-in break-glass route can report approval identity gaps and reject a stranded approval with an atomic audit entry and ordinary resume event. A transcript over its per-thread cap increments a bounded value-limit counter, state namespace capacity refusals have their own counters, and readiness remains independent of data capacity. Redacted action snapshots retain neither prior nor post state and cannot support undo. Successful state deletes and operator memory edits and deletes emit content free operation logs and bounded mutation counts; no value or memory content enters those observations. Requester display follows only a validated approval resume chain and does not change grant or resolution authority. Factory issue and comment reads use an execution scoped route and fresh App installation tokens owned by the API. Live execution and lease authority are validated around provider reads, and bounded Valkey attempts limit access. Canonical factory verification observations gate publication, and one Actions rerun on the exact current head precedes CI repair. It sends observations through the existing verification and admission path. Memory authority is checked at the state API: a sandbox can read only its own channel memory and needs a turn credential for fact writes; the server records the author. Transcript scope is also checked against the binding. Progress commands enter a generation scoped durable inbox, with rendering disabled. A live Console session now authenticates ordinary administrative API requests; cookie-authenticated mutations enforce same-origin authority. Hook source policy and immutable operation history are durable SQL state. Signed hook authentication is repeated under a dedicated agent-scoped source gate, whose continued liveness is checked before effects. Any configured source policy or operation history closes the current ordinary ingress path. Source administration and mutation coordinators exist as internal primitives, without a complete protected HTTP delivery path. Startup probes require readable source-policy and operation structures before runtime construction. Failed resume enqueues observed by the current API process are retried on the next reconciler pass. The process record is capped at 10,000 approvals; restart loss and failures beyond that cap retain the grace backstop. A short locked transaction enqueues before marking resumed and retains still-owed locked rows for another pass. Scheduled and manual hook runs have independent histories and nullable terminal reason codes. Per-agent reviewer_model is nullable; explicit null clears it while omission preserves it. The v0.12.5 candidate API and shared serving window are 0076 through 0106. When head checks fail, factory CI reads the current base branch head within the remaining observation budget. Matching failing check names or status contexts are reported as pre-existing and excluded from repair, but required Python or delegated checks failing on that base remain unverified. An unreadable base makes every head failure count as caused. A refused factory publication snapshot ends with approval_create_failed and carries the existing redacted, clipped refusal detail into the issue Details line. A sanitized-base mismatch names the first 12 hexadecimal characters of both snapshot and prepared commits; repository mismatch wording and refusal behavior remain unchanged. Publication prose reports CI at pull request creation time and points to the issue status comment for subsequent results. An owner-lost factory request settles before a new attempt is admitted on the same WorkItem, bounded to three consecutive owner losses. Status cards show RETRYING only when a successor was admitted; other failed and expired requests show NEEDS HUMAN. Acquired but unstarted requests renew their short lease every twenty seconds. Only not_started deferrals count toward the default five-attempt start cap; capacity and thread-busy waits do not. Started factory CI and approval continuations wait for sandbox capacity within their existing delivery and execution deadlines without charging runner retries. Factory status synchronization owns a versioned SQL lease, releases database sessions before GitHub I/O, and runs separately from dispatch reconciliation. Late matching runtime heartbeats may renew before the execution deadline, with one heartbeat-TTL grace before owner-loss cancellation. Verification replay preserves the first observation for an unchanged command. CI reports unavailable required check names and merge_conflict explicitly instead of waiting for checks GitHub will not start. A metadata-only CI repair uses the configured repository metadata policy, or, when none exists, failing check names and status contexts recorded in Valkey for that repair round. Recorded guards must rerun after the metadata edit to prove success. No fresh recorded rerun ends with checks_not_rerun; partial reruns retain failures that did not rerun at the deadline. Missing or invalid records remain metadata_ci_not_configured. Configured policy remains authoritative. The historical v0.12.3 released window is 0076 through 0093; v0.12.2 remains 0076 through 0081. The scoped issue read returns the current execution deadline and total granted seconds. The factory workflow paces its foreground reviews, implementation and verification against that reported grant, rather than assuming a three hour grant. The reported grant can be as long as 43200 seconds. Quickstart now defaults to 10800 seconds, while explicit shorter grants remain authoritative. The historical v0.12.4 released window remains 0076 through 0093. Migration 0106 follows 0093 and adds nullable reply_identity columns to approvals and publications. Approvals and publications persist named relay reply_identity independently of reply_adapter, normalizing default identity and non-relay routes to null. Resolution restores ReplyHandle.identity; publication admission and replay compare the selector against the selected Slack binding. Helm upgrades roll this component's consumers when a consumed chart-owned Secret value changes. Foreign Secret contents rotated in place require a separate rollout. Factory review admission retains the issue cancellation lock until the revision request and delivery settlement commit together; nested dispatch commits use savepoints. A publication attempt with no valid recorded publication reports publication_unrecorded and preserves redacted refusal detail in the issue outcome. The API disables FastAPI automatic telemetry configuration so the shared service bootstrap owns export and trace parentage. Its python -m curie_api entrypoint preserves shared logging handlers; Uvicorn access and error logs use the same redaction and telemetry configuration. Chart rendering accepts an empty GitHub App ID or a positive integral value of 1 to 18 decimal digits, preserving string digits without lossy numeric coercion and refusing malformed values. The factory core resolves typed tracker and code-host bindings. OIDC login, tenant scoping and provider namespace identity links are implemented, with unresolved senders returning explicit reasons. Model-free action and remediation authority live in the API. Accepted ADR 0220 plans read-only IdP people, group membership, account status and known channel accounts, with complete versioned membership snapshots and independent versioned status updates. Membership retains its last known state during sync outages, while sync health remains visible. Directory snapshot application, IdP status delivery, agent-wide invocation and approver policies, and the one-time account-connect flow remain planned; provider-specific directory adapters remain external integrations. Factory acquisition returns authenticated agent, tenant, binding and surface context; start and continuation adoption revalidate that authority. Tracker intake holds an unavailable issue without starving others, discovers initial Jira labels, and checks existing owned publications before replay. Static forge credentials refresh per operation, with redacted credential health. Bind and arm require an API-only remediation authority key independent of the platform key. Source policy routes compose ProvisionedSourceAuthority from provisioned runtime files. Status synchronization releases interrupted claims on shutdown. Bitbucket Cloud refuses an unverified open matching publication as unconfirmed and asks the operator to confirm; this grants no ownership or continuation authority. Tracker intake names credential repair actions and reports missing or inaccessible repositories. A pull request closed without merging ends CI wait as pr_closed before check evaluation. An unpublished revision with a recorded pull request ends as revision_unchanged. Handoff messages retain up to 4000 characters and render as quoted text with HTML, images and mentions neutralized. Budget stops omit raw verification preflight notes, and Jira links the first succeeded publication. Ordinary hook enqueue atomically retains a bounded receipt beside its permanent Valkey claim, preserving the original stream ID, conversation and selected tool policy after stream trimming. Faithful completed retries can return that receipt without the original queued turn. Mismatched, malformed or orphan receipt metadata refuses with 409. Legacy claims without receipt metadata still require the original queue entry. Sandbox state credential release checks retry Valkey connection and timeout faults four times with 0.2, 0.4 and 0.8 second delays before failing closed. The API now serves scoped IdP directory ingestion, team sync reads and metrics, agent access policies, identity administration reads and a one-time identity connect page. Channel ingress applies the agent's invocation team, and mutations that change identity state serialize behind an admission fence. Migrations 0120 through 0122 are the v0.14.0 schema head; the CLI registers the v0.14.0 window with minimum and head 0122. A separate commissioning ingress application exists for protected commissioning; the ordinary API never mounts it. For a first publication, the writer fetches the API-authoritative base branch and, if its tip advanced, replays the approved patch onto that descendant tip. Conflict, empty replay, unrelated history and replay failure stop publication. The API verifies the revision marker and one parent, proves the approved base is an ancestor of that parent and the parent is an ancestor of the current base tip, with one is_ancestor request per relation. GitHub answers from the status of one three-dot compare. Equal shas count as ancestors, and a forge that cannot answer leaves the publication unproved. The immutable approval base stays unchanged; lineage settlement records the actual first parent under publication, lease and lineage fences. Later revisions still require the exact prior published head. Factory CI now defaults to 3600 seconds from push, still capped by the execution deadline and preserving explicit operator values. GitHub reads base-branch ruleset and branch-protection required-check names. A required name absent from the published head stays pending until the deadline, then ends ci_unverified and names the missing trigger without applying it. Transient rule-read failures can time out; permanent unreadability refuses immediately. Other code hosts declare required-check reads unsupported rather than simulating them. Migration 0123 stores a redacted workspace preparation stage and reason, capped at 2000 characters, as last_start_failure_detail. Capacity deferrals and worker replacement preserve it; a successful-start compare-and-set clears it. Waiting, exhausted-start and capacity-expiry outcomes retain the previous start diagnosis instead of replacing it with a generic capacity reason. The v0.14.1 application window requires schema minimum and head 0123. The v0.14.3 and v0.14.4 application windows and candidate serving metadata all declare schema minimum and head 0140. With factory.enabled, the API Deployment and schema-migrate Job default to a shared 2Gi memory limit; other installs default to 512Mi. Explicit api.resources.limits.memory wins, including retained 512Mi under --reuse-values. Memory requests remain 256Mi and CPU remains 100m request and 1 limit. The 2Gi choice is headroom rather than a demonstrated memory requirement. A new publication from a running request is refused unless that request still has its runtime owner, an unexpired heartbeat lease, and an unexpired execution deadline, rechecked on the database clock after the row locks. An identity mutation uses a writer session that stays isolated until settlement, and is refused when that writer cannot be isolated. A re-admitted run can retire an open headless lineage only when it has failed publications whose outcomes are durable, all belonging to terminal failed executions of one uncancelled WorkItem for the same agent, thread and repository. The API first proves remote branch absence through CodeHost, then locks and rechecks eligibility and the observed lineage version before closing it. A surviving branch or any unavailable or unauthorized read preserves the old pin. Retired rows without a pull request read as absent; rows carrying a pull request remain terminal. After a GitHub ref 404, branch_head requires a successful matching-refs read and accepts only an exact ref match with a valid commit id. This permission-bearing read distinguishes confirmed absence from hidden or inaccessible content; malformed, forbidden or unavailable results cannot authorize retirement. v0.14.4 registers the existing 0140 through 0140 schema window without a new migration.

nodes.label: Valkey streams
nodes.subtitle: Runs · evals · delivery
nodes.description: At-least-once streams carry run and eval jobs. Shared consumer machinery provides bounded delivery, a renewable fenced owner per delivery, lease-expiry recovery, and dead-letter handling. Conversation locks are stamped with consumer ownership and can transfer only after capability plus sustained missing-alive proof. The same bounded graveyard also retains terminal completion-outbox failures, which are not replayable inbound entries. An external Valkey can require TLS; one shared chart helper keeps all seven consumers on the same transport and refuses TLS for the in-chart broker without a TLS listener. Interactive turns now park in a durable capacity wait when a sandbox cannot start. A fixed deadline, generation fence, wake reconciliation, and terminal notice prevent an unbounded or silently lost wait; the runner grants admission to the exact waiting turn epoch before input is sent. The supervised retention loop trims entries older than its lag window only below every consumer group settlement floor. Protected broker metadata transport, permission roles and atomic admission with bounded recovery are implemented as internal primitives; a complete separately deployed protected delivery endpoint and consumer remain planned. Delivery and consumer liveness renewals tolerate transport errors only until the last confirmed send plus TTL minus one heartbeat interval. A refused renewal loses authority immediately. Side-effect markers retry before applying the frame, and terminal settlement remains fenced. Runs and evals share this ownership rule. Helm upgrades roll this component's consumers when a consumed chart-owned Secret value changes. Foreign Secret contents rotated in place require a separate rollout. Parked capacity waits retry every five seconds, capped at the deadline, without repeating an already delivered notice when no grant was confirmed and the grant is known absent. Ordinary hook enqueue atomically retains a bounded receipt beside its permanent Valkey claim, preserving the original stream ID, conversation and selected tool policy after stream trimming. Faithful completed retries can return that receipt without the original queued turn. Mismatched, malformed or orphan receipt metadata refuses with 409. Legacy claims without receipt metadata still require the original queue entry.

nodes.label: Worker kernel
nodes.subtitle: Route · claim · steer · recover
nodes.description: The concurrency hub: resolves the active deployment, emits a typed terminal failure instead of dropping turns when none exists, enforces one live session per scoped conversation, selects steer versus fresh turn, and protects side effects. It resolves channel attachment references through the selected Slack file client or ChannelPortFileClient. The latter fetches opaque ids from the binding endpoint with its adapter egress credential; accepted bytes are stored under a private prefix and exposed through a short lived signed redemption reference before sandbox claim. Managed coding uses the canonical scoped thread identity rather than a bare reply id. The worker selects and sanitizes an allowlisted repository checkout, archives it privately, and swaps a late workspace into the route only at a fenced turn boundary; multiple ambiguous bare owner/repo-like tokens leave repository selection absent, while multiple explicit repository URLs are refused. Review turns never steer a live sandbox: fresh authority is verified again, the exact accepted pull request head is reserved and materialized, and a replacement sandbox cold-claims that checkout. Publication validates a revision against its base, captures the immutable GitHub repository, installation, and pull request node identities in the same write that opens the pull request, creates a fresh approval, and reconciles approved work through the same pull request lineage; stale, terminal, unavailable, or mismatched authority is refused before model or write work. Runs, evals, kill switch, heartbeat, connector, publication, and completion loops are individually supervised with exponential backoff; a repeatedly crashing loop is parked after a bounded streak while siblings continue. Terminal reply events enter a durable, generation fenced completion outbox before the done marker; independent bounded sweeps retry delivery and quarantine expired or malformed records. Each runner request is capped by both the configured runner ceiling and the delivery's remaining deadline. Upgrade drain refuses a fenced quiesce write and holds its quiesce marker as a short lease renewed while the gate waits, so a killed or deleted gate releases the fleet within one lease; SIGTERM and SIGINT clear it. Runner error classifications are allowlisted across runner and worker; escalation detail is redacted before it reaches either the user reply or logs. Generic turns still execute with repository workspaces disabled; named repository requests, verified review feedback, and retained repository sessions refuse before execution. Retained generic attachment turns replace only an authenticated idle runner with durable history through an exact claim and generation fence. Repository attachment replacement remains deferred. One bounded idle route reclamation follows a proven ResourceQuota refusal and retries only after exact quota headroom is observed. Bounded quota recovery rotates four-candidate windows across complete inventories, preserving eval-first and expiry order within each selection cycle. Unreadable retained routes cannot monopolize every pass. Selection memory grants no deletion authority: locked route, runner-safety and ownership checks still apply. Transient disappearance reads retry within the original cleanup deadline, and retry requires confirmed claim and sandbox absence plus exact quota headroom. Approval resume also attempts idle reclamation before returning sandbox-capacity, provided the same quota evidence and deadline permit it. The effective runner timeout bounds the whole stream; unconfirmed timeout ownership ends terminally instead of retrying. The factory dispatcher acquires durable requests before starting a turn, waits on capacity, reconciles orphaned runs, observes cancellation, and rotates CI repair rounds without losing the WorkItem. A declared cron trigger is claimed once per slot in SQL and enqueued onto the same bounded run stream. Factory execution is capped by the agent execution deadline and an explicit turn budget. The platform ceiling is 43200 seconds. The default deadline stays 1800 seconds, the factory quickstart stays 10800 seconds, and the shipped worker delivery budget and runner ceiling stay 10800 seconds. A longer deadline needs those worker ceilings raised with it. The CI wait ceiling stays 10800 seconds. Before each covered factory execute or CI turn, including warm runner reuse and continuations, the worker requests fresh publication precheck context from the API and binds it to the ACI Event; if minting fails it stops before starting the turn. A streaming turn refreshes its live route and workspace lease every third of the route TTL. An unpublished factory execute turn gets one continuation, and a factory execution whose claimed pod is Unschedulable at the claim timeout defers as capacity instead of failing. Slack edits are cut to the 4,000 byte chat.update limit and receipts list at most ten actions. Interactive turns now park in a durable capacity wait when a sandbox cannot start. A fixed deadline, generation fence, wake reconciliation, and terminal notice prevent an unbounded or silently lost wait; the runner grants admission to the exact waiting turn epoch before input is sent. A failed runner turn produces a marked channel reply and a failed message result, with distinct causes for exhausted turns and unclassified failures. The worker carries the selected bot identity through reply delivery, mints a signed connector caller token for the agent at sandbox boot, and reports factory usage. The progress store now persists one fenced, bounded record per logical turn chain and an idempotent card and milestone outbox in Valkey. A scoped model command ingress and worker pumps apply chain state; rendering remains disabled and no adapter delivers that outbox. The maintenance sweep can quarantine pending records. A disconnected cluster message keeps its reserved internal relay adapter after the Slack binding resolves, so its reply returns to the CLI instead of real Slack. The installation chooses whether terminal replies include all, failed, or no action receipts. Turns that the worker cannot start because capacity is unavailable, an attachment cannot be fetched, or the agent has no pool receive a terminal reply and count as classified failures in turn telemetry, not completed work. Restricted turns run only after the exact runner advertises enforcement; they never steer a live session or obtain a connector approval grant. A dropped stream is classified sandbox-terminated only when pod_termination confirms the exact Kubernetes pod or a matching recent event, otherwise it remains a transport failure; Docker supplies no termination evidence. Redacted action results retain neither prior nor post state and cannot promise undo. A card whose approval resolved before registration is settled immediately after registration. Thread reset records released or no route in a one hour Valkey result before clearing the in progress marker. The API exposes whether a route existed; the CLI refuses a no route result and the UI reports that nothing was released. Failed teardown stays pending and emits a failed lifecycle outcome. A fresh request clears the prior result. For a factory execution the worker mints and injects the issue read route and execution scoped wir capability. Terminal budget notices distinguish exhausted output tokens from the USD limit. The worker sends channel memory references even when writes are off, and supplies write authority per turn only when enabled. Turn closure revokes that authority, with credential expiry as the backstop. Eligible human Slack turns receive leased progress capabilities; a live pump and maintenance drainer apply the same durable inbox. No progress deliverer is enabled. Scheduled ordinary admission now holds task-owned source authority and rechecks its liveness before claims, queue writes and failure effects; configured policy or history refuses that path. Startup validates readable source authority structures and owns the separate source-gate resources through shutdown. Claim-scoped boot state credentials carry one credential id and a bounded expiry; claim deletion reports release, retaining failed reports for retry. Per-turn memory writes expire at the delivery deadline without grace, and the owning live turn closes its attempt credentials. A text-only follow-up can hand a fresh sandbox the newest retained attachment set for the same thread and agent. The worker remints short-lived object references without extending retention; missing, near-expiry or malformed sets are omitted, and the best-effort lookup is bounded to five seconds. Every newly created claim receives a fresh boot credential id, preventing replacement or retry claims from reusing a released credential while preserving agent, scope and expiry. Ordinary and eval boots forward reviewer_model. Hook settlement records a terminal reason, and model-usage-limited is distinct from credit exhaustion. A refused factory publication snapshot ends with approval_create_failed and carries the existing redacted, clipped refusal detail into the issue Details line. A sanitized-base mismatch names the first 12 hexadecimal characters of both snapshot and prepared commits; repository mismatch wording and refusal behavior remain unchanged. Publication prose reports CI at pull request creation time and points to the issue status comment for subsequent results. Delivery and consumer liveness renewals tolerate transport errors only until the last confirmed send plus TTL minus one heartbeat interval. A refused renewal loses authority immediately. Side-effect markers retry before applying the frame, and terminal settlement remains fenced. Runs and evals share this ownership rule. An owner-lost factory request settles before a new attempt is admitted on the same WorkItem, bounded to three consecutive owner losses. Status cards show RETRYING only when a successor was admitted; other failed and expired requests show NEEDS HUMAN. Acquired but unstarted requests renew their short lease every twenty seconds. Only not_started deferrals count toward the default five-attempt start cap; capacity and thread-busy waits do not. Started factory CI and approval continuations wait for sandbox capacity within their existing delivery and execution deadlines without charging runner retries. Publication snapshots accumulate the response through EOF under the encoded and decoded size limits. Retryable read faults receive at most three reads within the remaining budget, without rerunning the model. Exhaustion names infrastructure read failure in the issue. Idempotent publication creation and execution settlement writes retry transient API faults within bounded authority; unresolved terminal reports retain heartbeat and sandbox ownership until settlement or the execution deadline. Charged publication reconciliation retries back off from fifteen seconds to five minutes. A clean drain now hands off a 300 second lease. Attest renews only existing same-revision authority, schema-migrate renews throughout readiness and migration, and the last pre-upgrade hold hook extends that authority to the configured roll hold. Independent mail persistence and pre-upgrade gVisor checks run before drain. Missing or foreign authority refuses the upgrade without recreating a marker. Failure after the hold can still pause claims for the remaining roll hold; extend-only renewal never shortens a longer lease. Workspace preparation failures preserve their existing workspace-error classification and carry a bounded redacted stage reason into terminal diagnostics. Managed publication Jobs receive configured GitHub stub CA text in their existing ConfigMap, with the CA digest included in the publication contract. Invalid configured CA input refuses worker startup. Approval and publication creation preserve the named relay ReplyHandle.identity independently of cluster-message reply delivery. Approval resolution restores the durable selector into the queued reply handle. Helm upgrades roll this component's consumers when a consumed chart-owned Secret value changes. Foreign Secret contents rotated in place require a separate rollout. A publication attempt with no valid recorded publication reports publication_unrecorded and preserves redacted refusal detail in the issue outcome. The kernel is a package with bounded shared stream transport. Separate explicitly provisioned protected worker composition requires current artifact and runtime evidence. The action executor claims a restricted sandbox and makes an exact connector call without a model. Factory execution and continuations use the persisted admitted agent and current authenticated binding context, while ambiguous ordinary chat still refuses. Retried terminal not_running responses release only the recorded sandbox claim; stale-owner responses retain their fence. Runtime orphan declaration needs a positive peer capability and sustained absence of its independent alive lease. Docker inputs use claim-owned named volumes populated through the Docker API. Read-only find commands no longer produce changed-file receipts. The runner binds its HTTP listener and answers healthz before declared verification preflight and SDK connection finish. Status ready remains false until initialization completes, and admitted turns wait for the shared initialization task. Credential, approval and bundle refusals still precede binding. Verification subprocess groups are killed and reaped on exit, including cancellation during spawn. Managed checkout handoff re-reads only a fully attested candidate whose sole unmet fact is ready=false, polling every 0.25 seconds within its existing deadline; any other mismatch refuses immediately. Parked capacity waits retry every five seconds, capped at the deadline, without repeating an already delivered notice when no grant was confirmed and the grant is known absent. A successful turn now stores its final answer in an answer-bearing completion record before channel delivery, and redelivery replays that stored answer rather than the model. Assistant text deltas are internal diagnostics; the terminal answer is the delivered text. Turn receipts default to off. When a runner response negotiated exact output, a verbatim final is delivered literally through reply wire 1.2 and a version-isolated outbox family; an unnegotiated verbatim final fails closed. The action executor can read connector Deployments itself when the connector reconciler is off, and refuses that setting when it cannot apply. Owned-workload launch mechanics are shared behind a closed authorizer seam, and separate commissioning worker, observation channel and managed CNI probe compositions exist outside the production worker. A rejected deterministic Job is not recovery authority until the same UID is terminal on two reads around a complete pod inventory and every declared regular, init and ephemeral container is terminated. Missing, replaced, unreadable or incomplete evidence retains the wait without charging an attempt. A timed-out pull-request open similarly waits for quiescence, then permits adoption only of an open matching pull request at the verified head; it never repeats the open request in that recovery path. This is recovery with surviving publication authority, not reconstruction after database loss. For a first publication, the writer fetches the API-authoritative base branch and, if its tip advanced, replays the approved patch onto that descendant tip. Conflict, empty replay, unrelated history and replay failure stop publication. The API verifies the revision marker and one parent, proves the approved base is an ancestor of that parent and the parent is an ancestor of the current base tip, with one is_ancestor request per relation. GitHub answers from the status of one three-dot compare. Equal shas count as ancestors, and a forge that cannot answer leaves the publication unproved. The immutable approval base stays unchanged; lineage settlement records the actual first parent under publication, lease and lineage fences. Later revisions still require the exact prior published head. Failed runner roots carry the last mapped ErrorEvent classification only for classified_failure, with unclassified for an unknown value; budget-exceeded may additionally carry an output ceiling from 1 to 1000000. Provider-error assistant text is excluded from generation output. After a dropped runner stream, the worker waits up to ten seconds for confirmed Kubernetes termination and exports only a bounded OOMKilled, Evicted, Deleted or Unknown reason and an observed 0 to 255 exit code. Event diagnosis preserves a runner exit code; raw termination detail is excluded from span attributes. Review checkouts fetch the recorded base commit as a separate depth-one object without changing the checked-out pull-request head. A prior publication Job using another tag or digest of the same image repository may be adopted only when its remaining expected resource shape matches; a different image repository or script still rejects adoption. A remembered boot credential stays valid while its claim is still being provisioned. Release retry runs only after the claim is marked retiring, so a claim that is not yet visible is not treated as already gone. Failed or interrupted claim creation retires the claim, and that retirement marks the credential for release. When the chart publishes the sandbox admission contract, the worker checks that envelope and live quota headroom before creating a claim and refuses with computed admission evidence. Docker refuses to start if that contract is set. A structural workspace stage timeout defers as workspace_timeout on the flat base backoff without charging a start or capacity attempt, and the waiting request keeps its deadline and bounded stage diagnostic. The worker supplies its retained prepared base to the authenticated /v1/snapshot request; the body must contain exactly one full base_sha. Capture includes the net committed, staged, unstaged and nonignored untracked change from that base, so local commits cannot move publication authority. HEAD must be that base or a locally verified descendant within 256 commits and 1 MiB of commit objects. Missing authority, unrelated or unreadable history, changed HEAD or workspace observations, unsafe paths, changed symlinks or gitlinks, and patches above 900000 raw bytes refuse capture before approval creation. The worker still validates the patch against its private sanitized base.

nodes.label: Approval plane
nodes.subtitle: Durable human gate
nodes.description: A gate terminates the turn as AWAITING_APPROVAL, persists a durable record and its validated originating trace context, suspends the sandbox, and later resumes through a new queued resolution turn that continues that trace when available. The runner's PreToolUse hook is the primary permission gate and can_use_tool is its backstop. Configuration-time checks refuse a declared-but-unbound approval route before deployment or route mutation, while request-time checks remain the fail-safe. Legacy or malformed carriers intentionally start a clean root. The resume reconciler's grace is derived from the delivery budget plus shutdown reserve. Resolution accepts only authenticated chat, Console, operator, or scoped adapter principals and checks every principal, including the requester, against the captured approver set. An adapter can see and resolve only approvals served by its binding set, and only through explicit user routes. When multiple releases share one Slack app, only the API owning the approval record may resolve it. One resolution target owns the sole interactive card. An optional pager target receives text only, with no ConfirmIntent, action value, or remembered card reference, so it cannot create a second approval card or authority path. Publication approval is fresh for each proposed revision, never resumes the model directly, and review feedback is not itself an approval. Known read-only tools avoid approval and receipt side effects. Durable authority is recorded before any card or notice delivery, including turns without an existing reply reference. Publication cards preserve the CLI reply adapter and a stable pending lifetime. The shipped SRE gates, including mcp__curie__publish_changes, carry sre-approvals; explicit user bindings allow operator resolution without Slack transport. A separately granted administrative recovery path can reject and audit a stranded approval without widening the ordinary membership decision. For covered factory turns, the runner resolves an empty publication proposal before any path records pending publication state: blank body, local head drift, no change, stale context, unavailable comparison, and metadata only proposals return nonhalting refusals, while a real file change still takes the mandatory approval gate. Admission remains the independent authority check. A permission approval persists the denied call's canonical argument object and binds the one use resume grant to that same tool and argument object. Concurrent delivery copies of one resume event are fenced by an event claim tied to the active delivery lease. Session approvals have a 24 hour deadline. A card resolves at the location where its request was asked, and the requester thread receives notices in order. A settled card records the decision while the durable approval row remains authoritative. Email membership and card authorization are implemented, while current AgentMail replies are refused before resolution because sender authentication is unverifiable. The displayed requester is recovered only from a validated resume chain and never participates in authorization. When a decision precedes card registration, successful registration immediately checks durable authority and settles the card. Failed resume enqueues observed by the current API process are retried on the next reconciler pass. The process record is capped at 10,000 approvals; restart loss and failures beyond that cap retain the grace backstop. A short locked transaction enqueues before marking resumed and retains still-owed locked rows for another pass. The durable approval and publication rows preserve named relay reply_identity separately from reply_adapter. Default identity and non-relay routes normalize to null, and approval resolution restores ReplyHandle.identity. Unknown bare operator gate names and CLI aliases raise ApprovalPolicyError at runner boot. Canonical built-ins and resolvable declared MCP names retain their gate rules. Accepted ADR 0220 plans a separate agent-wide approver team evaluated from an active IdP person and current projected membership on every channel with a resolver. Route lists may only narrow that team, and card location stays unchanged. Agents without an approver team retain their existing approval behavior, with Slack approver sets and exact email lists deciding membership. Remediation writes use a distinct remediation.administer principal for attribution and request scope. Binding or arming additionally requires the independent API-only remediation authority header; platform-key-derived principals alone cannot enable automatic remediation. Unbind and disarm retain their reducing authority. Approver team enforcement now runs for approvals and gated undo rulings: when the agent's access policy names an approver team, the resolver must be an active IdP person in that synced team, and route lists can only narrow it. A request_approval whose route grants a tool on a proxied hosted connector is refused in-turn, so the permission gate holds the call itself and the resume grant binds its exact arguments.

nodes.label: Eval plane
nodes.subtitle: Cases · graders · report
nodes.description: The same bundle-carried eval suite runs across skill, local, local-release, and cluster. Worker scores and records cases, then reports a rollup to the API. Provisioned eval runners retain configured hosted connector scope, agent-only signed caller identity when signing is configured, and tenant-scoped operator approval gates. Ambient memory and history references remain absent.

nodes.label: Sandbox
nodes.subtitle: One isolated session
nodes.description: An isolated runtime claimed per conversation. Kubernetes Agent Sandbox is production; Docker runs the same image locally. Accepted inbound files appear read only under /attachments on both substrates. Managed repository content appears at /workspace from a private signed one-object reference and digest; GitHub and object-store credentials never enter the runner. Kubernetes redeems references in dedicated credentialless init containers, while Docker redeems them in the substrate driver. A late workspace or accepted review replaces the route only at a fenced turn boundary, and review work starts from the exact verified pull request head in a newly claimed sandbox. Session identity can arrive over the ACI so a warm pool sandbox may be prebound before the turn. Chart render fails closed if the retired in path LiteLLM sidecar is reenabled (ADR-0037). Retained attachment replacement preserves the logical session and transcript while cold creating a candidate before detaching the old route. Capacity, binding, or fence failure preserves the old claim. Quota pressure can reclaim at most one safe idle route and does not add a background scheduler. Package registry egress is closed by default; an agent listed under agentSandbox.registryEgress gets its own NetworkPolicy and a labeled per agent sandbox pool that the worker routes its claims to. A claim whose pod the scheduler cannot place is reported as unschedulable so factory work can defer for capacity. Kubernetes refuses a connector secret claim before scheduling if the chart rendered no secret capable agent pool. Local Docker has no warm pool and carries those secrets directly into its runner claim. Transient Kubernetes reads are treated as no observation while a claim binds. Claim timeout captures a bounded redacted runner log tail before cleanup; Docker offers no Kubernetes log-tail evidence. Direct installs can infer gVisor off from a present RuntimeClass with a nonempty selector and no matching node in readable evidence, including eligible fake-model auto installs. Explicit auto refuses and require retains the preflight. Prepared apply, dry runs and unreadable node evidence authorize no scheduling reduction; selectors do not prove taints, cordons, capacity or runtime-handler availability. The gVisor preflight and security probe verify exact sentry uname -v equality with "#1 SMP Sun Jan 10 15:06:54 PST 2016"; a hostname or release string containing gvisor is insufficient. Quota recovery rotates four-candidate windows through complete inventories, preserving eval-first and expiry order per cycle so unreadable retained routes cannot monopolize passes. Selection grants no deletion authority: locked route, runner-safety and ownership checks remain. Transient disappearance reads retry within the original cleanup deadline; requester retry needs confirmed claim and sandbox absence plus exact quota headroom. The chart resolves standard and factory sandbox profiles.
