Factory-enabled sandbox egress selects factory unless an agent explicitly chooses another profile: 8Gi memory request and limit, CPU 50m request and 2 limit, ephemeral storage 10Gi request and 20Gi limit, workspace and home ceilings 15Gi each, and tmp 4Gi. Per-agent workspace overrides win over generic workspace values and profile defaults; explicit generic resource pairs use standard values for an unspecified side, and claim-time API resource overrides still win. Explicit zero requests survive, while zero volume ceilings refuse rendering. The default 8Gi memory quota permits one factory sandbox, and existing pods retain their original envelope. An explicit generic writablePathSizeLimit sets every writable path. Older computed generic values retained by --reuse-values keep the old envelope; cluster upgrade takes profile defaults while preserving explicit operator values. A remembered boot credential stays valid while its claim is still being provisioned. Release retry runs only after the claim is marked retiring, so a claim that is not yet visible is not treated as already gone. Failed or interrupted claim creation retires the claim, and that retirement marks the credential for release. Each resource profile defaults scratchVolume.type to emptyDir, and a missing key, including a release reused from a chart without that key, means emptyDir. Type ephemeral backs only the workspace volume and the writable volume whose path is the runner home, using a claim-scoped generic ephemeral volume whose storage request is the size the envelope already resolved. Other writable paths stay emptyDir with a positive sizeLimit. An emptyDir eviction names the stamped values key and mentions scratchVolume.type=ephemeral only when that volume is eligible.

nodes.label: Runner / ACI server
nodes.subtitle: Multi-turn session loop
nodes.description: Serves event, steer, interrupt, timeout, reset, and snapshot; translates harness events into the frozen NDJSON union; injects memory and history; and probes MCP capabilities conservatively. For hosted Bearer connectors, the runner expands the named secret into the in memory MCP header, removes that name from the process environment, and writes the full MCP configuration to a mode 0600 file instead of the Claude process argv. Missing or empty credentials still halt before a model call with a names only diagnosis. A failed capability probe is retried inside each later accepted turn; a persistent probe failure denies that connector's tools and reports the condition while still running the model. The disallowed tool list blocks named tools rather than the underlying credential backed capability. Permission enforcement layers a primary PreToolUse hook with a can_use_tool backstop, and runner local disallowed tool policy applies to both real and fake sessions. Bundle command hooks run from the mounted plugin root with CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT set; exit 2 denies, while exit 0 stdout can return a deny, ask, or stop decision. Telemetry records each observed provider wait and tool wait interval as root siblings with bounded phase, terminal, round, TTFT, and outcome attributes. Portable structured history preserves ordered messages and tool results, with optional native checkpoints for cache reuse. Appends reserve room for durable publication outcomes. On a capacity refusal the runner compacts through versioned compare-and-set, preserves publication markers and the newest turn, reloads on conflicts, and retries. Only a capacity refusal that survives bounded compaction replaces success or approval with history-persistence-error and CLASSIFIED_FAILURE; ordinary append failures retain the outcome but mark durability lost. Boot uses the same bounded compaction and reload path before accepting a turn. For a covered factory turn, one per turn publication decision is shared by the stream observer, PreToolUse hook, and can_use_tool, keyed by the exact tool call identity. An empty working tree snapshot is compared through the API precheck endpoint, accepted only at the boot delivered trusted origin, without redirects, within ten seconds and at most five times per turn; refusals are nonhalting and record no pending approval. The runner reads the transcript value cap the state API advertises and can replace older completed tool exchanges within one long turn with a deterministic marker. Every SDK session disables commit and pull request attribution text. The turn start log is emitted inside agent.run so even a successful turn without tools has a runner log with the turn trace context. Hosted Kubernetes connector requests carry a worker signed cct to the mandatory caller proxy, with a separate one use ccg for an approval gated connector tool. The runner reports measured usage for factory accounting and keeps a checkpoint only under the matching system prompt. ACI 0.5.9 adds optional per turn read only enforcement. Tools outside the declared read only set, including approval requiring tools, are denied before approval or registered callback work; restricted steers and slash commands refuse. A prior unrestricted SDK session cannot accept a restricted prompt, and the first unrestricted prompt after a restricted turn replaces that SDK session. Portable history preserves proven assistant message grouping and refuses ambiguous overlapping tool calls; replay may reduce an independently isolatable ambiguous old turn to its visible text. Each boot's attachment notice is added to its first actual prompt and persisted with that message, preserving reattachment under an unchanged filename. Text block paragraph separators are placed after whole text redaction so they cannot split a held secret, and final redaction preserves the same boundaries. The current ACI version is 0.5.21. Per turn memory write authority is carried on the Event, while boot memory credentials remain read only. The platform get_issue tool uses the boot supplied issue read route and execution scoped capability. Credential variables are removed from Bash and hook environments before shell startup. SDK error subtypes produce classified terminal failures even when is_error is false, and usage accounting subtracts prior cumulative SDK totals. Agent and channel facts load with recorded authors even when writes are off. Enabled memory tools can remember, update and forget facts using the turn credential, with a bounded fact count. The harness exposes only the bundle skill list. Its platform progress tool uses a scoped API capability rather than the ACI event stream. Serving requires a nonblank bearer token unless the explicit development tokenless flag is set. Channel-bound turns hide SendMessage and PushNotification. A blocked declared verification check selects an offline PreflightBlockedSession before model startup and reports zero implementer usage. Reviewer credit exhaustion is terminal for the whole turn, and measured factory usage separates implementer and reviewer totals. ACI 0.5.15 adds optional BootEnv.reviewer_model, forwarded as CURIE_REVIEWER_MODEL. Local and cluster overrides can pin or clear it. Ordinary and eval boots forward the per-agent value; omission preserves the override and explicit null clears it. Without an override the runner resolves the SDK Opus alias from the effective credential. Factory quickstart selects a provider-appropriate implementer default for Anthropic or OpenRouter credentials while preserving an explicit model. Provider subscription usage refusals have a distinct terminal model-usage-limited classification, take precedence over credit refusals and interrupt before SDK retries or parent continuation. An OpenRouter key spend-limit 403 and an OpenRouter workspace budget 403 both remain credit exhaustion. Budget accounting counts a repeated assistant response id once per turn. Factory usage pairs base model observations with a unique context-window-suffixed aggregate key and avoids counting already reported reviewer usage twice; API pricing strips the trailing context suffix before matching rates. Turns ending without a ResultMessage report the observed token counts once; draining a later abandoned result advances the usage baseline without reporting those tokens again. A classified terminal failure that stores no transcript terminal can authorize durable replacement when no earlier history loss remains. Claude SDK initialization records start, outcome, elapsed time and SDK version. A failure retains at most 8192 bytes of redacted stderr; cancellation discards the tail. Callback forwarding continues and exception, retry and timeout behavior are unchanged. Bare operator approval gates must name recognized canonical Claude Code built-ins. Unknown names and CLI aliases refuse runner boot with ApprovalPolicyError. MCP gates must resolve to declared live names; invalid names cannot silently arm a no-op gate. Grant-bound Slack history and canvas tools ship. The attachment manifest separates current and retained files. Executor mode loads no harness and exposes a runner-private execute route for one canonical connector action. The runner binds its HTTP listener and answers healthz before declared verification preflight and SDK connection finish. Status ready remains false until initialization completes, and admitted turns wait for the shared initialization task. Credential, approval and bundle refusals still precede binding. Verification subprocess groups are killed and reaped on exit, including cancellation during spawn. Managed checkout handoff re-reads only a fully attested candidate whose sole unmet fact is ready=false, polling every 0.25 seconds within its existing deadline; any other mismatch refuses immediately. A bundle may declare a finalAnswer validation tool in its curie.bundle.json sidecar. The runner then correlates the current-turn validation call and result by call ID and draft digest, suppresses provisional text, and publishes only the validated text as Final.text_mode verbatim, or a final-answer-validation classified failure. HTTP callers must advertise X-Curie-Final-Answer before a constrained runner accepts an event. The empty-result fallback keeps only text after the last top-level tool request. A ResultMessage does not close a turn while a tracked non-ambient SDK background task remains live. The runner continues receive_turn on the same session while accounting usage, retaining existing timeout and budget termination. An exact first-line task-notification prompt preserves the factory review-gate state. A fresh prompt captures its checkout fingerprint in at most two attempts sharing seven seconds; failure stops before plan-review spending. Failed runner roots carry the last mapped ErrorEvent classification only for classified_failure, with unclassified for an unknown value; budget-exceeded may additionally carry an output ceiling from 1 to 1000000. Provider-error assistant text is excluded from generation output. After a dropped runner stream, the worker waits up to ten seconds for confirmed Kubernetes termination and exports only a bounded OOMKilled, Evicted, Deleted or Unknown reason and an observed 0 to 255 exit code. Event diagnosis preserves a runner exit code; raw termination detail is excluded from span attributes. A workspace snapshot is refused when HEAD or the changed path set moves during capture. The worker supplies its retained prepared base to the authenticated /v1/snapshot request; the body must contain exactly one full base_sha. Capture includes the net committed, staged, unstaged and nonignored untracked change from that base, so local commits cannot move publication authority. HEAD must be that base or a locally verified descendant within 256 commits and 1 MiB of commit objects. Missing authority, unrelated or unreadable history, changed HEAD or workspace observations, unsafe paths, changed symlinks or gitlinks, and patches above 900000 raw bytes refuse capture before approval creation. The worker still validates the patch against its private sanitized base. Review and capture share build_candidate. It reads final file contents, modes and index flags rather than trusting Git stat caches or a working-tree diff. Ordinary changed tracked files use Git built-in clean conversions; paths Git does not read use raw disk bytes. A missing skip-worktree entry still equal to the prepared base is retained, preserving preparation-removed links. Conversion refuses custom filter attributes and ambiguous Git configuration paths without running clean or process filter programs. Scratch index and object writes leave the real index, refs, HEAD and object store unchanged. The shell launcher self-check allows one 30 second cold start without a retry.

nodes.label: Claude harness
nodes.subtitle: Declared package today
nodes.description: The only production harness contribution. ModelSession exists, but raw SDK messages and the Claude Code plugin format still cross the conceptual boundary. Draft ADR-0140 would stop the speculative multi-harness program until a real second engine exists; while Draft, it authorizes no change to the accepted harness contracts. The runner tracks SDK background-task lifecycle on the same ModelSession; an intermediate result while a task is live does not finalize the factory turn.

nodes.label: Model endpoint
nodes.subtitle: Provider-selected inference
nodes.description: Anthropic is the default; OpenRouter, Zhipu, Moonshot, DeepSeek, and opt-in Ollama routes are also built. Cluster Ollama pulls now require an explicit durable-storage policy or a declaration that weights are pre-provisioned; ephemeral implicit downloads are refused before mutation. Native OpenAI wire format remains absent. ACI 0.5.15 adds optional BootEnv.reviewer_model, forwarded as CURIE_REVIEWER_MODEL. Local and cluster overrides can pin or clear it. Ordinary and eval boots forward the per-agent value; omission preserves the override and explicit null clears it. Without an override the runner resolves the SDK Opus alias from the effective credential. Factory quickstart selects a provider-appropriate implementer default for Anthropic or OpenRouter credentials while preserving an explicit model.

nodes.label: MCP connector hosts
nodes.subtitle: Collapsed MCP implementations
nodes.description: Bundle declared hosted, source built, remote, and unhosted fallback MCP implementations remain collapsed behind this role. Cluster deploy waits for each hosted Deployment's current revision to become ready or fails with a bounded redacted diagnosis. Skill and local startup use a separate Docker host outside the connector port and share one configurable bounded readiness deadline. The platform separately warns when a hosted workload has no mounted MCP entry. Runner boot performs the actual MCP capability and authentication probe, then later turns may retry a transient probe failure without redialing missing credentials. Renderer and CLI now share a frozen derived Bearer selection rule. Draft ADR-0158 documents a bundle-built HTTP MCP server that owns its provider credential, based on retained historical spike evidence, but it authorizes no new product surface. Hosted connector Deployments now expose TCP readiness on their MCP port. Several upstream SecretRef credentials are accepted without inventing a client Bearer header; skill and local tiers stage an explicitly derived Bearer credential when one is declared. Every hosted Kubernetes connector requires a caller proxy and public key; the API refuses a missing pair with 422. The proxy verifies a signed cct with agent and exp claims and optional paired run and work item claims, then enforces the declared admits policy. Approval gated tool calls additionally require a separate signed ccg matching agent, connector, tool, canonical arguments, expiry, and a jti spent once through Valkey. Skill and local startup require a caller public key and generate an ephemeral pair, but their Docker host runs the original connector image directly and enforces neither caller tokens nor connector grants. Upgrade refuses an absent or partial caller credential pair before mutation rather than generating one; cluster up can generate a missing pair. The caller proxy verifies optional paired run and work item claims and derives their forwarded headers from the signed caller token. The test environment connector requires this pair before creating a namespace. Hosted declarations can supply validated non-secret config. An explicit nonblank no_client_auth reason suppresses inferred client Bearer authentication for multi-secret upstream servers without weakening the caller proxy or approval grant checks. A hosted connector may also declare a loopback proxy_upstream_host, which only the caller proxy presents upstream on admitted requests, a readiness_path for the server container probe, and validated server-container resources merged over defaults. The caller proxy logs a fixed grant refusal sub-reason without claim values. Hosted connector objects are applied with one server-side apply.

nodes.label: MCP OAuth gateway
nodes.subtitle: Per-person delegated access
nodes.description: The accepted vision boundary for delegated MCP authorization. The control plane owns OAuth discovery, PKCE, encrypted tokens, refresh, revocation, and grants; the gateway applies the active run principal's grant without exposing raw OAuth tokens to the runner.

nodes.label: Agent Proxy
nodes.subtitle: Credentials + egress boundary
nodes.description: Accepted architecture moves provider credentials and enforceable egress policy out of the sandbox. The direction is decided, but substrate, TLS termination, credential injection, and implementation remain follow-up work.

nodes.label: OTel collector
nodes.subtitle: Telemetry write port
nodes.description: Receives OTLP from Curie services and the runner and exports to Langfuse over HTTP. Ingress, durable approval resolution, expiry, and reconciliation preserve the originating W3C trace context when valid; missing or malformed legacy carriers start clean roots. Request path operation spans may carry curie.channel.event_id from a task local scope, while metrics reject that unbounded identifier and maintenance work outside the request scope remains unstamped. The runner emits truthful sibling provider and tool phase intervals with a closed versioned attribute set; the collector boundary remains mostly vendor neutral. Chart CI discovers first party workloads from rendered images and rejects a new workload without the shared OTLP environment. Discord independently bootstraps the same telemetry package outside the chart. Provider teardown shares one wall clock deadline, and supervised worker restarts have bounded restart and give up outcomes. For chart managed sandboxes with NetworkPolicy enabled, a configured external collector endpoint requires declared runner egress CIDRs; chart rendering refuses an undeclared route. Disabling telemetry requires no collector egress rule. Generation spans now carry redacted, clipped langfuse.observation input and output: input is a prompt length placeholder or the names of tool results, and tool arguments and results are never recorded. A turn scope usage fallback stamps the result total when no generation received per message usage. The collector runs at the platform priority class. Metrics export selects cumulative temporality by default for Prometheus retention; an explicit preference can select delta for supported instruments. The example stale accepted-turn alert aggregates to one alert per installation rather than one per turn. Helm upgrades roll this component's consumers when a consumed chart-owned Secret value changes. Foreign Secret contents rotated in place require a separate rollout. The API disables FastAPI automatic telemetry setup, leaving export and trace parentage to the shared bootstrap. The module entrypoint preserves shared handlers and applies the same redaction and telemetry configuration to Uvicorn access and error logs. Failed runner roots carry the last mapped ErrorEvent classification only for classified_failure, with unclassified for an unknown value; budget-exceeded may additionally carry an output ceiling from 1 to 1000000. Provider-error assistant text is excluded from generation output. After a dropped runner stream, the worker waits up to ten seconds for confirmed Kubernetes termination and exports only a bounded OOMKilled, Evicted, Deleted or Unknown reason and an observed 0 to 255 exit code. Event diagnosis preserves a runner exit code; raw termination detail is excluded from span attributes. Socket Mode counts frames per configured identity with hello, disconnect, events_api, interactive, slash_commands and other types, and forwards SDK session lifecycle logs through the service logger. Slack identity labels admit at most 16 valid slugs per process before folding into other. Mentions in explicitly configured delivery-canary channels are counted and dropped after envelope validation, before relevance, principal lookup, approval handling, admission or dedupe: no API read, placeholder or queued turn is created. Frame counts expose received traffic; a delivery-canary count proves only that the configured mention reached that identity, separately from process heartbeat and connected-identity counts.

nodes.label: Langfuse
nodes.subtitle: Traces · metrics · eval scores
nodes.description: The current trace and eval store. The shipping Helm surface pins the reviewed Langfuse web and worker migration set together with ClickHouse 25.12.11.4, avoiding an upstream-republished minor alias; its AVX preflight fails the default installation on AVX-less nodes rather than allowing a migration-incompatible store. Compose retains its separate SSE4.2-safe ClickHouse pin for local evidence. The API reconstructs trees and metrics through a vendor-specific read adapter. Operators can disable the in-chart deployment and point every consumer at an explicit external Langfuse host without rendering a nonexistent in-cluster Service. External Langfuse and ClickHouse endpoints use validated HTTP or HTTPS scheme settings shared by their chart consumers. Observation trees expose toolName from the recorded tool span attribute so a consumer can identify the concrete tool executed. Langfuse web and worker now run at the platform priority class so sandboxes cannot preempt the trace store. Helm upgrades roll this component's consumers when a consumed chart-owned Secret value changes. Foreign Secret contents rotated in place require a separate rollout.

nodes.label: Postgres
nodes.subtitle: Control-plane state
nodes.description: Stores agents, versions, deployments, channel bindings, approvals, memory, WorkItems, ExecutionRequests, hook runs, factory status and outcome state, and per thread transcripts. Migrations 0040 through 0056 add scoped publication and review authority, operator source bindings, factory admission and dispatch, cron slots, publication policy, tenant groundwork, isolated transcripts, cancellation, execution deadlines, and status comments. Database constraints and compare and set versions fence competing publication, review, and factory work. Migration 0058 widens the factory terminal notice label check to accept the curie-factory names while retaining the legacy names, so a stored legacy label drives the next GitHub relabel. Migrations 0059 through 0061 record observed publication metadata, reconcile and remove legacy transcript state rows, and store canonical arguments for approved permission calls. After 0060 the transcript table is the sole runtime transcript store. Migrations 0062 through 0070 add durable review notices, factory revision queues, runner resources, deferred schedule claims and controls, model usage, caller allowlists, and identity scoped channel routes. Migrations 0075 and 0076 add durable source policies and immutable source-operation attempts. Candidate application serving metadata and ordered ancestry are owned by packages/protected-hooks, with checked API and chart mirrors. The v0.12.5 candidate serving head is 0106 and minimum is 0076; historical released windows remain separately recorded. Migrations 0079, 0080 and 0081 add hook reasons, hook source separation and the nullable reviewer model override. Migrations 0091 through 0093 add the owner-loss successor marker, start-deferral count and versioned factory status-sync lease. The v0.12.3 window is 0076 through 0093. Migration 0106 follows 0093 and adds nullable reply_identity columns to approvals and publications. The historical v0.12.4 released window remains 0076 through 0093. Helm upgrades roll this component's consumers when a consumed chart-owned Secret value changes. Foreign Secret contents rotated in place require a separate rollout. The v0.13.1 serving schema minimum and head are both 0108, unchanged from v0.13.0. The contract timing gate rejects new contract or irreversible migrations while the prior stable application still names a removed object. Migration 0123 stores a redacted workspace preparation stage and reason, capped at 2000 characters, as last_start_failure_detail. Capacity deferrals and worker replacement preserve it; a successful-start compare-and-set clears it. Waiting, exhausted-start and capacity-expiry outcomes retain the previous start diagnosis instead of replacing it with a generic capacity reason. The v0.14.1 application window requires schema minimum and head 0123. The v0.14.3 and v0.14.4 application windows and candidate serving metadata all declare schema minimum and head 0140. The v0.14.2 application window registers the same schema minimum and head 0123. Migration 0140 widens the agent and execution-request deadline checks from 10800 seconds to 43200 seconds and refuses downgrade while any row remains above 10800 seconds. v0.14.4 registers the existing 0140 through 0140 schema window without a new migration.

nodes.label: RustFS / S3
nodes.subtitle: Immutable bundles
nodes.description: Stores immutable agent bundles, eval inputs, managed workspaces, and inbound attachment bytes over an S3 compatible service. The API ObjectStore, worker BundleReader, and worker WorkspaceObjectPort are three distinct adapter surfaces. Attachment materialization additionally requires streaming operations and presigned reads. With a bring your own store and egress rail enabled, runner bundle fetch is fail closed until explicit store CIDRs and ports are supplied; the key free path also requires separate STS egress and uses projected service account identity rather than node metadata. The chart supplies rustfs.region as S3_REGION to both API and worker, reserving that environment name against extraEnv overrides. Helm upgrades roll this component's consumers when a consumed chart-owned Secret value changes. Foreign Secret contents rotated in place require a separate rollout. Persistent in-chart RustFS runs a storage-guard init container before startup. Below 10% free inodes or bytes, it removes expired Langfuse event objects only within the configured events prefix; any fresh constituent file protects its object. Retention zero disables deletion. The guard runs on pod creation, not a RustFS container-only restart. Fresh claims default to 10Gi; upgrades preserve the live StatefulSet data claim-template size through lookup. Offline renders must pin that existing template size.

nodes.label: Kubernetes
nodes.subtitle: Production substrate
nodes.description: Baseline production substrate: platform services, Agent Sandbox CRDs, security rails, connector workloads, and observability dependencies. A canonical external values profile disables the four chart owned backing stores and points consumers at operator supplied endpoints and Secrets. Helm upgrades preserve external credential references and heal missing or blank legacy chart managed Secret keys while retaining nonblank persisted values. Explicit adoption records a separate label pair and is retained on teardown. Runner API and OTLP egress rails key from the effective endpoint, including extra environment overrides, and fail closed without narrow peers. Connector and general runner egress entries require concrete ports and refuse metadata covering ranges or ineffective exceptions. Mail's external collector path has the same explicit peer requirement. In fake mode the worker and runner receive no live model credential, and an inference weights PVC with the keep annotation survives removal of the local model workload. Chart rendering rejects duplicate reserved environment variables; upgrade drains and digest pinned prewarm bundle fetch images are tied to the candidate generation, and BYO Postgres security probes omit an in chart endpoint they cannot reach. The platform PriorityClass now also covers Langfuse, the OTel collector, the UI, inference, and the mail adapter, while runner prewarm stays unclassed. Per agent registry egress policies pass the same floor as connector egress, and the worker Role gains namespaced get on pods for unschedulable diagnosis. The controller preflight fails on a current cluster-scope NetworkPolicy list/watch refusal or restart-count growth during observation. Namespaced refusals and previous-container failures remain diagnostic. A completed rollout with a stable Ready leader and advancing Lease renewal can pass. After a restart, the startup-log or successful-reconcile path additionally requires that exact current Ready pod to hold and visibly renew the Lease. Readable empty RuntimeClass node-selector results can infer gVisor off on direct installs, including eligible fake-model auto installs. Explicit auto refuses; require retains the preflight. Unreadable evidence preserves isolation, fake-model lookup failure preserves the original plan, and prepared apply and dry runs do no scheduling inference. This checks selector membership only, excluding taints, cordons, capacity and runtime-handler availability. The gVisor preflight and security probe verify exact sentry uname -v equality with "#1 SMP Sun Jan 10 15:06:54 PST 2016"; a hostname or release string containing gvisor is insufficient. The chart resolves managed Secret plaintext once per render and hashes each pod's consumed chart-owned keys into checksum/secret, including rendered extraEnv references. Changing a consumed value rolls its consumers; unrelated keys leave checksums unchanged. The first upgrade adds the annotation and rolls existing consumers once. Foreign Secret contents, Jobs and SandboxTemplates are excluded. A store restart does not rotate its persisted database password. Dev installation identity is deterministic for the namespace and release pair; sealed fresh installs remain unique. Persistent in-chart RustFS runs an init storage guard on pod creation. Below 10% free inodes or bytes it deletes expired objects only under the configured Langfuse events prefix, preserving any object with a fresh constituent file; retention zero disables deletion. Container-only restarts do not run it. Fresh claims default to 10Gi; upgrades retain the live data claim-template size by lookup, which offline renders must pin. Convergence excludes non-deleting Succeeded and Failed pods from replica counting and Node-image discovery. Active surplus and terminating pods still block convergence. Status keeps retained terminal pods visible without counting them as active replicas. The CLI deletes none of them. Chart rendering accepts an empty GitHub App ID or a positive integral value of 1 to 18 decimal digits, preserving string digits without lossy numeric coercion and refusing malformed values. Protected commissioning building blocks run against Kubernetes: a provisioner that owns creation and signing, a control process that reobserves facts per call over a signed observation channel, and a local Cilium behavioral network producer for disposable installations. A managed CNI probe kit exists for ADR 0238. None of these is wired into a shipped install path yet. The chart resolves standard and factory sandbox profiles. Factory-enabled sandbox egress selects factory unless an agent explicitly chooses another profile: 8Gi memory request and limit, CPU 50m request and 2 limit, ephemeral storage 10Gi request and 20Gi limit, workspace and home ceilings 15Gi each, and tmp 4Gi. Per-agent workspace overrides win over generic workspace values and profile defaults; explicit generic resource pairs use standard values for an unspecified side, and claim-time API resource overrides still win. Explicit zero requests survive, while zero volume ceilings refuse rendering. The default 8Gi memory quota permits one factory sandbox, and existing pods retain their original envelope. An explicit generic writablePathSizeLimit sets every writable path. Older computed generic values retained by --reuse-values keep the old envelope; cluster upgrade takes profile defaults while preserving explicit operator values. With factory.enabled, the API Deployment and schema-migrate Job default to a shared 2Gi memory limit; other installs default to 512Mi. Explicit api.resources.limits.memory wins, including retained 512Mi under --reuse-values. Memory requests remain 256Mi and CPU remains 100m request and 1 limit. The 2Gi choice is headroom rather than a demonstrated memory requirement. The worker receives CURIE_SANDBOX_ADMISSION when the agent sandbox and the resource quota are both enabled. A sandbox profile may select emptyDir or ephemeral scratch for workspace and home only.

nodes.label: Docker
nodes.subtitle: Local parity substrate
nodes.description: Runs the same worker and runner image behind SandboxClient. Validated bundles, managed workspaces and attachments cross the Docker API into claim-owned named volumes; no shared host filesystem is needed. Creation attempts own their seed helpers and volumes, and teardown removes only matching owned inputs. Connector secrets still enter the runner environment directly rather than through Kubernetes pool Secrets.

nodes.label: Dark Factory
nodes.subtitle: Operating pattern
nodes.description: A shipped single agent bundle and durable platform loop for one labelled tracker issue and one pull request. Signed issue intake admits a WorkItem, SQL owns waiting and execution identity, the worker claims an isolated sandbox, and an explicitly configured automatic publication policy can open or revise the same pull request. Status comments, cancellation, worker loss recovery, runs whose deadline ceiling is twelve hours, CI wait and repair rounds, and outcome reads are part of this operating pattern. The platform records state and evidence; the bundle owns correctness judgments. Factory state labels use the curie-factory prefix, and a label whose webhook was lost is admitted by reconciliation. The CI wait defaults to 3600 seconds as an operator setting under the execution deadline, the platform reports the wait_ci phase, repair prompts include bounded Actions job log tails, and a configured card URL replaces the checklist. An unpublished execute turn gets one continuation and zero work ends as early_stop; SDK USD budget stops map to the budget failure, and unschedulable sandboxes defer for capacity. Covered turns carry a scoped publication precheck so an empty publication request is refused inside the turn. Publication can revise pull request title or body without a new source commit when the bound identity and CI evidence remain current. Human review events arriving before the pull request identity is recorded are held for bounded admission replay. Verified review mentions received during an active run remain durable queued requests and are admitted after that run. Factory runs now report measured usage and can use a bundle layered runner image. An accepted test policy permits an isolated end to end namespace on a separate test cluster. The bundle reads its issue and comments through mcp__curie__get_issue without a GitHub credential in the sandbox. One foreground advisory plan review and at most five completed diff reviews are enforced, canonical verification observations gate publication, and one Actions rerun on the exact current head precedes bounded repair. Releases publish the first party factory runner layer, and rendering records digest locks for both that layer and its platform runner base. Polling is the default intake and uses durable cursors under a replica lock. Each admitted ticket retains its selected base branch through execution and publication. The first test environment connector provides owned namespace creation and destruction with quotas, expiry and network restrictions; image building, workload deployment, execution and reaping are established by the later connector slices. Repository edits require the loaded workflow and an approved plan. Declared unavailable verification without explicit CI delegation stops the run before model execution. Delegated check names must be observed and pass before CI settlement; unrelated passing checks cannot substitute. Reviewer credit refusal ends the turn. Accounting separates implementer and reviewer measurements and distinguishes zero usage from missing reports. Provider subscription usage refusals have a distinct terminal model-usage-limited classification, take precedence over credit refusals and interrupt before SDK retries or parent continuation. An OpenRouter key spend-limit 403 and an OpenRouter workspace budget 403 both remain credit exhaustion. Budget accounting counts a repeated assistant response id once per turn. Factory usage pairs base model observations with a unique context-window-suffixed aggregate key and avoids counting already reported reviewer usage twice; API pricing strips the trailing context suffix before matching rates. When head checks fail, factory CI reads the current base branch head within the remaining observation budget. Matching failing check names or status contexts are reported as pre-existing and excluded from repair, but required Python or delegated checks failing on that base remain unverified. An unreadable base makes every head failure count as caused. A refused factory publication snapshot ends with approval_create_failed and carries the existing redacted, clipped refusal detail into the issue Details line. A sanitized-base mismatch names the first 12 hexadecimal characters of both snapshot and prepared commits; repository mismatch wording and refusal behavior remain unchanged. Publication prose reports CI at pull request creation time and points to the issue status comment for subsequent results. An owner-lost factory request settles before a new attempt is admitted on the same WorkItem, bounded to three consecutive owner losses. Status cards show RETRYING only when a successor was admitted; other failed and expired requests show NEEDS HUMAN. Acquired but unstarted requests renew their short lease every twenty seconds. Only not_started deferrals count toward the default five-attempt start cap; capacity and thread-busy waits do not. Started factory CI and approval continuations wait for sandbox capacity within their existing delivery and execution deadlines without charging runner retries. Factory status synchronization owns a versioned SQL lease, releases database sessions before GitHub I/O, and runs separately from dispatch reconciliation. Late matching runtime heartbeats may renew before the execution deadline, with one heartbeat-TTL grace before owner-loss cancellation. Verification replay preserves the first observation for an unchanged command. CI reports unavailable required check names and merge_conflict explicitly instead of waiting for checks GitHub will not start. Publication snapshots accumulate the response through EOF under the encoded and decoded size limits. Retryable read faults receive at most three reads within the remaining budget, without rerunning the model. Exhaustion names infrastructure read failure in the issue. Idempotent publication creation and execution settlement writes retry transient API faults within bounded authority; unresolved terminal reports retain heartbeat and sandbox ownership until settlement or the execution deadline. Charged publication reconciliation retries back off from fifteen seconds to five minutes. Default factory reviewer selections were updated; per-agent overrides remain explicit. Adoption of an orphaned factory PR under accepted ADR 0208 remains planned. ADR 0209 post-drain lease handoff and the final hold hook are implemented. The scoped issue read returns the current execution deadline and total granted seconds. The factory workflow paces its foreground reviews, implementation and verification against that reported grant, rather than assuming a three hour grant. The reported grant can be as long as 43200 seconds. Quickstart now defaults to 10800 seconds, while explicit shorter grants remain authoritative. Metadata-only repair uses configured repository policy first, falling back only when absent to that round's Valkey-recorded failing check names and status contexts. Fresh reruns must settle those guards: none yields checks_not_rerun, partial reruns retain missing failures at deadline, and invalid records yield metadata_ci_not_configured. A publication attempt with no valid recorded publication reports publication_unrecorded and preserves redacted refusal detail in the issue outcome. The factory refuses any root .github path change, including case variants, even when requested by the ticket. Edit hooks stop such changes, the diff-review hook checks changed and untracked paths, and the workflow refuses tickets requiring them before partial implementation. Diff review requires a buildable canonical candidate and checks every changed path for the protected root .github directory, including symlink and dotdot traversal; unreadable candidate construction refuses review. Factory verification resolves CURIE_BIN and records its version before external actions. Live runs use per-run release and PriorityClass ownership and inspect the shared controller before mutation. Scripted mode drives the installed platform through a GitHub stub and recorded model responses, requiring matching durable preflight and publication observations and verified cleanup. Replay establishes recorded boundary behavior, not live provider or model acceptance. Draft ADR 0211 proposes bounded sandbox-loss successors; the current kernel still escalates sandbox loss after side effects. The factory now uses separate Tracker and CodeHost ports. GitHub with GitHub, Jira Cloud with GitHub, and GitLab with GitLab have passed live acceptance on a dedicated test cluster; GitLab supports gitlab.com and self-managed servers. Jira Cloud quickstart supports Bitbucket Cloud and Data Center through verified tracker and code-host reads. One factory agent can serve multiple operator-bound repositories and per-surface trigger labels. Repository runner images are built from a pinned tool catalog, probed and advertised through their immutable manifest. ADR 0217 places a Docker-enabled run's daemon outside the sandbox; the chart renders that boundary and the worker parses its configuration, but per-run daemon creation and certificate issuance are not implemented yet. The test connector can build images daemonlessly, deploy by digest, run and inspect workloads, and reap only owned expired namespaces. Bitbucket Cloud refuses an unverified open matching publication as unconfirmed and asks the operator to confirm; this grants no ownership or continuation authority. Tracker intake names credential repair actions and reports missing or inaccessible repositories. A pull request closed without merging ends CI wait as pr_closed before check evaluation. An unpublished revision with a recorded pull request ends as revision_unchanged. Handoff messages retain up to 4000 characters and render as quoted text with HTML, images and mentions neutralized. Budget stops omit raw verification preflight notes, and Jira links the first succeeded publication. The published factory runner installs checksum-pinned cargo-nextest 0.9.146. Each Docker repository runner pool entry now carries a strict daemon object with namespace, pinned image, TLS port, selector labels and Pod settings, and the chart grants the worker create and get on pods/portforward because ADR 0217 now names an API port-forward with the claim certificate as the ping transport. Cluster upgrade rebuilds repository runners, and a stale_base reply names the repository runner rebuild command. Accepted ADR 0222 plans to move factory policy into a versioned bundle policy artifact. Factory CI now defaults to 3600 seconds from push, still capped by the execution deadline and preserving explicit operator values. GitHub reads base-branch ruleset and branch-protection required-check names. A required name absent from the published head stays pending until the deadline, then ends ci_unverified and names the missing trigger without applying it. Transient rule-read failures can time out; permanent unreadability refuses immediately. Other code hosts declare required-check reads unsupported rather than simulating them. The chart resolves standard and factory sandbox profiles. Factory-enabled sandbox egress selects factory unless an agent explicitly chooses another profile: 8Gi memory request and limit, CPU 50m request and 2 limit, ephemeral storage 10Gi request and 20Gi limit, workspace and home ceilings 15Gi each, and tmp 4Gi. Per-agent workspace overrides win over generic workspace values and profile defaults; explicit generic resource pairs use standard values for an unspecified side, and claim-time API resource overrides still win. Explicit zero requests survive, while zero volume ceilings refuse rendering. The default 8Gi memory quota permits one factory sandbox, and existing pods retain their original envelope. An explicit generic writablePathSizeLimit sets every writable path. Older computed generic values retained by --reuse-values keep the old envelope; cluster upgrade takes profile defaults while preserving explicit operator values. Factory quickstart sets max_output_tokens_per_run to 250000 through the ordinary per-agent budget command for supported forge paths and adding an agent to an existing install. A positive --output-tokens overrides it. Generic platform defaults remain 100000; the factory allowance is per run. Human and JSON ready receipts report the selected allowance, with factory-quickstart result schema v1.3. A ResultMessage does not close a turn while a tracked non-ambient SDK background task remains live. The runner continues receive_turn on the same session while accounting usage, retaining existing timeout and budget termination. An exact first-line task-notification prompt preserves the factory review-gate state. A fresh prompt captures its checkout fingerprint in at most two attempts sharing seven seconds; failure stops before plan-review spending. Factory status quotes now neutralize bracket links, references, images and scheme URLs as well as HTML and mentions. Only model-service causes label text Provider message; infrastructure and CI causes use Details. A failed publication warns that its branch or pull request may already exist. A no-change forge loop still persists the terminal notice. Publish stays allowed only while the base and canonical candidate tree fingerprint matches the approving diff review. A changed or unreadable checkout clears that verdict and requires a fresh diff review. A snapshot that sees the tree change during capture is refused. Review and capture share build_candidate. It reads final file contents, modes and index flags rather than trusting Git stat caches or a working-tree diff. Ordinary changed tracked files use Git built-in clean conversions; paths Git does not read use raw disk bytes. A missing skip-worktree entry still equal to the prepared base is retained, preserving preparation-removed links. Conversion refuses custom filter attributes and ambiguous Git configuration paths without running clean or process filter programs. Scratch index and object writes leave the real index, refs, HEAD and object store unchanged. The diff reviewer receives the rendered candidate patch and its base and tree identities. The gate hashes that patch at admission and checks both its digest and the candidate fingerprint before accepting a verdict. A changed or missing patch, changed candidate, or unverifiable checkout requires fresh review without consuming a completed round. State and patch files share the agent user, so this is bundle policy rather than OS isolation or protection from forged state or transient patch replacement. One advisory plan review completes on either verdict. Diff review permits five completed verdicts per loop; incomplete calls and unchanged rejected candidates spend no round, and already approved candidates cannot be reviewed again. A completed edit clears diff approval. Hook state follows the Curie session and exact checkout root across prompts, keeps separate nested checkouts, and a platform wait_ci continuation opens a new diff loop. Timing comes from the registered get_issue result: execution_deadline D and execution_seconds S. At D minus S//6, no plan review or new implementation round starts. At D minus S//12, edits, Bash and diff review stop; earlier Bash foreground timeouts are capped at the remaining wrap-up allowance. Approved candidates may publish until D. A timed-out Bash command can continue in the background until sandbox termination; an unobserved exit never proves verification. Refusal replies retain unresolved findings while pod logs expose bounded gate causes without those findings. The first-party factory runner layer now includes checksum-pinned Helm 3.16.4 for Linux amd64 and arm64, extending its existing toolchain without changing the harness or bundle format. Verification routing selects runner checks for runner-only changes instead of also selecting unrelated backend suites. Local kind trial guidance requires at least 16 GiB allocated to Docker Desktop and treats an opened pull request as publication, with CI settlement and human acceptance checked separately. The new capability and evaluator guides separate shipped source, supported adoption, design gaps and executed acceptance; passing checks or a published pull request does not establish correctness, billing reconciliation or ROI. The runner progress tool still applies the later wait_ci cap of three to the shared implement phase, so implement reports for rounds four and five are refused as documented in #5203. The hook separately records all five review_diff rounds; this reporting limit does not lower the review gate cap.

nodes.label: Chief of Staff
nodes.subtitle: Operating pattern
nodes.description: A scheduled briefing pattern that reads across sources on a fixed cadence and posts one digest to a channel. It is a bundle plus a schedule plus a channel binding, not a new architecture box.

nodes.label: SRE triage
nodes.subtitle: Example bundle
nodes.description: A shipped example bundle that triages alerts, gathers Kubernetes evidence, and gates mutations through approval routes. Its default credential limits writes to demo workloads. An optional, operator applied grant expands that same connector across built in resources while keeping Secret reads blocked; approval remains the checkpoint for writes, but the connector credential itself carries the wider Kubernetes authority. This is a bundle policy choice within the isolated runtime. Its reliability alerts count a new counter series' first sample and watch always recorded gauges for absent metrics, and the acceptance path provisions its observability connector before the first deploy. The installer can add observability to an existing release without upgrading Curie. It selects Alloy parsing from the uniform eligible node runtime and refuses mixed or unsupported formats. Reliability alerts observe active log files, stopped Loki delivery, and missing Alloy scrapes. Bound protected deliveries may nominate policy-declared remediation as data. The platform performs precondition reads, bounded model-free execution and independent verification; failed recovery opens a breaker and offers argument-bound human approval. Qualification and protected installation commissioning remain independent gates. The alert signer returns 502 on upstream faults and logs only a numeric status or transport_error. SRE guidance compares metrics by timestamp and window. An opt-in scaler connector serves a reversible scale_deployment action with a sealed prior state, observe_version and an executor-only restore, so automated remediation has an acting connector it can qualify; the default bundle does not declare it. The alert signer enforces a read-only intake policy whose success receipts must carry the probed source generation. Adapter credential sync can retire and repair credentials, startability can exclude binding kinds, and an example turn canary standing monitor turns selected routes through the worker stream and compares declared bindings for drift. The turn canary independently observes a matching relay lifecycle with one delivered completion and a nonblank text reply, while preserving the legacy exact-response success, timestamps and exit status. A nonce mismatch can report delivery success with exact-response failure; malformed or unrelated events and duplicate completions fail closed. Skips and cleanup holds create no new delivery observation; the exporter retains prior samples until route removal, and restart leaves delivery unknown until another attempted turn. Internal relay delivery proves neither Slack ingress or posting nor useful work, policy compliance or user impact. SRE triage requires fresh same-route observations and actual transport or user-turn evidence before attributing an outage. Optional probe profiles, selected by an exact inventory agent slug, replace the nonce question with a bounded role-appropriate prompt and pass only when the delivered final reply contains every required literal marker group and no forbidden marker. An optional prefix exclusion rejects a normalized reply that starts with a configured marker and ignores that wording later in the reply. Unmatched routes keep the nonce question. Exact nonce success, delivery success, timestamps and exit status keep their existing meanings, and profiles do not change isolation, wire correlation, cleanup or agent permissions.

nodes.label: Agent identity
nodes.subtitle: Who the agent is
nodes.description: The agent record and its principal: the name a channel binds to, the credentials it may use, and the approval routes that answer for it. Identity is what Curie supplies to an agent that was authored anywhere else. Accepted ADR-0155 fixes the future tenant, human principal, provider installation, bot identity, release, and installation vocabulary, Its tenant schema groundwork has landed, while the broader identity and enforcement stages remain incomplete. An installation now selects among declared Slack bot identities. Each identity has its own application token and binding route; the dispatcher and reply path preserve that selection through a turn. A binding may also restrict which callers can reach its bot. Named Slack relay identity survives approval and publication pauses in reply_identity, independently of the delivery adapter. Default identity and non-relay routes store null; publication admission and replay compare the selector against the selected binding. Provider installation identities and provider namespaces resolve human principals only from exact active links; mismatched installations, namespaces and unsupported providers refuse rather than guess. The current human link resolver supports Slack only. Binding caller lists and the current approval sets still decide access for an agent without a team policy. Accepted ADR 0220 plans a read-only IdP projection of people, groups, account status and known channel accounts. IdP-known accounts require no user action on first use; an unknown chat account connects once through an IdP sign-in button, without administrator-made mappings. Separate invocation and approver teams belong to the agent and apply across its channels. Directory synchronization, account connection and team enforcement remain planned. Migrations 0120 through 0122 now add team sync state, versioned agent access policies and directory identity. A scoped, bounded directory credential lets an external IdP sync write complete versioned team snapshots, people and account status through the directory API; Curie ships no IdP connector of its own. An unknown chat account connects once through a sender-bound, single-use IdP sign-in link. An agent access policy names separate invocation and approver IdP-group teams; channel admission and approval and undo rulings require an active IdP person who is a current member, while a role without a team keeps the legacy lists. Identity mutations publish an admission fence so cached dispatcher decisions never outlive the state they read. The identity writer session stays isolated until settlement, and the mutation is refused when that isolation cannot be held.

nodes.label: Agent bundle
nodes.subtitle: What it knows
nodes.description: The versioned bundle that carries the agent prompt, skills, tool policy, and connector declarations. It is the unit that moves between installs. The curie.bundle.json sidecar may declare an optional finalAnswer validation policy.

nodes.label: Agent deployment
nodes.subtitle: Where it runs
nodes.description: The active deployment of a bundle in one install: the sandbox template, the substrate it claims, and the channel it answers on. Replacing the deployment is how an agent is upgraded. A deployment can select a bundle supplied runner image layered on the platform base, with admission and resource settings checked before its sandbox starts. Factory repositories select operator-built runner digests from tool catalogs and probes. Per-repository templates and pools preserve platform base checks. Runtime per-agent runner binding under ADR 0219 is still planned.

seams.label: Channel ingress + binding
seams.implementations: 3 shipped channel adapters (Slack Bolt, Discord HTTP, email HTTP with current inbound admission refused), a built-in cluster-message reply relay, plus the CLI transport stub
seams.contract: QueuedTurn + ReplyHandle; neutral {kind, address} deployment binding; adapter scoped Attachment references accepted by TurnIn and resolved at the binding endpoint
seams.reason: Slack, Discord, and email all mint or consume the same channel neutral QueuedTurn and (kind, address) binding. Discord and email prove the HTTP edge that Slack does not use, every adapter token remint rotates its row generation, and the reserved built-in cluster-message relay provides the third ReplySink implementation for CLI-driven turns. Slack additionally proves that file references can cross ingress without putting bytes or URLs on the wire. Bindings can limit their admitted caller set, and Slack turns retain the selected bot identity. TurnIn now carries references onto the queue, and the worker selects SlackFileClient or ChannelPortFileClient by binding kind. The generic client fetches opaque ids from the binding endpoint with the same adapter egress credential used for reply delivery. In the cluster relay, adapter chooses reply delivery while optional ReplyHandle.identity chooses the named Slack binding; unknown identities refuse. Named hook signatures use curie.hook.delivery.v2 and authenticate the requested tool_access policy. The email HTTP implementation remains shipped, but current AgentMail messages are refused before the HTTP ingress call because sender authentication is unverifiable. The interface now documents the signed hook tool-access path. Approval and publication pauses persist the named relay reply_identity separately from reply_adapter; default identity and non-relay routes normalize it to null. The dispatcher carries platform sender facts. Grant-bound Slack history and canvas tools read the receiving binding; identity resolution uses exact provider namespace links and named refusal reasons. When an agent access policy names an invocation team, channel ingress additionally requires an active IdP person in that synced team, resolved from Slack identity links or exact IdP email; other channel kinds cannot resolve a person and refuse. Agents without a team keep binding caller lists. Socket Mode counts frames per configured identity with hello, disconnect, events_api, interactive, slash_commands and other types, and forwards SDK session lifecycle logs through the service logger. Slack identity labels admit at most 16 valid slugs per process before folding into other. Mentions in explicitly configured delivery-canary channels are counted and dropped after envelope validation, before relevance, principal lookup, approval handling, admission or dedupe: no API read, placeholder or queued turn is created. Frame counts expose received traffic; a delivery-canary count proves only that the configured mention reached that identity, separately from process heartbeat and connected-identity counts. An agent with an IdP invocation team refuses a caller who is not an active member of that team, even when the binding names no allowed_callers list. An empty caller list admits everyone only for an agent with no invocation team. When OIDC is enabled with an HTTPS redirect, a Slack sender with no linked account who already passed the binding caller check can be offered a one-time connect URL while the turn is still refused.
seams.leakage: Discord v1 and email do not share Slack's in process dispatcher or approval cards; exact address validation remains Slack specific while other kinds use the generic nonempty rule. Discord and mail still emit no attachment references, so their attachment producer behavior remains unproved despite the shipped generic transport. A read only hook receipt cannot establish homogeneous worker and runner support.
seams.nextStep: Exercise another channel attachment producer against the shipped generic transport and establish verifiable sender authentication before reopening email intake.

seams.label: Reply delivery semantics
seams.implementations: 4 ReplySink implementations (Slack, HTTP reply wire used by Discord and email, built-in cluster-message relay, acknowledge-only GitHub)
seams.contract: ReplySink.emit over turn.status, reply.update, reply.post, and turn.completed
seams.reason: The four versioned reply events now leave the worker for three surfaces. Slack still owns edit-in-place streaming and approval-card settlement. The reply wire defines stable progress delivery identities. Scoped API ingress now reaches the durable worker progress store, while progress rendering and adapter delivery remain disabled. The cluster message reply relay retains its reserved adapter after channel binding. Terminal action receipts follow the installation setting, which now defaults to off. The cluster-message adapter continues to select delivery while durable reply_identity selects the Slack binding. Resolution restores ReplyHandle.identity, and publication admission and replay refuse a selector mismatch; default identity and non-relay routes store null. Final answers are stored in the completion outbox before delivery and replayed rather than regenerated. Reply wire 1.2 adds an optional text_mode verbatim on text-only updates; only that form uses 1.2, and adapters must refuse unsupported versions. Slack verbatim answers use one rich text section of text and literal link elements per partition, so the approved characters and line breaks stay exact without a code box. A msg_too_long refusal is resent as smaller keyed parts, and a smaller part that is also refused is replaced by a notice. The turn canary independently observes a matching relay lifecycle with one delivered completion and a nonblank text reply, while preserving the legacy exact-response success, timestamps and exit status. A nonce mismatch can report delivery success with exact-response failure; malformed or unrelated events and duplicate completions fail closed. Skips and cleanup holds create no new delivery observation; the exporter retains prior samples until route removal, and restart leaves delivery unknown until another attempted turn. Internal relay delivery proves neither Slack ingress or posting nor useful work, policy compliance or user impact. SRE triage requires fresh same-route observations and actual transport or user-turn evidence before attributing an outage.
seams.leakage: Discord v1 falls back to text and does not implement buttons. Email sends one correspondent-visible reply per turn.completed and resolves approvals through scoped reply references rather than interactive buttons. Neither surface may fall back to Slack. The kernel also asks undeliverable_reason and edits_in_place through undeclared capability methods. ReplySinkRouter supplies silent defaults for implementations lacking them, so another identity-aware or edit-capable adapter receives no protocol conformance failure.
seams.nextStep: Keep the HTTP reply wire; add Discord interaction or treat email's one-shot reply as a distinct delivery policy rather than a missing Slack feature.

seams.label: Semantic channel interaction
seams.implementations: 4 renderers (Slack Block Kit, terminal selector, mail approval-card and reply text, Discord plain text)
seams.contract: Versioned OutboundMessage with text fallback, Choice, Confirm, and semantic action values
seams.reason: Slack Block Kit, the terminal selector, mail and Discord consume the shared semantic message with different affordances. Scoped progress ingestion reaches the durable worker store, but rendering remains disabled and no deliverer emits those messages. Verbatim Slack text is one rich text section of text and literal link elements per partition, so the approved characters and line breaks stay exact without a code box (ADR 0250).
seams.leakage: The terminal mirror is handwritten; Rust and Python tests share a schema corpus that gates represented bounds but does not regenerate the Rust model and capabilities are modeled but not dynamically negotiated. Discord renders text without interaction widgets. Mail renders Confirm approval cards and settlement, but current inbound provider replies are refused before resolution; it does not render Choice widgets and drops progress.
seams.nextStep: Wire capability negotiation when a shipped surface other than Slack needs buttons or cards.

seams.label: Queue / stream broker
seams.implementations: 1 real broker (Valkey) behind producer and consumer ports
seams.contract: StreamPublisher + StreamBroker ports, frozen payload field, shared bounded consumer, one renewable fenced owner per delivery, and an independently retried terminal completion outbox; durable generation fenced interactive capacity wait with a fixed deadline and reconciled wake
seams.reason: The port and consumer invariants are explicit, but a second broker has not exercised them. The capacity wait is backed by Valkey atomic scripts, so it does not establish another broker implementation. Protected metadata ACLs, authenticated transport and atomic admission are separate internal Valkey primitives, with a separate explicitly provisioned protected consumer. They do not establish a second broker implementation. Delivery and consumer liveness renewals tolerate transport errors only until the last confirmed send plus TTL minus one heartbeat interval. A refused renewal loses authority immediately. Side-effect markers retry before applying the frame, and terminal settlement remains fenced. Runs and evals share this ownership rule. A separate protected consumer now uses authenticated broker authority, generation fences, bounded delivery and dead-letter settlement. The API reconciler recovers preparing admission and releases terminal capacity. Ordinary worker boot cannot activate this lane. Parked capacity waits retry every five seconds, capped at the deadline, without repeating an already delivered notice when no grant was confirmed and the grant is known absent. Ordinary hook enqueue atomically retains a bounded receipt beside its permanent Valkey claim, preserving the original stream ID, conversation and selected tool policy after stream trimming. Faithful completed retries can return that receipt without the original queued turn. Mismatched, malformed or orphan receipt metadata refuses with 409. Legacy claims without receipt metadata still require the original queue entry.
seams.leakage: Some API producers and graveyard readers still bypass the ports; the completion outbox is another off-port writer to the shared graveyard. Conversation lock ownership, liveness records, token checked Lua, set verbs, and redis-py exception types also leak Valkey semantics. Settled retention reads group and pending state and trims with raw Lua outside StreamBroker. DeliveryLeaseStore also reads exact entries and moves pending ownership with XCLAIM JUSTID outside that port. Factory metadata repair records failing check names and status contexts directly in Valkey outside StreamBroker. Hook claim, enqueue and receipt retention also use raw Valkey Lua and MSET outside StreamBroker. Commissioning admission appends with XADD through its authenticated session, outside StreamPublisher, onto the permit-derived protected commissioning lane. Its consumer stays on StreamBroker.
seams.nextStep: No speculative adapter; promote only if a real broker demand appears.

seams.label: Sandbox substrate
seams.implementations: 2 real implementations (Kubernetes, Docker)
seams.contract: Ten method SandboxClient lifecycle with bounded request deadlines, complete quota rejection evidence, quota_has_headroom, pod_unschedulable, and pod_termination; reap_claim_templates removes only stale claim-owned auxiliary resources
seams.reason: The same kernel and runner operate through two materially different runtime implementations. Deployments can use a validated layered runner image with per agent resource settings. Every newly created claim receives a fresh boot credential id, preventing replacement or retry claims from reusing a released credential while preserving agent, scope and expiry. Transient Kubernetes reads are treated as no observation while claims bind; on Kubernetes, claim-timeout diagnostics include a bounded redacted runner log tail. A deleted, deletion-marked, or same-name replaced runner pod now classifies as sandbox-terminated, and WorkItem release deletes only the run's own recorded claim. The gVisor preflight and security probe verify exact sentry uname -v equality with "#1 SMP Sun Jan 10 15:06:54 PST 2016"; a hostname or release string containing gvisor is insufficient. Repository bindings can choose a digest-pinned runner and its rendered pool. ADR 0217 places an opted-in factory execution's Docker daemon outside the sandbox. The chart renders its namespace, quota, NetworkPolicies, admission policy and worker RBAC, and the worker parses a strict daemon configuration, but per-run daemon creation and certificate issuance are not implemented yet. Docker bundle, workspace and attachment inputs use validated named volumes owned by claim and creation attempt, with targeted orphan reaping. Kubernetes retains its init-container and per-claim template/Secret delivery. The chart resolves standard and factory sandbox profiles. Factory-enabled sandbox egress selects factory unless an agent explicitly chooses another profile: 8Gi memory request and limit, CPU 50m request and 2 limit, ephemeral storage 10Gi request and 20Gi limit, workspace and home ceilings 15Gi each, and tmp 4Gi. Per-agent workspace overrides win over generic workspace values and profile defaults; explicit generic resource pairs use standard values for an unspecified side, and claim-time API resource overrides still win. Explicit zero requests survive, while zero volume ceilings refuse rendering. The default 8Gi memory quota permits one factory sandbox, and existing pods retain their original envelope. An explicit generic writablePathSizeLimit sets every writable path. Older computed generic values retained by --reuse-values keep the old envelope; cluster upgrade takes profile defaults while preserving explicit operator values. Failed runner roots carry the last mapped ErrorEvent classification only for classified_failure, with unclassified for an unknown value; budget-exceeded may additionally carry an output ceiling from 1 to 1000000. Provider-error assistant text is excluded from generation output. After a dropped runner stream, the worker waits up to ten seconds for confirmed Kubernetes termination and exports only a bounded OOMKilled, Evicted, Deleted or Unknown reason and an observed 0 to 255 exit code. Event diagnosis preserves a runner exit code; raw termination detail is excluded from span attributes. A remembered boot credential stays valid while its claim is still being provisioned. Release retry runs only after the claim is marked retiring, so a claim that is not yet visible is not treated as already gone. Failed or interrupted claim creation retires the claim, and that retirement marks the credential for release. When CURIE_SANDBOX_ADMISSION is set, claim creation is preceded by an admission check against the published quota envelope and live headroom. A profile may back workspace and home scratch with a claim-scoped ephemeral volume. The default remains emptyDir.
seams.leakage: SandboxView.port, model credential forwarding, connector secret delivery, warm pool behavior, attachment redemption, and production capacity still differ across Kubernetes and Docker. Docker redeems accepted files in the substrate driver and copies them through the Docker API into named volumes; Kubernetes gives the signed reference only to an init container and keeps it off the runner. Kubernetes proves exact named ResourceQuota headroom before one requester retry; Docker cannot prove Kubernetes quota state and returns false. Retained attachment replacement temporarily needs capacity for two claims. Only Kubernetes can report an Unschedulable pod; Docker returns None. Per agent registry egress and its labeled pool are Kubernetes chart features. Kubernetes rejects a connector secret claim when the rendered agent pool cannot deliver it; Docker has no warm pool and injects the value into the runner directly. Only Kubernetes can confirm termination of the exact claimed pod through status or a matching recent event after the stream began; pod_termination distinguishes sandbox-terminated from a transport failure. Docker returns None for that evidence. Quota recovery rotates four-candidate windows through complete inventories, with eval-first and expiry order inside each selection cycle so unreadable routes cannot monopolize passes. It still requires locked route, runner-safety and ownership checks, permits one victim, and retries disappearance reads only within the original cleanup deadline. Requester retry requires confirmed claim and sandbox absence plus exact quota headroom; approval resume uses the same bounds before a capacity refusal. Pool selection branches on the concrete Docker client, while a Kubernetes-only warm_pool_exists probe is undeclared on SandboxClient; a third substrate would inherit these assumptions. Claim-timeout diagnosis bypasses the port: SandboxSubstrate checks for KubernetesSandboxClient and calls its concrete pod_log_tail, which SandboxClient does not declare, so Docker and any third substrate receive no equivalent diagnosis.
seams.nextStep: Keep parity tests focused on the shared outcomes; do not turn substrate choice into a product axis.

seams.label: Cluster lifecycle admission
seams.implementations: 1 Helm and kubectl lifecycle coordinated by the Rust CLI with a worker pre-upgrade hook
seams.contract: Resolve and pin target chart; validate target version, configuration, and schema metadata; own one namespaced CAS checkpoint; drain, migrate once, apply, converge, canary, and commit observed known-good state
seams.reason: The resumable nine-phase driver now owns one namespaced ConfigMap through resourceVersion and holder tests while the pre-upgrade hook keeps installation-scoped drain authority. Retained configuration preserves scalar types and literal dotted keys, explicit context selection binds all child processes to one cluster, and the v0.11.2 release catalog and target API both declare schema 0070 through 0070 independently of the development head. Pending approvals have a versioned additive v2.2 identity shape plus an audited opt-in recovery path for upgrades that strand old rows. The drain gate renews installation-scoped pause authority while waiting, and status reports the remaining lease. A same version verification records skipped drain, migration, and apply phases distinctly from completed work. The driver checks the rendered drain budget against the Helm timeout before mutation. Per-consumer chart Secret checksums roll API and worker when consumed caller keys change. Dev defaults provide a published pair only when neither inline half is present; leaving dev defaults with the retained published key and no replacement refuses. Cluster up preserves recorded runner values and credential references, reuses only a healthy matching unowned controller, and reads the rendered RuntimeClass before the first Helm install. NotFound inference remains distinct from Forbidden admission retry. The historical v0.12.1 serving window is 0076 through 0076. Cluster upgrade removes cleared runner image keys from retained values instead of emitting a null override. Cluster teardown bounds owned namespace deletion to 300 seconds, preserves finalizers, and reports remaining phase, conditions, objects and an exact resume command. A remaining owned namespace yields a transient failure unless an independent permanent teardown failure takes precedence. The controller preflight fails on a current cluster-scope NetworkPolicy list/watch refusal or restart-count growth during observation. Namespaced refusals and previous-container failures remain diagnostic. A completed rollout with a stable Ready leader and advancing Lease renewal can pass. After a restart, the startup-log or successful-reconcile path additionally requires that exact current Ready pod to hold and visibly renew the Lease. The historical v0.12.2 released window is 0076 through 0081, and v0.12.3 is 0076 through 0093. The v0.12.5 candidate and catalog register 0076 through 0106; v0.12.4 remains 0076 through 0093. A clean drain now hands off a 300 second lease. Attest renews only existing same-revision authority, schema-migrate renews throughout readiness and migration, and the last pre-upgrade hold hook extends that authority to the configured roll hold. Independent mail persistence and pre-upgrade gVisor checks run before drain. Missing or foreign authority refuses the upgrade without recreating a marker. Failure after the hold can still pause claims for the remaining roll hold; extend-only renewal never shortens a longer lease. A bare rollback resumes the newest pending-rollback toward its recorded target only when that target exists below it, is deployed or superseded, and matches its chart. An unconfirmed target refuses with explicit recovery choices. Schema-gated dry runs require a catalogued target application version without probing the live database. Schema refusals include the next step in human output and JSON. Without an asserted live revision, a dry run cannot name the safe fail-forward version. Upgrade --take-over lets an operator who has verified that the exact named holder's CLI and Helm action stopped take over its checkpoint; the CLI checks the holder name and refuses while a release hook Job runs.
