After apply, upgrade retires claims whose runner image differs from the agent's rendered template or cannot be resolved, falling back to agent-wide deletion when the template, claims, or pods cannot be read, and rebinds the stock dark factory layer to the layer published for the target when its base matches. Cluster up, apply, diff and upgrade accept ordered -f/--values-file inputs captured once in owner-only copies. Retained typed values are merged before file inputs, with explicit flags last, and admission uses that final overlay. Inline credentials replacing retained external Secret references clear those references before validation. Metadata CI extraEnv configuration migrates to the typed api.githubFactoryMetadataCi value, preserving object shape and masking rendered JSON. Stock runner layers that cannot be rebound are refused during Validate unless the operator explicitly permits clearing. Dry-run namespace ownership follows the effective controller deployment setting. Direct cluster up can infer gVisor off when a present RuntimeClass has a nonempty nodeSelector and a readable node list contains no matching node. Explicit auto refuses that contradiction; explicit require retains the preflight for on-demand nodes. Eligible fake-model auto installs use the same inference. Unreadable node evidence authorizes no reduction, and fake-model lookup failures preserve the original plan. Prepared apply and dry runs do no scheduling inference. Selector membership does not establish taints, cordons, capacity or runtime-handler availability. The chart resolves managed Secret plaintext once per render and hashes each pod's consumed chart-owned keys into checksum/secret, including rendered extraEnv references. Changing a consumed value rolls its consumers; unrelated keys leave checksums unchanged. The first upgrade adds the annotation and rolls existing consumers once. Foreign Secret contents, Jobs and SandboxTemplates are excluded. A store restart does not rotate its persisted database password. Dev installation identity is deterministic for the namespace and release pair; sealed fresh installs remain unique. Every failed upgrade phase exits 1 while preserving the structured report. After failed Helm apply, the driver compares API, worker and UI container and init-container image maps before and after the call. Changed images or an unreadable post-apply Deployment force previous_serving=false even when Helm retains an older deployed revision. This observation covers image maps only. Recovery commands preserve the selected context and an available chart operand. Convergence excludes non-deleting Succeeded and Failed pods from replica counting and Node-image discovery. Active surplus and terminating pods still block convergence. Status keeps retained terminal pods visible without counting them as active replicas. The CLI deletes none of them. Chart rendering accepts an empty GitHub App ID or a positive integral value of 1 to 18 decimal digits, preserving string digits without lossy numeric coercion and refusing malformed values. The v0.13.0 candidate and registered release window are both 0108 through 0108. Historical release windows remain unchanged. Legacy factory migration is part of Validate, before mutation. Plans preserve conditional ownership and model changes, bounded convergence tolerates transient observations, and long release names are shortened consistently before suffixed resources are rendered. The v0.13.1 released application catalog registers schema minimum and head 0108, matching the current API and prior stable release. Failed-only first installs remove data PVCs only after release ownership, installed StatefulSet claim-template matching, revision-one Helm Secret identity, strictly later PVC creation and recorded UID checks. Cleanup deletes proven claims, uninstalls the failed release, and waits for those UIDs to disappear before retry; uncertain provenance refuses cleanup and preserves diagnostics. Cold default-release upgrade dry runs describe stock runner-layer rebinding as conditional until the target chart and runner base are observed. Legacy factory migration omits absent CI policy rather than emitting null required checks. The v0.13.2 release catalog registers schema minimum and head 0108, preserving the v0.13.1 window. Upgrade now rebuilds retained repository runners before Helm and fails forward on a pre-Helm build failure. Draft ADR 0230 proposes one lifecycle record shared with rollback. Printed Helm and kubectl commands retain the pinned Kubernetes context. Saved cluster-message continuation records the resolved context, with an explicit caller context taking precedence. Connectivity failure with no resolvable context uses the shared operator diagnosis; authorization and other failures keep their own diagnoses. With factory.enabled, the API Deployment and schema-migrate Job default to a shared 2Gi memory limit; other installs default to 512Mi. Explicit api.resources.limits.memory wins, including retained 512Mi under --reuse-values. Memory requests remain 256Mi and CPU remains 100m request and 1 limit. The 2Gi choice is headroom rather than a demonstrated memory requirement. The v0.14.1 serving window is 0123 through 0123. The v0.14.3 and v0.14.4 application windows and candidate serving metadata all declare schema minimum and head 0140. Convergence commands retain the 10 second child, 30 second observation and 300 second convergence deadlines. A timeout or read/wait error explicitly kills and waits for the spawned Helm or kubectl child before returning the failure; kill-on-drop also protects cancellation. This changes subprocess cleanup, not lifecycle substitutability.
seams.leakage: Helm, kubectl, rendered chart metadata, worker drain state, approval identity migration fences, and the target API's serving window remain concrete dependencies. The checkpoint is a durable recovery owner, not a general distributed transaction across Helm and Kubernetes. Upgrade refuses absent or partial caller credential pairs before mutation, including dry run, same version verification, and resume. Cluster up can generate a missing pair; upgrade does not. Existing proxies move to replacement keys on agent redeploy or enabled reconciliation, and existing Secret contents changed in place require a manual rollout.
seams.nextStep: Use release upgrade and interruption drills to harden recovery without adding a second lifecycle implementation prematurely.

seams.label: Frozen ACI protocol
seams.implementations: 1 production producer + scripted reference/conformance implementation
seams.contract: SessionConfig, boot env, HTTP control verbs, versioned NDJSON events, optional publication context, canonical approval argument carriers, exact turn admission, and optional per turn tool_access=read-only under ACI 0.5.9, shared across Python, TypeScript, and Rust. Current ACI 0.5.21 also carries the optional BootEnv issue read route and execution scoped capability, plus per turn memory write authority. ACI 0.5.15 adds optional BootEnv.reviewer_model, forwarded as CURIE_REVIEWER_MODEL. Local and cluster overrides can pin or clear it. Ordinary and eval boots forward the per-agent value; omission preserves the override and explicit null clears it. Without an override the runner resolves the SDK Opus alias from the effective credential. Factory quickstart selects a provider-appropriate implementer default for Anthropic or OpenRouter credentials while preserving an explicit model. ApprovalRequest carries optional reply_identity, with regenerated Python schema, TypeScript and Rust artifacts. ACI 0.5.22 adds the optional attachment manifest. It distinguishes files arriving with this message from retained thread files without changing SessionConfig.
seams.reason: This is the strongest documented boundary, and runner and worker now normalize error classifications through shared vectors, but only one production harness stack has proven it end to end. The additive publication context carries a signed execution scoped capability for covered factory turns; its absence preserves the existing path for other producers. Approval grants now bind the resumed call to the stored JSON argument object, including an empty object, and the runner admits only the waiting epoch before it receives the turn input. For a restricted turn, the worker checks the exact runner's advertised enforcement before dispatch. The runner denies tools outside its read only set before approvals or registered callbacks, including tools that require approval even if otherwise classified read only. Restricted steers and slash commands refuse. A session that already sent an unrestricted prompt cannot accept a restricted one; the first unrestricted prompt after a restricted one replaces the SDK session. The worker binds factory issue read authority, and the runner mounts the platform issue tool only when both boot fields are present. The serving runner now refuses a missing bearer credential unless explicit development tokenless serving is enabled. Per-turn memory credentials reach the runner process inside the sandbox, while remaining absent from boot environment and hook or subprocess input. The runner binds its HTTP listener and answers healthz before declared verification preflight and SDK connection finish. Status ready remains false until initialization completes, and admitted turns wait for the shared initialization task. Credential, approval and bundle refusals still precede binding. Verification subprocess groups are killed and reaped on exit, including cancellation during spawn. Managed checkout handoff re-reads only a fully attested candidate whose sole unmet fact is ready=false, polling every 0.25 seconds within its existing deadline; any other mismatch refuses immediately. ACI 0.5.23 adds the optional Final.text_mode verbatim, set only for a validated constrained answer; every other final omits it. The worker-to-runner snapshot control call now carries the retained prepared base explicitly and refuses a missing or malformed base. The frozen ACI event and boot schemas do not change.
seams.leakage: A non-Claude harness must still consume or translate the Claude Code plugin bundle shape. A producer must establish compatible worker and runner artifacts; a hook receipt proves queued policy rather than homogeneous fleet enforcement.
seams.nextStep: Use the conformance guide against a genuinely different production harness.

seams.label: Runner ↔ harness / ModelSession
seams.implementations: 1 production SDK, fake session, and offline blocked-preflight session
seams.contract: In-process ModelSession protocol and declared harness contribution
seams.reason: The named protocol is real, but its message union is still SDK-shaped and the bundle distribution format is Claude Code verbatim. PreflightBlockedSession provides an offline zero-token failure response for blocked declared verification; it is not a second production harness. The existing Claude adapter now times initialization and retains a bounded redacted failure stderr tail without changing ModelSession, ACI, cancellation or retry semantics. A ResultMessage does not close a turn while a tracked non-ambient SDK background task remains live. The runner continues receive_turn on the same session while accounting usage, retaining existing timeout and budget termination. An exact first-line task-notification prompt preserves the factory review-gate state. A fresh prompt captures its checkout fingerprint in at most two attempts sharing seven seconds; failure stops before plan-review spending. Factory review hooks now use the shared canonical candidate and enforce one advisory plan review, five completed diff verdicts and issue-derived timing; these remain bundle policy on the same Claude SDK harness.
seams.leakage: A foreign harness must emit Claude SDK-shaped objects or replace the runner adapter while also interpreting the Claude plugin format. Read-only enforcement is implemented in SDK callback fronts rather than a ModelSession operation. A foreign harness must enforce it itself or the runner can advertise a restriction the harness does not apply.
seams.nextStep: Prove the out-of-process ACI boundary with a second harness; keep provider-native checkpointing an optional capability.

seams.label: Declared harness package
seams.implementations: 1 declared contribution (Claude)
seams.contract: HarnessContribution declares assets, environment and bundle compilation. Internal boot accepts only Claude and its aliases; other names refuse before entry point discovery.
seams.reason: Selection and declared assets are clean, but there is no second real package and third-party conformance remains unproven. ADR 0140 deliberately stops the unfinished multi-harness selector; registered non-Claude contributions are refused.

seams.label: Model provider + credentials
seams.implementations: Multiple live endpoints through one Claude-SDK / Anthropic-wire strategy
seams.contract: Declared wire protocol, provider endpoint, canonical credential keys, and boot-env forwarding ACI 0.5.15 adds optional BootEnv.reviewer_model, forwarded as CURIE_REVIEWER_MODEL. An OpenRouter key spend-limit 403 and an OpenRouter workspace budget 403 both remain credit exhaustion. Budget accounting counts a repeated assistant response id once per turn. Factory usage pairs base model observations with a unique context-window-suffixed aggregate key and avoids counting already reported reviewer usage twice; API pricing strips the trailing context suffix before matching rates.

seams.label: Telemetry / OTLP
seams.implementations: 1 trace backend (Langfuse) behind an OTel collector
seams.contract: OTLP write path + versioned phase semantics + Curie API DTO read path
seams.reason: Curie preserves valid W3C parentage from ingress through durable approval resolution, expiry, and reconciliation. Request path operation spans may carry a task local channel event id without widening metric cardinality. The runner records real provider and tool intervals, Discord uses the shared bootstrap, chart CI discovers instrumented workloads, provider shutdown shares one deadline, and supervised restarts emit bounded restart and give up outcomes. Only Langfuse has exercised both sides. A transcript over its per-thread cap produces a bounded value-limit failure counter, and observation trees preserve concrete tool identity. Generation spans now record redacted input placeholders and output with a turn scope usage fallback. The shared metrics bootstrap defaults to cumulative export for Prometheus and permits an explicit temporality preference for supported instruments. Factory execution now reports measured usage through runner and API records. Provider subscription usage refusals have a distinct terminal model-usage-limited classification, take precedence over credit refusals and interrupt before SDK retries or parent continuation. An OpenRouter key spend-limit 403 and an OpenRouter workspace budget 403 both remain credit exhaustion. Budget accounting counts a repeated assistant response id once per turn. Factory usage pairs base model observations with a unique context-window-suffixed aggregate key and avoids counting already reported reviewer usage twice; API pricing strips the trailing context suffix before matching rates. Operators can add ordered extra trace processors between memory_limiter and batch. An SDK server error naming a transport failure is classified as retryable model-unreachable. FastAPI automatic telemetry setup is disabled so the shared API bootstrap owns export and trace parentage. The module entrypoint preserves logging handlers and applies the same redaction and telemetry configuration to Uvicorn access and error logs. Failed runner roots carry the last mapped ErrorEvent classification only for classified_failure, with unclassified for an unknown value; budget-exceeded may additionally carry an output ceiling from 1 to 1000000. Provider-error assistant text is excluded from generation output. After a dropped runner stream, the worker waits up to ten seconds for confirmed Kubernetes termination and exports only a bounded OOMKilled, Evicted, Deleted or Unknown reason and an observed 0 to 255 exit code. Event diagnosis preserves a runner exit code; raw termination detail is excluded from span attributes. Socket Mode counts frames per configured identity with hello, disconnect, events_api, interactive, slash_commands and other types, and forwards SDK session lifecycle logs through the service logger. Slack identity labels admit at most 16 valid slugs per process before folding into other. Mentions in explicitly configured delivery-canary channels are counted and dropped after envelope validation, before relevance, principal lookup, approval handling, admission or dedupe: no API read, placeholder or queued turn is created. Frame counts expose received traffic; a delivery-canary count proves only that the configured mention reached that identity, separately from process heartbeat and connected-identity counts. The turn canary independently observes a matching relay lifecycle with one delivered completion and a nonblank text reply, while preserving the legacy exact-response success, timestamps and exit status. A nonce mismatch can report delivery success with exact-response failure; malformed or unrelated events and duplicate completions fail closed. Skips and cleanup holds create no new delivery observation; the exporter retains prior samples until route removal, and restart leaves delivery unknown until another attempted turn. Internal relay delivery proves neither Slack ingress or posting nor useful work, policy compliance or user impact. SRE triage requires fresh same-route observations and actual transport or user-turn evidence before attributing an outage.
seams.leakage: Vendor attributes and /langfuse URL namespaces still leak into the otherwise neutral boundary; the read adapter spans multiple modules. The default collector trace pipeline has no attribute mapping, and optional trace processors are operator configuration rather than a shipped mapping. Generation content is written under langfuse.observation attribute names, adding vendor naming on the write side. The five vendor attributes are trace.name, session.id, user.id, observation.input and observation.output under langfuse, plus the bare model key. Eval recording also calls Langfuse ingestion directly rather than only OTLP.
seams.nextStep: Ship a default collector mapping for vendor span attributes and neutralize read-route naming.

seams.label: Eval case + scorer
seams.implementations: Multiple grader kinds plus a trajectory matcher across Python and Rust
seams.contract: Frozen eval-case schema + shared trajectory vectors + tri-state outcomes
seams.reason: Distinct scoring implementations and two languages exercise the case boundary, with shared fixtures pinning semantics.

seams.label: Eval result store
seams.implementations: 1 backend (Langfuse traces + scores)

seams.label: Blob storage
seams.implementations: 1 backend (RustFS) over S3-compatible protocol
seams.contract: API ObjectStore + worker BundleReader + worker WorkspaceObjectPort + bundle, attachment, and managed workspace init paths A text-only follow-up can hand a fresh sandbox the newest retained attachment set for the same thread and agent. The worker remints short-lived object references without extending retention; missing, near-expiry or malformed sets are omitted, and the best-effort lookup is bounded to five seconds.

Chart API and worker consumers now receive the same chart-owned S3 region. Persistent in-chart RustFS runs a storage-guard init container before startup. Below 10% free inodes or bytes, it removes expired Langfuse event objects only within the configured events prefix; any fresh constituent file protects its object. Retention zero disables deletion. The guard runs on pod creation, not a RustFS container-only restart. Fresh claims default to 10Gi; upgrades preserve the live StatefulSet data claim-template size through lookup. seams.label: Relational database

The v0.12.5 candidate API serving head is 0106 and minimum is 0076, sourced from the protected-hooks package and mirrored into API and chart metadata. Read-only startup probes verify one live revision and readable source-policy and operation columns with compatible types; this proves structure, not runtime qualification. Migrations 0091 through 0093 add the owner-loss successor marker, start-deferral count and versioned factory status-sync lease. The v0.12.3 window is 0076 through 0093. The v0.12.5 catalog registers 0076 through 0106; migration 0106 follows 0093 and adds nullable approval and publication reply_identity columns. The historical v0.12.4 released window remains 0076 through 0093. Feature-train models use tenant-scoped relationships and provider identity namespaces. Aggregate CRUD and schema modules replace the prior monoliths without changing the Postgres backing. The current v0.13.1 API serving window remains 0108 through 0108. ADR 0232 is enforced by a gate that compares new destructive migrations with the previous stable application readers. Migrations 0120 through 0122 add team sync state, versioned agent access policies and directory identity. The v0.14.0 release window is 0122 through 0122.

Session and transaction advisory locks, the separate int4 and bigint lock spaces, and NULLS NOT DISTINCT constraints for bindings and transcripts also require preserving Postgres-specific semantics. The catalog also names PostgreSQL full-text search and dialect-specific upsert and conflict behavior; a DSN-only swap proves managed PostgreSQL, not another SQL engine.

seams.label: Approval authorizer
seams.implementations: 6 approver sets (Slack channel, Slack user group, explicit users, email list, no verifiable approvers, IdP approver team)
seams.contract: ApproverSet / ApprovalCreator + authenticated ApprovalPrincipal + durable semantic approval record, with one interactive resolution card, a fresh publication approval for each revision, and a separately granted audited recovery path ; covered factory turns resolve empty publication proposals through one shared runner decision before pending state. Bare operator approval gates must name recognized canonical Claude Code built-ins. Unknown names and CLI aliases refuse runner boot with ApprovalPolicyError. MCP gates must resolve to declared live names; invalid names cannot silently arm a no-op gate.
seams.reason: Six approver-set implementations exercise one API-owned authorization interface after resolver identity is authenticated separately. Chat, Console, operator, and adapter credentials all derive server-owned principal facts before that common decision. The shipped SRE publication gate carries its policy route, enabling explicit user operator resolution; durable rows precede transport delivery. The recorded request location selects the resolving route, and a settled card remains a decision record. Factory publication additionally requires canonical verification observations without changing principal eligibility. Email membership and card authorization remain implemented, while current AgentMail replies are refused before resolution because their sender authentication is unverifiable. Approvals and publications preserve named relay reply_identity independently of reply_adapter. Approval resolution restores it into ReplyHandle.identity, while publication admission and replay compare it against the selected binding. Remediation approvals bind to the nomination argument hash and start a model-free executor rather than resuming a model. Independent verification failure opens a breaker and can offer undo through a separate approval. An approver team named by the agent's access policy now gates approvals and gated undo rulings; route lists can only narrow it. For a first publication, the writer fetches the API-authoritative base branch and, if its tip advanced, replays the approved patch onto that descendant tip. Conflict, empty replay, unrelated history and replay failure stop publication. The API verifies the revision marker and one parent, proves the approved base is an ancestor of that parent and the parent is an ancestor of the current base tip, with one is_ancestor request per relation. GitHub answers from the status of one three-dot compare. Equal shas count as ancestors, and a forge that cannot answer leaves the publication unproved. The immutable approval base stays unchanged; lineage settlement records the actual first parent under publication, lease and lineage fences. Later revisions still require the exact prior published head. A rejected deterministic Job is not recovery authority until the same UID is terminal on two reads around a complete pod inventory and every declared regular, init and ephemeral container is terminated. Missing, replaced, unreadable or incomplete evidence retains the wait without charging an attempt. A timed-out pull-request open similarly waits for quiescence, then permits adoption only of an open matching pull request at the verified head; it never repeats the open request in that recovery path. This is recovery with surviving publication authority, not reconstruction after database loss. When an agent has an IdP approver team, IdpTeamApprovers replaces the route set and a declared route restriction only narrows it. Operator and test-driver principals are not eligible for that set. Agents without an approver team keep the route's set, including channel membership when no approvers are declared. The worker supplies its retained prepared base to the authenticated /v1/snapshot request; the body must contain exactly one full base_sha. Capture includes the net committed, staged, unstaged and nonignored untracked change from that base, so local commits cannot move publication authority. HEAD must be that base or a locally verified descendant within 256 commits and 1 MiB of commit objects. Missing authority, unrelated or unreadable history, changed HEAD or workspace observations, unsafe paths, changed symlinks or gitlinks, and patches above 900000 raw bytes refuse capture before approval creation. The worker still validates the patch against its private sanitized base. A re-admitted run can retire an open headless lineage only when it has failed publications whose outcomes are durable, all belonging to terminal failed executions of one uncancelled WorkItem for the same agent, thread and repository. The API first proves remote branch absence through CodeHost, then locks and rechecks eligibility and the observed lineage version before closing it. A surviving branch or any unavailable or unauthorized read preserves the old pin. Retired rows without a pull request read as absent; rows carrying a pull request remain terminal.
seams.leakage: Channel membership remains Slack-shaped, while Console, operator, and adapter principals are intentionally eligible for only the approver sets their credential kind can satisfy: operators answer explicit-user sets, adapters answer email lists, and neither answers a Slack set. The administrative recovery route deliberately bypasses ordinary membership only when its installation grant is enabled and writes an atomic audit entry. Publication approvals settle durable publication state rather than resuming a model turn, and optional pager delivery is text only. The ADR 0174 precheck is a factory only, read only comparison with its own ppc capability; ordinary managed publication keeps the existing approval path. Bound title or body changes can be admitted without a source commit when identity and current CI evidence pass. Candidate review freshness is enforced by the installed factory bundle, not independently attested by the platform publication service. Draft ADR 0256 proposes object-overlay validation and pushing without a full checkout; the shipped worker still validates a private base archive and the Job still checks out and applies the approved patch.
seams.nextStep: Exercise the scoped adapter principal through another interactive channel before broadening approval authority. Accepted ADR 0220 plans an agent-wide approver team checked against active IdP people and current membership on every channel with a resolver. Route lists may narrow the team; agents without a team retain current sets and card placement stays unchanged.

seams.label: Approval principal identity
seams.implementations: 4 authenticated principal kinds (chat, Console, operator, adapter)
seams.contract: Canonical ApprovalPrincipal + credential-kind eligibility + authenticated audit fields
seams.reason: Four independent credential paths derive one server-owned principal shape before the common membership decision. The adapter credential is bound to a subject, a nonempty set of channel bindings, three exact scopes, and a bounded expiry. The authenticated adapter and selected bot identity are checked against the recorded route before resolution. Console API and approval requests now carry the live HttpOnly session rather than a browser-held platform key, with origin checking before cookie-authenticated mutations. Approver team checks resolve the authenticated principal to an active IdP person and current team membership before the common membership decision.

seams.nextStep: Exercise the adapter principal with another real interactive channel without widening any existing principal kind or accepting the platform key as resolver identity. Accepted ADR 0220 plans IdP-known account links first and one-time IdP sign-in for unknown chat accounts, with no administrator-made mappings. Directory ingestion, one-time connect and approver team checks now exist; an IdP connector that feeds the directory API remains outside Curie.

seams.label: Workflow state store
seams.implementations: 1 state API router over Postgres JSONB
seams.contract: Scoped namespace/key document API with size limits, CAS behavior, and singular shared NULL-scope identity
seams.reason: The HTTP state router is useful, but not every state consumer stays behind it; operator memory and relational paths can bypass the supposed boundary. Successful state deletes and operator memory edits and deletes emit content free operation logs and bounded mutation metrics; ordinary state writes record none, and stored values and memory content are excluded. Action completion and undo acquisition are conditional SQL transitions, and redacted action results retain no prior or post snapshot and cannot promise restore. Binding claims now confine sandbox memory and transcript reach; memory fact writes require a live turn credential and cannot overwrite operator guidance. The API refuses released boot credential ids and closed per-turn write claims. A boot release report that fails remains queued for retry; a failed turn-close report leaves that write credential valid until expiry. The operator memory plane also accepts a live Console session. Every newly created claim receives a fresh boot credential id, preventing replacement or retry claims from reusing a released credential while preserving agent, scope and expiry. SQL additionally owns provider identity namespaces, tracker-neutral work item identities, action execution ledgers, remediation generations and durable protected admission records. Migration 0123 stores a redacted workspace preparation stage and reason, capped at 2000 characters, as last_start_failure_detail. Capacity deferrals and worker replacement preserve it; a successful-start compare-and-set clears it. Waiting, exhausted-start and capacity-expiry outcomes retain the previous start diagnosis instead of replacing it with a generic capacity reason. The v0.14.1 application window requires schema minimum and head 0123. The v0.14.3 and v0.14.4 application windows and candidate serving metadata all declare schema minimum and head 0140. The v0.14.2 application window registers the same schema minimum and head 0123.
seams.leakage: A second state backend would not cover direct model/JSONB access, while memory and transcript loaders still depend on the HTTP shape and capacity limits.
seams.nextStep: Inventory and close bypasses before extracting another backend; then treat retention, capacity, and back-pressure as one admission policy.

seams.label: Agent memory
seams.implementations: 1 loader plus a facts store on the same Postgres backing
seams.contract: Memory loading plus agent and channel fact tools, with binding scoped reads and turn scoped writes
seams.reason: The loader port remains single backed. A separate facts store provides bounded remember, update and forget operations and prompt loading; the API enforces channel scope, fact keys and server recorded authors. Boot reads are claim-scoped with a credential id and bounded expiry, and released ids are refused. Per-turn writes have no expiry grace; steering hands closure ownership to the live turn, while an unsuccessful close remains valid until its deadline. The write token reaches the in-sandbox ACI runner process but stays out of boot environment, hook input and subprocess input. Every newly created claim receives a fresh boot credential id, preventing replacement or retry claims from reusing a released credential while preserving agent, scope and expiry. Operators can list and delete individual facts through the fact store routes.

Legacy SessionRunner.remember appends and consolidation replacement PUTs need platform authorization; the worker's boot token and per-turn fact credentials cannot write the legacy log, so in-sandbox writes go through the remember fact tool.
seams.nextStep: Keep loader, facts and operator paths consistent; automatic compaction remains separate work.

seams.label: Conversation history
seams.implementations: 1 real loader (StateApiTranscriptStore)
seams.contract: TranscriptStore load/append of portable structured turn and summary records, scoped by agent and thread
seams.reason: One real state API store supports structured replay, tool result continuity, bounded compaction, optional native checkpoint reuse, and versioned capacity recovery. Appends reserve space for publication outcomes; on 413 the store rewrites a compacted value by compare-and-set, preserves publication markers and the newest turn, reloads on conflict, and retries before returning a classified terminal failure. The state API advertises its transcript value cap and the runner requires it for every bound, and a single long turn can replace older completed tool exchanges with a deterministic marker while keeping the first user message, final answer, recent pairs, and pending approval. Migration 0060 reconciles newer legacy rows, removes them, and blocks future legacy transcript writes, leaving the transcript table authoritative. Assistant grouping records causal evidence rather than inferring a group from arrival order, and unprovable overlapping tool calls reduce the affected turns to visible user and assistant text, transitively across turns, clearing the native checkpoint; other malformed history is still refused. Subagent messages stay out of portable history while the parent's Agent call and result remain. A boot's attachment notice rides on the first actual prompt and its durable user message, so reattaching the same filename remains visible even when the system prompt matches a native checkpoint. ADR 0205 retains files with the thread, rebuilds them in replacement sandboxes and announces only the current message files as current input.
seams.leakage: Compaction deliberately replaces older message and tool detail with a bounded summary and drops the old native checkpoint. Each thread transcript has its own byte cap with no agent-wide cap, and a value that cannot fit its publication markers, summary, newest turn, and reserve requires operator recovery through versioned export and delete. Ordinary persistence failure marks durability lost, preventing safe cold handoff. Thread files are rebuilt from the ledger on boot. The attachment manifest and materialization status distinguish current, earlier and missing files; disk contents are the final observation.
seams.nextStep: Keep portable replay authoritative, preserve publication outcomes under pressure, and make any future source retention policy explicit.

seams.label: Trigger ingestion
seams.implementations: 8 hardcoded ingress paths (Slack, GitHub push, GitHub review, commit polling, HMAC hooks, factory issue events, factory poll intake, missed-label reconcile) plus worker cron slots
seams.contract: No unified runtime trigger port. Bespoke authenticated producers converge on QueuedTurn and bounded stream delivery; factory issues and reviews retain their durable authority and outbox checks, cron claims one SQL slot, and generic hooks keep HMAC and delivery admission. Signed hooks and ordinary manual or scheduled cron admission also hold current SQL source authority and recheck liveness before effects; configured policy or durable history closes those ordinary paths. hook_runs.source separates manual and scheduled histories, and settlement records a closed vocabulary of terminal reason codes.
seams.reason: Slack, GitHub push and review, factory issues, commit polling, named HMAC hooks, and cron have distinct producer admission rules but converge on the typed queue boundary. Declared cron schedules ship and can be test fired through the operator route without losing their single slot admission. The lost factory label reconciler reuses webhook verification after its grace period. Hook signatures use the curie.hook.delivery.v2 domain and authenticate the requested tool_access policy with the delivery data. Protected source records, signing, broker metadata transport and atomic admission/recovery are internal primitives. Complete protected provisioning, consumer lifecycle and qualified execution remain planned. Protected admission recovery preparation is bounded to 32 attempts. Reads that straddle a concurrent commit are reread before an inconsistent combination is refused; stable orphan combinations remain fail-closed. This does not establish protected consumer wiring or qualified execution. Factory review admission retains the issue cancellation lock until the revision request and delivery settlement commit together; nested dispatch commits use savepoints. Non-GitHub trackers poll per binding through Tracker; repository and trigger label routing are recorded independently. GitHub polling remains the default, and missed-label reconciliation is a webhook-mode path. The catalog now enumerates ten hardcoded producer paths plus cron, including tracker intake and code-host review polling. Initial Jira labels and per-issue hold/retry behavior are implemented. Owned-publication rediscovery suppresses old replay without adopting missing execution history. Ordinary hook enqueue atomically retains a bounded receipt beside its permanent Valkey claim, preserving the original stream ID, conversation and selected tool policy after stream trimming. Faithful completed retries can return that receipt without the original queued turn. Mismatched, malformed or orphan receipt metadata refuses with 409. Legacy claims without receipt metadata still require the original queue entry.
seams.leakage: Slack enters through dispatcher; GitHub push, review, factory issues, polling, and generic hooks enter through API handlers; cron starts in the worker. Review feedback and factory work have their own durable admission and outbox rules. Bundle declared generic hook installation remains planned. Missed factory label recovery polls GitHub from the API reconciler rather than a shared trigger lifecycle.
seams.nextStep: Wire bundle declared generic webhooks into deployment and define their delivery destinations and operator admission; preserve the existing producer authority checks and bounded QueuedTurn delivery.

seams.label: Protected hook source authority
seams.implementations: 1 production resolver (ProvisionedSourceAuthority) plus 2 test resolvers
seams.contract: SourceAuthorityResolver.resolve opens a SourceControlSession for the requested source and target under the agent source gate; its reader returns a reconciled generation floor and its writer reserves and publishes the next generation; publish_protected now accepts an AuthorityTarget and brackets publication with current evidence
seams.reason: ProvisionedSourceAuthority implements the production resolver from authenticated provisioned runtime files. Source policy routes compose it with SourceMutationCoordinator for mutations and SourceAdminService for reads. Protected publication checks current runtime evidence and confirms the broker record. One production implementation establishes a clean boundary; commissioning and qualified installation acceptance remain separate gates. ADR 0236 commissioning components now exist as separate compositions: provisioner core, journal and campaign floor, reservations, ACL observation, a per-call campaign guard with a signed observation channel, standalone ingress and worker entries, and dedicated Qualification, Readiness and acceptance writers. Production composition is barred from importing campaign records, and no shipped command runs a full campaign. BehavioralNetworkProducer is a Protocol implemented structurally by ProbeKit (managed-behavioral-v1) and LocalCiliumNetworkProducer (local-cilium-v1). No production composition root constructs either producer.
seams.leakage: The coordinator and production authority enumerate broker-specific errors, and router composition constructs the resolver directly. Separate protected worker composition cannot manufacture commissioning or installation qualification.
seams.nextStep: Exercise complete commissioning and qualification before accepting an installation; add another resolver only for a concrete broker need.

seams.label: Agent-facing CLI output
seams.implementations: 72 typed outputs behind one trait, with 70 distinct committed result schema files
seams.contract: CliOutput + Ui.emit + versioned JSON result schemas. The strict dark factory renderer receipt schema v2 requires bundle_dir, rendered, runner_image, and runner_note. Its runner fields accept string or null and unknown fields are rejected. Hook fire succeeds only for the durable ran outcome; failed, blocked, skipped and reclaimed outcomes fail while preserving the record and reason. Open runs remain polled until settlement or a transient timeout naming the same-tier record command. Hook record reads an existing run without waiting or judging its outcome. Schedule reads separate newest scheduled and manual histories. Deploy schema v1.2 always includes cron declarations and advisory warnings from the immutable uploaded bundle; unresolved explicit targets warn after successful deployment. Every failed upgrade phase exits 1 while preserving the structured report. After failed Helm apply, the driver compares API, worker and UI container and init-container image maps before and after the call. Changed images or an unreadable post-apply Deployment force previous_serving=false even when Helm retains an older deployed revision. This observation covers image maps only. Recovery commands preserve the selected context and an available chart operand. Cluster rollback schema v1.1 adds resumed_interrupted_rollback to completed results. Schema refusals preserve the next step in human output and JSON.
seams.reason: Many independent command results exercise the same human/JSON emission boundary. The CLI is split into argument, dispatch and command modules. Result families include action execution, remediation policy, qualification and repository runner build receipts. Printed Helm and kubectl commands retain the pinned Kubernetes context. Saved cluster-message continuation records the resolved context, with an explicit caller context taking precedence. Connectivity failure with no resolvable context uses the shared operator diagnosis; authorization and other failures keep their own diagnoses. Factory quickstart sets max_output_tokens_per_run to 250000 through the ordinary per-agent budget command for supported forge paths and adding an agent to an existing install. A positive --output-tokens overrides it. Generic platform defaults remain 100000; the factory allowance is per run. Human and JSON ready receipts report the selected allowance, with factory-quickstart result schema v1.3.
seams.leakage: A tracked set of legacy/operator verbs still has inline or unstructured success output.
seams.nextStep: Finish migrating the tracked exceptions without widening the output contract.

seams.label: MCP connector host
seams.implementations: 1 real Kubernetes host + in-memory fake
seams.contract: Bundle declaration → rendered workload → bounded rollout readiness → mounted MCP entry → runner capability probe
seams.reason: The lifecycle now observes rollout and runner capability outcomes, and transient probe failures can recover on later turns. The renderer and CLI share frozen vectors for the derived Bearer rule, accepting an explicit bearer_secret or one plain-string secret while excluding an implicit SecretRef. The typed client still exposes raw Kubernetes JSON, rendering remains Kubernetes specific outside the port, and CLI and reconciler paths do not share identical apply and prune semantics. TCP readiness now reflects whether the hosted MCP port accepts a connection. Multiple SecretRef credentials remain upstream pod secrets and do not imply client Bearer authentication. The hosted Kubernetes path requires a caller proxy and public key, with API 422 refusal when absent. Its cct proves only agent and expiry, and its admits decision is separate from the one use, argument bound ccg needed for approval gated calls. The Docker development host requires a public key but runs the original image directly with no caller or grant enforcement. Hosted non-secret config is separate from credentials. A nonblank no_client_auth declaration disables implicit client Bearer selection and conflicts with an explicit bearer_secret; caller and grant authorization remain mandatory on Kubernetes. CLI-rendered connector Deployments carry curie.dev/connector-secret-digest over the canonical map of consumed owned Secret keys, including init-container environment and explicit volume items. Changing a consumed owned key rolls that connector; unrelated keys and Deployments without consumed owned keys are unchanged. This does not observe foreign Secret contents rotated in place. Hosted declarations add a loopback proxy_upstream_host rendered only into the caller proxy, a readiness_path and merged server-container resources; they remain one hosted implementation behind the plugin-format renderer.
seams.leakage: Build inputs, pinned images, delegated OAuth, runtime injection, reconciliation, and Kubernetes objects cross control plane and cluster ownership. Only one real host sits behind the port. Skill and local tiers use a separate Docker applier with its own label, pruning, and readiness wait outside this interface. Upgrade refuses absent or partial caller credential pairs before mutation and does not generate a missing pair; cluster up can generate one. Per-consumer chart Secret checksums roll API and worker when caller keys they consume change. Existing connector proxies move on redeploy or reconciliation; foreign Secret contents rotated in place require a manual rollout.
seams.nextStep: Converge CLI and reconciler lifecycle before calling the host portable.

seams.label: MCP service-key authentication
seams.implementations: 1 deployment-owned service identity mode
seams.contract: Named hosted Bearer secret plus a mandatory caller proxy; signed caller claims include agent and expiry with an optional paired run and work item identity; approval grants remain separate
seams.reason: Service credentials cross a named secret boundary, expand into the MCP header in memory, and are removed from the runner process environment before turns, but no second production identity mode has proved the abstraction. For hosted Kubernetes calls, the runner supplies a signed cct with agent and exp, plus an optional paired run and work item identity, and the mandatory proxy checks the admitted agent before forwarding. An approval gated call also needs a separate signed ccg matching agent, connector, tool, canonical args, exp, and jti; Valkey spends that jti once. Docker development connectors run directly without either check. Hosted non-secret config is separate from credentials. A nonblank no_client_auth declaration disables implicit client Bearer selection and conflicts with an explicit bearer_secret; caller and grant authorization remain mandatory on Kubernetes. The caller proxy presents a declared loopback Host only after admission and grant checks. Policy approval routes that would grant a proxied connector tool are refused in-turn, so the argument-bound permission gate holds the call.
seams.leakage: Secret rendering and delivery still span bundle declaration, API, Kubernetes, kubelet and container environment exposure before process startup, and SecretRef residuals. With dev defaults and neither inline key half set, the chart supplies a published caller pair. Leaving dev mode with its retained public key and no replacement is refused. Per-consumer chart Secret checksums roll API and worker when caller keys they consume change. Existing connector proxies move on redeploy or reconciliation; foreign Secret contents rotated in place require a manual rollout. The data-tier policy admits connector pods to in-chart Valkey by default; the allowMcpConnectorValkeyIngress opt-out removes only that peer and does not change caller authorization.
seams.nextStep: Keep service authentication explicit and fail closed; prove delegated OAuth as a separate identity mode with no fallback between them.

seams.label: Per-person MCP OAuth
seams.implementations: 0; accepted architecture only
seams.contract: Canonical run principal → principal-scoped grant → control-plane-owned OAuth gateway → MCP server
seams.reason: ADR-0088 defines the ownership and fail-closed behavior, but the gateway, grant lifecycle, connection action, and resume path are not shipped.
seams.leakage: Until implemented, MCP calls cannot safely act with each human's authority; the existing deployment service identity is the only current mode.
seams.nextStep: Implement discovery, PKCE, encrypted grant storage, refresh and revocation, then prove missing-auth pause and post-callback resume without giving the runner a raw token.

seams.label: Sealed connector credential
seams.implementations: 1 cross-language wire (Rust sealer, Python opener)
seams.contract: Frozen sealed-credential envelope with cluster-side opening. curie seal refuses the exact connector names curie and curie-state before key discovery or encryption; prefixed names remain legal.
seams.reason: The Rust sealer and Python opener interoperate, but the product path is disconnected: validation and delivery do not yet form one working production consumer path.
seams.leakage: Security depends on exact agreement between CLI, API rendering, cluster delivery, and the currently uncalled opener.
seams.nextStep: Connect and prove the complete sealed-secret path before expanding its wire or consumers.

seams.label: Bundle / plugin format
seams.implementations: 1 deliberately adopted format (Claude Code plugin)
seams.contract: Frozen Pydantic models including unhosted_url, SecretRef, and bearer_secret, plus regenerated committed JSON Schema and an immutable content-addressed bundle. The exact platform publication tool mcp__curie__publish_changes is a recognized approval gate without requiring a declared external MCP server. Bundle tool policy cannot remove Curie's built-in platform MCP tools, while a bundle-mounted server named curie remains fully in scope. Invalid cron declarations name the first failing field and distinguish malformed syntax from an out-of-range value. Field-count errors name the existing five-field grammar and observed count. Seven Curie authoring extensions include optionalSecrets. Connector names that forge the -mcp- join are refused only for hosted connectors, those declaring image: or build:; remote url: connectors derive no Kubernetes object name.
seams.reason: The format is strongly enforced but intentionally has one implementation and one ecosystem shape. Bundles can declare a layered runner image and an agent caller policy for hosted connectors. Releases publish the first party factory runner layer, and the renderer records both its layer digest and its platform base digest. The frozen plugin schema is paired with a Rust field-parity gate rather than generated Rust plugin models. Bundles may declare optionalSecrets; operator repository runner tooling remains separate from bundle policy. The Curie-owned curie.bundle.json sidecar gains an optional strict finalAnswer object, and hosted connector declarations gain proxy_upstream_host, readiness_path and resources. The first-party factory runner layer now includes checksum-pinned Helm 3.16.4 for Linux amd64 and arm64, extending its existing toolchain without changing the harness or bundle format.
seams.leakage: This is the main coupling that a non-Claude harness must interpret or translate. A published runner lock written by example rendering trusts the release pipeline for the source-to-image link rather than proving it locally.
seams.nextStep: Do not invent another format; require alternate harnesses to demonstrate a translation strategy.

seams.label: Third-party port adapter
seams.implementations: 0 generic adapter-kit services; Discord and email are first-party adapters on the shipped HTTP edge
seams.contract: Intended deployed-service placement with a shipped scoped adapter credential; generic packaging and conformance remain unbuilt
seams.reason: ADR-0096 places a third-party adapter as a deployed service, and ADR-0154 now supplies a scoped runtime principal for channel token rotation plus approval listing and resolution. The generic kit is still unbuilt; first-party Discord and email adapters use the HTTP edge without that kit.
seams.leakage: Adapter discovery, installation, routing, conformance, and lifecycle are still future work. The scoped credential is a prerequisite, not a complete third-party adapter product.
seams.nextStep: Build the adapter kit only if a third-party channel needs install, discovery, and conformance beyond the two shipped first-party adapters.

seams.label: Agent Proxy boundary
seams.contract: Accepted credential and egress enforcement boundary outside the sandbox
seams.reason: The direction is accepted but intentionally unimplemented pending narrower substrate, TLS, and injection decisions.
seams.leakage: Provider credentials and web egress still enter the sandbox under current controls.
seams.nextStep: Land the follow-up ADRs for substrate, TLS termination, and credential injection before implementation.

seams.label: Eval result → promotion authority
seams.implementations: Commit status exists; internal promotion enforcement does not
seams.contract: Reserved policy boundary between graded evidence and production deployment
seams.reason: The API reports eval state to GitHub, but process_push does not read that result before creating a production deployment.
seams.leakage: Safety depends on external branch protection and release policy rather than a product invariant.
seams.nextStep: Land semantic provenance first, then bind promotion to an authoritative graded result without rebuilding the artifact.

seams.label: Tracker + code host
seams.implementations: GitHub and GitLab tracker/code-host pairs, Jira Cloud tracker, Bitbucket Cloud and Data Center code hosts, plus in-memory contract pairs
seams.contract: Tracker, CodeHost and MarkedComments; immutable provider-qualified references, exact-head CI and declared operation capabilities
seams.reason: GitHub, Jira Cloud with GitHub, and GitLab with GitLab have exercised the factory roles. Jira with Bitbucket Cloud and Data Center now has install drivers; provider-backed acceptance of the expanded pairings remains outstanding. Authenticated acquisition binds the persisted agent through continuation adoption. Existing owned publications suppress replay, per-operation static credentials support rotation, and unavailable issues do not starve the remaining label. Bitbucket Cloud refuses an unverified open matching publication as unconfirmed and asks the operator to confirm; this grants no ownership or continuation authority. Tracker intake names credential repair actions and reports missing or inaccessible repositories. A pull request closed without merging ends CI wait as pr_closed before check evaluation. An unpublished revision with a recorded pull request ends as revision_unchanged. Handoff messages retain up to 4000 characters and render as quoted text with HTML, images and mentions neutralized. Budget stops omit raw verification preflight notes, and Jira links the first succeeded publication. Factory CI now defaults to 3600 seconds from push, still capped by the execution deadline and preserving explicit operator values. GitHub reads base-branch ruleset and branch-protection required-check names. A required name absent from the published head stays pending until the deadline, then ends ci_unverified and names the missing trigger without applying it. Transient rule-read failures can time out; permanent unreadability refuses immediately. Other code hosts declare required-check reads unsupported rather than simulating them. GitHub publication listing keeps one raw page plus matching owned rows. Feedback-only code-host repositories poll conversation comments without issue intake. Factory status quotes now neutralize bracket links, references, images and scheme URLs as well as HTML and mentions. Only model-service causes label text Provider message; infrastructure and CI causes use Details. A failed publication warns that its branch or pull request may already exist. A no-change forge loop still persists the terminal notice. First-publication ancestry is one is_ancestor request per relation. A superseded cancelled GitHub check run is ignored. Configured publication labels are applied once and are not used to start required checks. After a GitHub ref 404, branch_head requires a successful matching-refs read and accepts only an exact ref match with a valid commit id. This permission-bearing read distinguishes confirmed absence from hidden or inaccessible content; malformed, forbidden or unavailable results cannot authorize retirement.
seams.leakage: Legacy GitHub modules remain explicitly allowlisted. Bitbucket CI diagnostics, rerun and write-access queries remain unsupported. Provider fixtures and kind runtime tests do not establish live third-party account parity for every pairing.
seams.nextStep: Complete the Jira with Bitbucket supported install and live acceptance in v0.13.1.

seams.label: Model-free connector execution
seams.implementations: One worker executor, runner-private execute endpoint and caller proxy grant path
seams.contract: Claim one action execution, bind canonical arguments and target connector, commit dispatch once, report confirmed/refused/indeterminate; shared runner-execute vectors freeze the image boundary
seams.reason: The action executor loads no model or harness. Read, forward and restore executions use separate bounded phases. Remediation adds policy generation checks, precondition reads and an independent verifier. With the connector reconciler off, the executor may read connector Deployments itself, and the worker refuses that setting when it cannot apply. The example SRE scaler connector is an opt-in acting connector that returns sealed prior state and version for restore.
seams.leakage: The local tier has no caller proxy or connector deployment, so restore is refused there. Production remediation additionally requires protected delivery and qualified action evidence; executor code alone does not prove that installation.
seams.nextStep: Measure qualification and live recovery on an independently commissioned protected installation.

seams.label: Channel history and canvas read
seams.implementations: 1 production Slack history and canvas reader pair plus HTTP test fakes
seams.contract: Grant-scoped channel history and canvas operations through ChannelReader and CanvasReader
seams.reason: The API checks current binding, generation and per-operation grants before the production Slack reader accesses history or canvas. One reader pair exercises the protocols.
seams.leakage: Reader registration and credential selection remain Slack-specific. Canvas orchestration uses Slack method names for rate-limit keys; another channel needs explicit mapping.
seams.nextStep: Implement another real reader before claiming interchangeable channel history.

seams.label: Mail provider
seams.implementations: 1 built-in provider (AgentMail); conformance kit for out-of-tree providers
seams.contract: Versioned MailProvider Protocol: inbox address, sender verification declaration, sent visibility bound, list, read, reply in thread, thread marker lookup, config problems and neutral failure kinds
seams.reason: ADR 0228 moved every service-specific call behind one internal Python interface inside the neutral email adapter, which keeps the channel protocol, delivery state, inbound gate, intake and approvals by email. Only AgentMail implements it, and it declares no sender verification, so a second real provider has not exercised the boundary.
seams.leakage: The interface is internal to the adapter and not a frozen or generated contract. A provider that cannot promise read-after-write or a bounded sent visibility does not conform. The test verifying provider is a fixture, not a second implementation.
seams.nextStep: Ship or qualify a provider that verifies senders so email ingress can open, and run it through the conformance kit.

routes.label: fresh HMAC and live ordinary source gate
routes.description: Ordinary hook enqueue atomically retains a bounded receipt beside its permanent Valkey claim, preserving the original stream ID, conversation and selected tool policy after stream trimming. Faithful completed retries can return that receipt without the original queued turn. Mismatched, malformed or orphan receipt metadata refuses with 409. Legacy claims without receipt metadata still require the original queue entry.

start ACI server

Status ready remains false until initialization completes, and admitted turns wait for the shared initialization task. Credential, approval and bundle refusals still precede binding. Verification subprocess groups are killed and reaped on exit, including cancellation during spawn. Managed checkout handoff re-reads only a fully attested candidate whose sole unmet fact is ready=false, polling every 0.25 seconds within its existing deadline; any other mismatch refuses immediately.

Tracker intake names credential repair actions and reports missing or inaccessible repositories. A pull request closed without merging ends CI wait as pr_closed before check evaluation. An unpublished revision with a recorded pull request ends as revision_unchanged. Handoff messages retain up to 4000 characters and render as quoted text with HTML, images and mentions neutralized. Kubernetes MCP via caller proxy; Docker direct
context-pinned admission / converge / canary / recover

A timeout or read/wait error explicitly kills and waits for the spawned Helm or kubectl child before returning the failure; kill-on-drop also protects cancellation. This changes subprocess cleanup, not lifecycle substitutability.

flows.label: Whole system
flows.summary: Every currently visible component and route in one architecture map. Choose a specific flow to isolate and walk its path.

flows.label: Slack turn
flows.summary: A mention and any file references become one queued, isolated, multiturn model session with accepted files mounted read only and one durably delivered edited thread reply. Under capacity pressure an interactive turn is durably queued until an exact runner admission succeeds or its fixed deadline expires. A selected bot identity and caller admission policy are preserved from ingress through reply. A verified bot authored thread root may be quoted as bounded untrusted context with neutralized slashes and no new routing authority. The final answer is stored in the completion outbox before Slack delivery and replayed rather than regenerated. Delivery-canary mentions stop at ingress without starting this flow. Verbatim answers preserve exact characters and line breaks as rich text sections with literal links, and a msg_too_long refusal is resent as smaller keyed parts, and runner stream failures wait up to ten seconds for positive termination evidence.

steps.title: Receive and deduplicate
steps.caption: Bolt receives the mention and file references; the dispatcher claims the event id and posts the placeholder without downloading file bytes. For threaded mentions it verifies a bot authored root and adds bounded untrusted context with neutralized slashes. A configured delivery-only canary is counted and refused before this dedupe or placeholder path, with no API middleware lookup.

steps.title: Normalize ingress
steps.caption: The dispatcher serializes a channel-neutral QueuedTurn onto curie:runs.

steps.title: Claim delivery
steps.caption: The worker consumer group claims the event and acquires the conversation lock.

steps.title: Park accepted attachments
steps.caption: The worker downloads and validates accepted channel references, stores bytes under a private prefix, and mints one short lived signed object reference.

steps.title: Materialize private inputs
steps.caption: A credentialless init path streams, hash verifies, and materializes the immutable bundle and accepted files; the runner receives neither channel nor object store credentials. A text-only follow-up can hand a fresh sandbox the newest retained attachment set for the same thread and agent. The worker remints short-lived object references without extending retention; missing, near-expiry or malformed sets are omitted, and the best-effort lookup is bounded to five seconds.

steps.title: Resolve and isolate
steps.caption: The binding selects agent, version, and bundle, then SandboxClient claims or resumes the runtime with accepted files mounted read only. An idle retained generic thread with files uses a fenced cold replacement only after proving durable history; active or unsafe routes refuse.

steps.title: Start or steer
steps.caption: The worker sends event for a fresh turn or steer for an unrestricted live one. A restricted turn requires the exact runner to advertise enforcement and never steers.

steps.title: Rehydrate durable memory
steps.caption: At boot the runner loads attributed agent and channel facts using its binding scoped read credential before composing the effective prompt. Writes use a separate live turn credential when enabled.

steps.title: Enter the harness
steps.caption: The runner translates the ACI request into the active ModelSession.

steps.title: Run inference
steps.caption: The declared Claude harness calls the selected provider and streams its result.

steps.title: Stream outcomes
steps.caption: The runner emits text deltas, tool notes, side-effect markers, and a terminal result as NDJSON. A transcript capacity refusal replaces a successful or approval final with an explicit classified failure before delivery. An SDK result while non-ambient background tasks remain live holds this same turn open; timeout and budget stops still terminate it.

steps.title: Return to the surface
steps.caption: The worker records turn.completed in its durable outbox before the done marker, ReplySink updates the original placeholder, and the stream entry is acknowledged; a failed emit is retried independently. Verbatim finals use rich text sections with literal links so exact characters and line breaks survive, and a msg_too_long part is resent in smaller keyed pieces.

flows.label: Discord turn
flows.summary: A Discord mention becomes a public thread, a platform-minted QueuedTurn, and streamed text edits on that thread.

steps.title: Admit the mention
steps.caption: adapters/discord creates a public thread and placeholder, then posts to POST /channels/turns under a scoped channel token.

steps.title: Enter the same core
steps.caption: The API mints a channel-neutral QueuedTurn onto curie:runs.

steps.title: Claim delivery
steps.caption: The worker consumer group claims the event under one renewable fenced owner.

steps.title: Resolve and isolate
steps.caption: Multi-surface binding selects the agent by (kind, address) without cloning the bot identity.

steps.title: Start or steer
steps.caption: The worker sends event for a fresh turn or steer for a live one.

steps.title: Return to the thread
steps.caption: HttpReplyAdapter streams text edits to the Discord placeholder. Buttons and approvals are not implemented.

flows.label: Approval + resume
flows.summary: A gated tool call ends the turn, persists authority, suspends the sandbox, then resumes through a new queued event. A permission grant is tied to the denied tool and canonical argument object, and duplicate resume deliveries share one fenced event claim. The request location selects the card route, and settled cards preserve an ordered record in the requester thread. Durable approvals preserve named relay reply_identity independently of reply_adapter; the queued resolution turn restores ReplyHandle.identity. An agent with an approver team additionally requires a current IdP team member.

steps.title: Gate the side effect
steps.caption: The runner terminates AWAITING_APPROVAL; the kernel converts it into durable governance work.

steps.title: Persist the decision point
steps.caption: The API stores the approval, policy, requester, allowed approver set, and validated originating trace context. The durable record also preserves a named relay reply identity independently of its delivery adapter.

steps.title: Render a semantic confirm
steps.caption: Only after the durable row and suspension, the worker delivers the card and pending notice. Missing transport or reply reference does not erase the decision point; operator credentials can resolve routes bound to explicit users.

steps.title: Authorize the human
steps.caption: Slack signs an approval-bound chat attestation; the API derives the principal and resolves membership without trusting caller-supplied identity or channel. A non-owning release acknowledges an exact record miss without changing the approval or card, leaving the owning release's compare-and-set as the only mutation path.

steps.title: Queue a new resolution turn
steps.caption: The original event is already acknowledged; resolution enters as its own QueuedTurn under the stored trace context, while legacy or malformed carriers start clean roots. Failed resume enqueues observed by the current API process are retried on the next reconciler pass. The process record is capped at 10,000 approvals; restart loss and failures beyond that cap retain the grace backstop. A short locked transaction enqueues before marking resumed and retains still-owed locked rows for another pass. The queued ReplyHandle restores the stored reply identity.

steps.title: Reclaim the conversation
steps.caption: The worker restores the same thread affinity and suspended sandbox.

steps.title: Resume with one-shot allowance
steps.caption: The resolution turn tells the runner whether to continue or terminate the rejected action.

steps.title: Settle the surface
steps.caption: The card becomes non-interactive and the final reply returns to the same conversation.

flows.label: PR / git deploy
flows.summary: A development branch push becomes an immutable bundle, deployment, and eval fan-out; a production push promotes the stored artifact without cloning or rebuilding it.

steps.title: Ingest a push
steps.caption: HMAC webhook or outbound commit poller converges on the same process_push function.

steps.title: Archive, validate, store
steps.caption: The API archives the SHA, validates the frozen plugin shape, and writes an immutable bundle.

steps.title: Create version + deployment
steps.caption: Dev branches activate the new version; production branches promote an existing artifact.

steps.title: Fan out evals
steps.caption: A newly built development bundle appends one deduplicated EvalJob to curie:evals.

steps.title: Grade the exact bundle
steps.caption: The eval consumer loads cases from the immutable bundle and drives the runner.

steps.title: Record evidence
steps.caption: Each case writes a tagged trace; graded cases also write an eval score, while plumbing-only cases remain ungraded.

steps.title: Report the rollup
steps.caption: The worker posts the result to the API.

steps.title: Publish, but do not internally gate
steps.caption: GitHub receives a commit status; production promotion still relies on external policy rather than an API invariant.

flows.label: Eval + parity ladder
flows.summary: One bundle and one case file cross skill, local, local-release, and cluster to expose environment drift. Push and pull-request CI runs the smoke upgrade shard; scheduled or manual full kind dispatches exercise the complete upgrade matrix. Python pytest runs six isolated shards behind its required aggregator, with static and workflow-policy gates separate. Image proofs consolidate smoke, connector import, Docker daemon and toolchain checks. Kind upgrade image imports stream platform-specific Docker exports into each node using its configured CRI snapshotter and discard unpacked layer blobs. Provisioned evals preserve hosted connector authority and operator tool gates. Matrix reads remain complete within a bounded, uniquely ordered trace history and filter a requested stream exactly. Scripted factory kind imports use inspected candidate image sizes to require their sum plus the largest in-flight image plus a 10 GiB runtime reserve. Exports stream directly into each node using its configured CRI snapshotter with discard-unpacked-layers; no Docker save archive is materialized. The upgrade matrix uses the same streamed import strategy. These are test harness resource bounds, not a production storage guarantee. Disposable upgrade CI force deletes its release pods before deleting their namespace, preserving namespace finalizers. Retained-values cleanup failures collect bounded read-only namespace conditions, finalizers, resource summaries and read errors. flows.label: MCP with service key
flows.summary: An MCP connector acts as a deployment owned service account. Hosted Kubernetes calls must pass caller admission and, for an approval gated tool, an argument bound one use connector grant. Skill and local Docker connectors run the original image directly without those proxy checks.

steps.title: Reconcile the hosted workload
steps.caption: The worker lists, applies, and deletes the bundle derived Kubernetes connector resources. Hosted rendering requires the caller proxy and public key; the API returns 422 without them.

steps.title: Bind the service identity
steps.caption: The bundle names the connector secret; deployment configuration supplies the value and the platform injects it into the hosted MCP connector.

steps.title: Call the MCP server
steps.caption: The mandatory Kubernetes proxy verifies cct {agent, exp} and admits the agent. An approval gated tool additionally needs a signed ccg matching agent, connector, tool, canonical args, exp, and a jti spent once through Valkey. flows.label: Future per-person MCP OAuth
flows.summary: The accepted vision binds each run's canonical human principal to that person's OAuth grant. Curie applies the grant at a gateway, and the runner never receives the raw token.

steps.title: Resolve principal and grant
steps.caption: The control plane owns OAuth discovery, PKCE, encrypted token storage, refresh, revocation, and the principal-to-grant binding.

steps.title: Call as the run principal
steps.caption: The runner sends a principal-bound MCP request to the gateway without receiving a provider token.

steps.title: Apply delegated authority
steps.caption: The gateway applies only that principal's active grant and exchanges MCP traffic with the declared server. Missing auth pauses the run for a connection action, then resumes after callback.

flows.label: Email turn
flows.summary: Current AgentMail inbound messages are refused before a turn or approval can start because sender authentication is unverifiable. The shipped HTTP and worker path remains available for historical accepted deliveries, whose completion can still send one threaded reply. Mail service calls now go through a versioned MailProvider; AgentMail is the built-in provider and still refuses unverifiable senders.

steps.title: Refuse unverifiable inbound messages
steps.caption: The adapter polls AgentMail and records authentication_unverifiable in local SQLite before body fetch, HTTP turn admission or approval handling.

steps.title: Retain the historical HTTP path
steps.caption: The adapter retains its row-scoped channel credential and HTTP contract, but current provider messages do not pass the authentication gate and make no POST /channels/turns call.

steps.title: Enter the same core
steps.caption: For historically accepted deliveries, the API minted the same QueuedTurn used by Slack, Discord and the CLI stub. Current provider intake creates no new queued turn.

steps.title: Reuse the worker invariants
steps.caption: Existing accepted work retains ordinary routing, concurrency, sandboxing and renewable delivery ownership.

steps.title: Reuse the ACI
steps.caption: The ACI path remains unchanged for existing accepted work; current provider intake cannot reach model execution.

steps.title: Send one threaded reply
steps.caption: Historical accepted deliveries still receive worker reply events and can send one threaded reply at confirmed completion. Failed terminal delivery remains independently retryable.

flows.label: Generic webhook turn

Signed authentication is repeated under a live source gate; configured policy or operation history refuses this ordinary path. Complete protected delivery remains planned. Ordinary hook enqueue atomically retains a bounded receipt beside its permanent Valkey claim, preserving the original stream ID, conversation and selected tool policy after stream trimming. Faithful completed retries can return that receipt without the original queued turn. Mismatched, malformed or orphan receipt metadata refuses with 409. Legacy claims without receipt metadata still require the original queue entry.

steps.title: Authenticate the named hook
steps.caption: The API verifies the per hook HMAC under the curie.hook.delivery.v2 signature domain, authenticates the requested tool_access policy, claims the delivery id, and resolves the target agent.
