steps.caption: For a configured alert hook, the API extracts only the named workload field, maps it through operator-owned agent state to an allowlisted repository and recorded revision, and refuses missing, ambiguous, malformed, or unauthorized mappings. Payload URLs never select a workspace.

steps.title: Mint the platform turn
steps.caption: The API creates the typed webhook-sourced QueuedTurn with bounded delivery metadata, escaped and explicitly delimited untrusted payload, and trusted source binding facts outside that payload. A requested read only policy is carried on this exact turn; receipt or replay acknowledgement does not prove fleet enforcement or reply delivery. The held source gate is rechecked before every delivery effect; no protected payload falls back into the ordinary stream.

steps.title: Reuse bounded delivery
steps.caption: The shared consumer claims, caps, and dead-letters the hook turn like other run traffic.

steps.title: Run through the same ACI
steps.caption: The worker drives the selected bundle without a channel adapter in the path. A webhook turn starts fresh and never steers a live session. For a restricted turn it checks the exact runner's advertised enforcement before dispatch; the runner denies disallowed and approval requiring tools before registered callbacks. Restricted slash commands refuse, and incompatible session history cannot accept a restricted prompt.

flows.label: Future bundle hooks

steps.title: Reuse API-owned ingress
steps.caption: A future declaration resolves onto the shipped named-hook endpoint rather than a new dispatcher.

steps.title: Create a typed turn

steps.title: Reuse bounded delivery
steps.caption: The shared stream consumer must still cap attempts, dead-letter, and expose failure.

flows.label: Managed workspace
flows.summary: A scoped server thread selects one allowlisted repository, receives a sanitized private checkout, and can replace a generic sandbox only at a fenced turn boundary. The runner binds its HTTP listener and answers healthz before declared verification preflight and SDK connection finish. Status ready remains false until initialization completes, and admitted turns wait for the shared initialization task. Credential, approval and bundle refusals still precede binding. Verification subprocess groups are killed and reaped on exit, including cancellation during spawn. Managed checkout handoff re-reads only a fully attested candidate whose sole unmet fact is ready=false, polling every 0.25 seconds within its existing deadline; any other mismatch refuses immediately. Review revision checkouts fetch the recorded base commit as a depth-one object without changing the verified head. Pre-start workspace failures retain their bounded diagnostic across later capacity waits until a successful start.

steps.title: Resolve scoped workspace identity
steps.caption: The worker sends the canonical channel binding plus conversation identity and any trusted repository fact. Review bodies and webhook payload URLs cannot select a repository.

steps.title: Authorize and persist sticky selection
steps.caption: The API derives the agent from durable deployment state, checks the repository allowlist, and atomically establishes or confirms one repository for that scoped thread. A conflicting selection is terminal.

steps.title: Redeem bounded clone authority
steps.caption: The API rechecks current selection and policy, then returns a short lived repository credential for the server-derived target and optional recorded revision only.

steps.title: Clone, sanitize, and archive
steps.caption: The trusted worker clones the selected revision, rewrites and verifies the clean remote, bounds the archive, and stores it under the scoped workspace identity. A review checkout additionally fetches its recorded base commit without changing the exact head checkout or unshallowing the repository.

steps.title: Materialize the private checkout
steps.caption: A one-object signed reference and digest let credentialless init stream and verify /workspace. The runner receives no GitHub or object store credential.

steps.title: Commit the fenced handoff
steps.caption: A late workspace cold-claims a prepared replacement and compare-and-set swaps the scoped route only at the next turn boundary. A failed or stale candidate leaves the prior route authoritative.

flows.label: Approval gated publication
flows.summary: Each proposed workspace revision receives a fresh durable approval, then a fenced cluster job creates or advances the one pull request owned by that scoped thread and repository. Bound pull request metadata can change without a source commit when identity and CI evidence remain current. Approvals and publications preserve the named relay selector independently of reply_adapter; admission and replay compare it against the selected Slack binding. For a first publication, the writer fetches the API-authoritative base branch and, if its tip advanced, replays the approved patch onto that descendant tip. Conflict, empty replay, unrelated history and replay failure stop publication. The API verifies the revision marker and one parent, proves the approved base is an ancestor of that parent and the parent is an ancestor of the current base tip, with one is_ancestor request per relation. GitHub answers from the status of one three-dot compare. Equal shas count as ancestors, and a forge that cannot answer leaves the publication unproved. The immutable approval base stays unchanged; lineage settlement records the actual first parent under publication, lease and lineage fences. Later revisions still require the exact prior published head. A rejected deterministic Job is not recovery authority until the same UID is terminal on two reads around a complete pod inventory and every declared regular, init and ephemeral container is terminated. Missing, replaced, unreadable or incomplete evidence retains the wait without charging an attempt. A timed-out pull-request open similarly waits for quiescence, then permits adoption only of an open matching pull request at the verified head; it never repeats the open request in that recovery path. This is recovery with surviving publication authority, not reconstruction after database loss. A running request can open a new publication only while its runtime owner, heartbeat lease, and execution deadline are all still live. Local commits remain part of the net prepared-base candidate. Shared candidate construction aligns bundle review with capture, while trusted worker validation and revision-bound approval remain separate authority checks. Draft ADR 0256 proposes replacing archive validation and checkout-based pushing with a bounded object overlay; it authorizes no implementation.

steps.title: Capture from the trusted prepared base
steps.caption: The worker supplies its retained prepared base to the authenticated /v1/snapshot request; the body must contain exactly one full base_sha. Capture includes the net committed, staged, unstaged and nonignored untracked change from that base, so local commits cannot move publication authority. HEAD must be that base or a locally verified descendant within 256 commits and 1 MiB of commit objects. Missing authority, unrelated or unreadable history, changed HEAD or workspace observations, unsafe paths, changed symlinks or gitlinks, and patches above 900000 raw bytes refuse capture before approval creation. The worker still validates the patch against its private sanitized base. Review and capture share build_candidate. It reads final file contents, modes and index flags rather than trusting Git stat caches or a working-tree diff. Ordinary changed tracked files use Git built-in clean conversions; paths Git does not read use raw disk bytes. A missing skip-worktree entry still equal to the prepared base is retained, preserving preparation-removed links. Conversion refuses custom filter attributes and ambiguous Git configuration paths without running clean or process filter programs. Scratch index and object writes leave the real index, refs, HEAD and object store unchanged.

steps.title: Validate the proposed revision
steps.caption: The worker verifies repository, base commit, changed paths, binary patch, scoped workspace identity, and any review reservation before creating governance work. Review feedback never grants publication. Factory publication also validates canonical verification observations before governance work, while ordinary managed publication retains its existing revision authority. Publication snapshots accumulate the response through EOF under the encoded and decoded size limits. Retryable read faults receive at most three reads within the remaining budget, without rerunning the model. Exhaustion names infrastructure read failure in the issue. Idempotent publication creation and execution settlement writes retry transient API faults within bounded authority; unresolved terminal reports retain heartbeat and sandbox ownership until settlement or the execution deadline. Charged publication reconciliation retries back off from fifteen seconds to five minutes. The diff reviewer receives the rendered candidate patch and its base and tree identities. The gate hashes that patch at admission and checks both its digest and the candidate fingerprint before accepting a verdict. A changed or missing patch, changed candidate, or unverifiable checkout requires fresh review without consuming a completed round. State and patch files share the agent user, so this is bundle policy rather than OS isolation or protection from forged state or transient patch replacement.

steps.title: Create approval and publication atomically
steps.caption: One transaction records a fresh revision-bound approval, publication, reply route, immutable lineage authority, and optional review reservation. Stale or already consumed authority is refused. The publication gate carries its declared policy route. Both rows preserve the named relay reply identity, and replay refuses an identity mismatch.

steps.title: Deliver one interactive card
steps.caption: The leased outbox posts the sole interactive resolution card. Any configured pager receives text only and cannot create a second card or approval authority. CLI ingress retains its reply adapter, and card delivery does not shorten the pending approval lifetime.

steps.title: Resolve durable publication authority
steps.caption: An authenticated eligible chat, Console, or operator principal resolves the captured approver set. Denial settles without redeeming a credential or creating a Job; approval never resumes the model.

steps.title: Claim the exact lineage revision
steps.caption: The reconciler leases the approved publication, compare-and-set checks current lineage generation, parent head, reservation, and allowlist, then redeems a short lived writer credential. Terminal or stale lineages are refused.

steps.title: Run a deterministic writer
steps.caption: A tokenless, no-RBAC Job receives the validated patch and file-backed askpass credential, checks out the recorded parent, safely applies and commits, and emits one bounded result marker. For a first publication, the writer fetches the API-authoritative base branch and, if its tip advanced, replays the approved patch onto that descendant tip. Conflict, empty replay, unrelated history and replay failure stop publication. The API verifies the revision marker and one parent, proves the approved base is an ancestor of that parent and the parent is an ancestor of the current base tip, with one is_ancestor request per relation. GitHub answers from the status of one three-dot compare. Equal shas count as ancestors, and a forge that cannot answer leaves the publication unproved. The immutable approval base stays unchanged; lineage settlement records the actual first parent under publication, lease and lineage fences. Later revisions still require the exact prior published head.

steps.title: Create or advance the same pull request
steps.caption: The fenced branch and lineage generation create the first pull request or advance that same open pull request. Retry adopts the deterministic branch and existing pull request instead of creating a second lineage. The Job pushes only the branch. The API verifies its marked remote commit and finds or opens the pull request through CodeHost. A rejected deterministic Job is not recovery authority until the same UID is terminal on two reads around a complete pod inventory and every declared regular, init and ephemeral container is terminated. Missing, replaced, unreadable or incomplete evidence retains the wait without charging an attempt. A timed-out pull-request open similarly waits for quiescence, then permits adoption only of an open matching pull request at the verified head; it never repeats the open request in that recovery path. This is recovery with surviving publication authority, not reconstruction after database loss.

steps.title: Commit lineage and result
steps.caption: The API records the new exact head and parent under compare-and-set, consumes any review reservation, and durably settles the publication result. On the first publication, the immutable approval base is retained and the proved actual parent becomes lineage.base_sha. A later revision requires its exact expected prior head; stale publication, lease and lineage versions cannot settle it.

steps.title: Settle the original thread
steps.caption: The result outbox updates the card and original scoped reply route exactly once; delivery retry does not rerun repository work.

flows.label: GitHub human review
flows.summary: Human review on the current bound pull request becomes a durable fresh turn in the original scoped thread, starting from the exact accepted head and requiring a new approval before the same pull request advances.

steps.title: Authenticate and normalize feedback
steps.caption: The GitHub route verifies the webhook signature and accepts actionable issue comments, pull request review comments, and submitted reviews into one normalized identity.

steps.title: Verify immutable review authority
steps.caption: Fresh provider reads must match the persisted repository, installation, pull request, binding generation, open state, and exact lineage head. Stale heads and terminal, unavailable, ambiguous, or mismatched authority enqueue no turn.

steps.title: Persist audit and durable outbox
steps.caption: The API commits the delivery receipt, normalized feedback, captured lineage version, original scoped reply route, and outbox row together. Per-lineage reservation serializes distinct feedback without dropping it. Factory review admission retains the issue cancellation lock until the revision request and delivery settlement commit together; nested dispatch commits use savepoints.

steps.title: Enqueue the original scoped thread
steps.caption: The reconciler appends a typed review turn to the bounded run stream only from durable outbox state; transport retry cannot create a second feedback identity.

steps.title: Claim without steering
steps.caption: The worker recognizes verified review provenance, uses the stored workspace and reply identity, and never treats review text or links as repository selection.

steps.title: Reverify and reserve the exact head
steps.caption: Immediately before work, the worker repeats provider truth checks and compare-and-set reserves a new revision against the captured lineage head. A changed pull request is refused before the model starts.

steps.title: Prepare the accepted pull request head
steps.caption: The trusted workspace path fetches the exact verified head, sanitizes and privately archives it under the scoped identity, rather than reusing an older sandbox checkout.

steps.title: Materialize exact review input
steps.caption: Credentialless init verifies the private workspace digest and mounts the exact pull request head at /workspace.

steps.title: Cold-claim a fenced replacement
steps.caption: The scoped route swaps only after the exact-head candidate is ready; review feedback never steers a live sandbox with stale files.

steps.title: Run the review turn
steps.caption: The reviewer body is untrusted requested-change context, not authority. The runner starts a fresh turn on the accepted head.

steps.title: Require fresh publication approval
steps.caption: If the turn proposes changes, its new revision enters the publication flow and receives a fresh approval before the fenced lineage can advance the same pull request.

flows.label: Cluster lifecycle
flows.summary: Cluster upgrade resolves and validates the exact target chart before mutation, owns a namespaced CAS checkpoint across nine resumable phases, then proves exact convergence and a target version canary. Retained scalar types and dotted keys survive, and explicit context selection pins Helm and kubectl. Same version verification names skipped phases separately, and Helm timeout must cover the rendered drain budget. Per-consumer chart Secret checksums roll API and worker when caller keys they consume change. Existing connector proxies move on redeploy or reconciliation; foreign Secret contents rotated in place require a manual rollout. An absent or partial caller credential pair refuses before upgrade mutation; upgrade does not generate a missing pair. Cluster up retains installed runner settings, verifies unowned controller reuse and handles rendered RuntimeClass NotFound before install. Cluster teardown bounds owned namespace deletion to 300 seconds, preserves finalizers, and reports remaining phase, conditions, objects and an exact resume command. A remaining owned namespace yields a transient failure unless an independent permanent teardown failure takes precedence. The controller preflight fails on a current cluster-scope NetworkPolicy list/watch refusal or restart-count growth during observation. Namespaced refusals and previous-container failures remain diagnostic. A completed rollout with a stable Ready leader and advancing Lease renewal can pass. After a restart, the startup-log or successful-reconcile path additionally requires that exact current Ready pod to hold and visibly renew the Lease. The historical v0.12.2 released window is 0076 through 0081. The historical v0.12.3 released window is 0076 through 0093. A clean drain now hands off a 300 second lease. Attest renews only existing same-revision authority, schema-migrate renews throughout readiness and migration, and the last pre-upgrade hold hook extends that authority to the configured roll hold. Independent mail persistence and pre-upgrade gVisor checks run before drain. Missing or foreign authority refuses the upgrade without recreating a marker. Failure after the hold can still pause claims for the remaining roll hold; extend-only renewal never shortens a longer lease. The historical v0.12.4 released window remains 0076 through 0093. The v0.12.5 candidate and catalog register schema minimum 0076 and head 0106; migration 0106 follows 0093 and adds nullable approval and publication reply_identity columns. Cluster up, apply, diff and upgrade accept ordered -f/--values-file inputs captured once in owner-only copies. Retained typed values are merged before file inputs, with explicit flags last, and admission uses that final overlay. Inline credentials replacing retained external Secret references clear those references before validation. Metadata CI extraEnv configuration migrates to the typed api.githubFactoryMetadataCi value, preserving object shape and masking rendered JSON. Stock runner layers that cannot be rebound are refused during Validate unless the operator explicitly permits clearing. Dry-run namespace ownership follows the effective controller deployment setting. Direct installs, including eligible fake-model auto installs, can infer gVisor off from a readable empty RuntimeClass node-selector result. Explicit auto refuses and require retains preflight; unreadable evidence authorizes no reduction, and fake-model lookup failure preserves the plan. Prepared apply and dry runs do no scheduling inference; this checks selectors only, excluding taints, cordons, capacity and runtime-handler availability. Failed upgrade phases exit 1 with their structured report. Failed-apply recovery compares API, worker and UI container and init-container image maps; changed images or an unreadable post-apply Deployment force previous_serving=false despite older deployed Helm history. The observation covers image maps only, and recovery preserves the selected context and an available chart operand. Bare rollback resumes the newest pending-rollback only toward a recorded lower deployed or superseded target with the same chart; an unconfirmed target refuses with recovery choices. Schema-gated dry runs require a catalogued application without probing the database. Schema refusals include a next step in human output and JSON; without an asserted live revision, dry run cannot name a safe fail-forward version. Legacy factory configuration migrates before apply, and transient convergence observations share the existing bounded deadline. Failed-only first installs remove data PVCs only after release ownership, installed StatefulSet claim-template matching, revision-one Helm Secret identity, strictly later PVC creation and recorded UID checks. Cleanup deletes proven claims, uninstalls the failed release, and waits for those UIDs to disappear before retry; uncertain provenance refuses cleanup and preserves diagnostics. Cold default-release upgrade dry runs describe stock runner-layer rebinding as conditional until the target chart and runner base are observed. Legacy factory migration omits absent CI policy rather than emitting null required checks. The v0.13.2 release catalog registers schema minimum and head 0108, preserving the v0.13.1 window. Printed Helm and kubectl commands retain the pinned Kubernetes context. Saved cluster-message continuation records the resolved context, with an explicit caller context taking precedence. Connectivity failure with no resolvable context uses the shared operator diagnosis; authorization and other failures keep their own diagnoses. With factory.enabled, the API Deployment and schema-migrate Job default to a shared 2Gi memory limit; other installs default to 512Mi. Explicit api.resources.limits.memory wins, including retained 512Mi under --reuse-values. Memory requests remain 256Mi and CPU remains 100m request and 1 limit. The 2Gi choice is headroom rather than a demonstrated memory requirement. The v0.14.1 application window is 0123 through 0123. Separately, tagged publication requires the complete kind proof described by ADR 0239; release authorization remains its own gate. CI runner OS labels are pinned, and next pull requests select kind proof. Release-workflow edits select the local-release rung. Scheduled kind verification polls the child run at a slower interval and waits through declared rate limits; dispatch failures carry bounded cause text into the tracking report rather than only reporting an absent child run. The v0.14.2 application window registers the same schema minimum and head 0123. When the tagged commit's own required checks are absent or still running, and no current attempt concluded non-passing, release authorization tries every parent with the identical git tree first, including a merge's second parent, and accepts the first whose required checks are current and green. It then walks at most ten first-parent ancestors while the delta stays version-only. Registering this tag's schema window, equal to the ancestor's candidate and changing nothing else in that catalog, still counts as version identity. A parent with a different tree is not consulted. A current failure, cancellation or skip on the tagged commit refuses both paths. The authorizer records the path it used, tree-identical parent or version-only ancestor, and the proof commit. A refused rollback names history builds whose retained manifests declare a window containing the live schema. The v0.14.3 and v0.14.4 application windows and candidate serving metadata all declare schema minimum and head 0140. Exports stream directly into each node using its configured CRI snapshotter with discard-unpacked-layers; no Docker save archive is materialized. The upgrade matrix uses the same streamed import strategy. These are test harness resource bounds, not a production storage guarantee. Disposable upgrade CI force deletes its release pods before deleting their namespace, preserving namespace finalizers. This changes subprocess cleanup, not lifecycle substitutability.

steps.caption: The CLI owns <release>-upgrade-checkpoint in the selected namespace through server observed resourceVersion plus holder and action compare-and-set tests. An active holder refuses a second operation; every completed phase is durable and resumable.

steps.title: Validate all pre-mutation contracts
steps.caption: The driver migrates retained configuration, renders target chart schema metadata, validates the live revision and target version, and refuses pending contract or irreversible migrations unless --forward-only is explicit. For the historical v0.11.2 release, the catalog and API declared schema 0070 through 0070. Absent or partial caller credential pairs refuse before mutation, including dry run, same version verification, and resume; upgrade does not generate a missing pair. Dev caller defaults retain their separate exit guard. The historical v0.12.1 API and release catalog declare 0076 through 0076. The historical v0.12.2 release declares 0076 through 0081, with source-policy and operation structure checked at application startup. The v0.12.5 candidate and catalog declare 0076 through 0106, while the historical v0.12.4 released window remains 0076 through 0093. The v0.14.1 application window requires schema 0123. The candidate and both v0.14.3 and v0.14.4 windows require schema 0140, and the chart resolves factory and standard envelopes while preserving explicit retained resource values.

steps.title: Fence and drain the installation
steps.caption: The pre-upgrade hook writes revision-fenced installation authority and refuses stale or unobserved ownership before the workload roll.

steps.title: Migrate once and apply
steps.caption: The migrate phase is a checkpoint boundary; the chart's pre-upgrade Job owns the one schema migration phase during apply, with api.migrate.forwardOnly merged only after explicit admission. With factory.enabled, the API Deployment and schema-migrate Job default to a shared 2Gi memory limit; other installs default to 512Mi. Explicit api.resources.limits.memory wins, including retained 512Mi under --reuse-values. Memory requests remain 256Mi and CPU remains 100m request and 1 limit. The 2Gi choice is headroom rather than a demonstrated memory requirement.

steps.title: Prove exact convergence
steps.caption: The driver checks target images, observed generations, ready replicas, zero unavailable replicas, hook completion, queue health, and the installed manifest rather than treating Helm success as convergence. Convergence excludes non-deleting Succeeded and Failed pods from replica counting and Node-image discovery. Active surplus and terminating pods still block convergence. Status keeps retained terminal pods visible without counting them as active replicas. The CLI deletes none of them.

steps.title: Canary and commit observed state
steps.caption: A target version smoke canary must pass. Commit reads the release version back from Helm, records that observed version as known good, persists the final checkpoint, and releases only its own holder authority.

flows.label: Factory issue to pull request
flows.summary: Polling observations or optional signed webhooks admit one durable WorkItem for a labelled issue. An isolated agent executes bounded requests, posts status, can be cancelled or recovered, and ends in one pull request or an issue comment. CI and authorized review may revise that same pull request. Declared verification can stop the run before model startup or delegate to named CI checks that must actually pass. An owner-lost factory request settles before a new attempt is admitted on the same WorkItem, bounded to three consecutive owner losses. Status cards show RETRYING only when a successor was admitted; other failed and expired requests show NEEDS HUMAN. Acquired but unstarted requests renew their short lease every twenty seconds. Only not_started deferrals count toward the default five-attempt start cap; capacity and thread-busy waits do not. Started factory CI and approval continuations wait for sandbox capacity within their existing delivery and execution deadlines without charging runner retries. The scoped issue read returns the current execution deadline and total granted seconds. The factory workflow paces its foreground reviews, implementation and verification against that reported grant, rather than assuming a three hour grant. The reported grant can be as long as 43200 seconds. Quickstart now defaults to 10800 seconds, while explicit shorter grants remain authoritative. Sandbox loss after side effects still escalates; Draft ADR 0211 proposes a bounded successor but authorizes no implementation. The factory now uses separate Tracker and CodeHost ports. GitHub with GitHub, Jira Cloud with GitHub, and GitLab with GitLab have passed live acceptance on a dedicated test cluster; GitLab supports gitlab.com and self-managed servers. Bitbucket Cloud and Data Center adapters and Jira quickstarts now ship; the expanded live-provider pairing campaign remains outstanding. One factory agent can serve multiple operator-bound repositories and per-surface trigger labels. Repository runner images are built from a pinned tool catalog, probed and advertised through their immutable manifest. Docker-enabled runs get their own authorized daemon outside the sandbox. The test connector can build images daemonlessly, deploy by digest, run and inspect workloads, and reap only owned expired namespaces. Authenticated acquisition preserves the admitted agent across execution and continuations. Existing owned publications suppress replay without adopting missing lineage history. Bitbucket Cloud refuses an unverified open matching publication as unconfirmed and asks the operator to confirm; this grants no ownership or continuation authority. Tracker intake names credential repair actions and reports missing or inaccessible repositories. A pull request closed without merging ends CI wait as pr_closed before check evaluation. An unpublished revision with a recorded pull request ends as revision_unchanged. Handoff messages retain up to 4000 characters and render as quoted text with HTML, images and mentions neutralized. Budget stops omit raw verification preflight notes, and Jira links the first succeeded publication. Parked capacity waits retry every five seconds, capped at the deadline, without repeating an already delivered notice when no grant was confirmed and the grant is known absent. Factory CI now defaults to 3600 seconds from push, still capped by the execution deadline and preserving explicit operator values. GitHub reads base-branch ruleset and branch-protection required-check names. A required name absent from the published head stays pending until the deadline, then ends ci_unverified and names the missing trigger without applying it. Transient rule-read failures can time out; permanent unreadability refuses immediately. Other code hosts declare required-check reads unsupported rather than simulating them. Migration 0123 stores a redacted workspace preparation stage and reason, capped at 2000 characters, as last_start_failure_detail. Capacity deferrals and worker replacement preserve it; a successful-start compare-and-set clears it. Waiting, exhausted-start and capacity-expiry outcomes retain the previous start diagnosis instead of replacing it with a generic capacity reason. The v0.14.1 application window requires schema minimum and head 0123. The v0.14.3 and v0.14.4 application windows and candidate serving metadata all declare schema minimum and head 0140. Factory quickstart sets max_output_tokens_per_run to 250000 through the ordinary per-agent budget command for supported forge paths and adding an agent to an existing install. A positive --output-tokens overrides it. Generic platform defaults remain 100000; the factory allowance is per run. Human and JSON ready receipts report the selected allowance, with factory-quickstart result schema v1.3. A ResultMessage does not close a turn while a tracked non-ambient SDK background task remains live. The runner continues receive_turn on the same session while accounting usage, retaining existing timeout and budget termination. An exact first-line task-notification prompt preserves the factory review-gate state. A fresh prompt captures its checkout fingerprint in at most two attempts sharing seven seconds; failure stops before plan-review spending. Factory status quotes now neutralize bracket links, references, images and scheme URLs as well as HTML and mentions. Only model-service causes label text Provider message; infrastructure and CI causes use Details. A failed publication warns that its branch or pull request may already exist. A no-change forge loop still persists the terminal notice. A structural workspace stage timeout waits as workspace_timeout without spending a start attempt. Publish requires the base and canonical candidate tree fingerprint from the approving diff review. One advisory plan review completes on either verdict. Diff review permits five completed verdicts per loop; incomplete calls and unchanged rejected candidates spend no round, and already approved candidates cannot be reviewed again. A completed edit clears diff approval. Hook state follows the Curie session and exact checkout root across prompts, keeps separate nested checkouts, and a platform wait_ci continuation opens a new diff loop. Timing comes from the registered get_issue result: execution_deadline D and execution_seconds S. At D minus S//6, no plan review or new implementation round starts. At D minus S//12, edits, Bash and diff review stop; earlier Bash foreground timeouts are capped at the remaining wrap-up allowance. Approved candidates may publish until D. A timed-out Bash command can continue in the background until sandbox termination; an unobserved exit never proves verification. Refusal replies retain unresolved findings while pod logs expose bounded gate causes without those findings. The diff reviewer receives the rendered candidate patch and its base and tree identities. The gate hashes that patch at admission and checks both its digest and the candidate fingerprint before accepting a verdict. A changed or missing patch, changed candidate, or unverifiable checkout requires fresh review without consuming a completed round. State and patch files share the agent user, so this is bundle policy rather than OS isolation or protection from forged state or transient patch replacement. A re-admitted run can retire an open headless lineage only when it has failed publications whose outcomes are durable, all belonging to terminal failed executions of one uncancelled WorkItem for the same agent, thread and repository. The API first proves remote branch absence through CodeHost, then locks and rechecks eligibility and the observed lineage version before closing it. A surviving branch or any unavailable or unauthorized read preserves the old pin. Retired rows without a pull request read as absent; rows carrying a pull request remain terminal. The runner progress tool still applies the later wait_ci cap of three to the shared implement phase, so implement reports for rounds four and five are refused as documented in #5203. The hook separately records all five review_diff rounds; this reporting limit does not lower the review gate cap.

steps.title: Verify the issue observation
steps.caption: Outbound polling uses durable cursors under a replica lock; optional webhooks require signature verification. Both paths verify provider identity, installation, repository, sender and label authority before canonical WorkItem admission. Non-GitHub observations use the binding-scoped Tracker polling path; provider-specific marking authority remains in the adapter.

steps.title: Persist the WorkItem
steps.caption: SQL owns one issue identity, execution requests, per item start authority, waiting, cancellation, deadlines and the status comment outbox. The selected base branch remains recorded through execution and publication. Migration 0123 stores a redacted workspace preparation stage and reason, capped at 2000 characters, as last_start_failure_detail. Capacity deferrals and worker replacement preserve it; a successful-start compare-and-set clears it. Waiting, exhausted-start and capacity-expiry outcomes retain the previous start diagnosis instead of replacing it with a generic capacity reason. The v0.14.1 application window requires schema minimum and head 0123. The v0.14.3 and v0.14.4 application windows and candidate serving metadata all declare schema minimum and head 0140.

steps.title: Dispatch a durable request
steps.caption: The reconciler enqueues bounded execute, terminate or CI continuation events only from recorded state.

steps.title: Claim and recover
steps.caption: The worker acquires the request, waits for capacity when needed, and reconciles orphaned claims without creating a second item. An execution whose sandbox pod is Unschedulable defers as capacity. Delivery and consumer liveness renewals tolerate transport errors only until the last confirmed send plus TTL minus one heartbeat interval. A refused renewal loses authority immediately. Side-effect markers retry before applying the frame, and terminal settlement remains fenced. Runs and evals share this ownership rule. An owner-lost factory request settles before a new attempt is admitted on the same WorkItem, bounded to three consecutive owner losses. Status cards show RETRYING only when a successor was admitted; other failed and expired requests show NEEDS HUMAN. Acquired but unstarted requests renew their short lease every twenty seconds. Only not_started deferrals count toward the default five-attempt start cap; capacity and thread-busy waits do not. Started factory CI and approval continuations wait for sandbox capacity within their existing delivery and execution deadlines without charging runner retries. Owner-loss recovery requires positive capability and sustained absence of the peer alive lease; it never infers death from a missing capability marker.

steps.title: Run the factory bundle
steps.caption: The recorded repository checkout and deadline reach the isolated sandbox; the bundle implements and judges the issue. The worker binds fresh publication precheck context to each covered turn, and an unpublished execute turn gets one continuation. The worker supplies execution scoped issue read authority for platform get_issue; the API reads the issue and comments with its App installation token, and the sandbox receives no GitHub credential. Foreground plan and diff reviews are enforced. The workflow must be loaded and the single advisory plan review must return APPROVE or CHANGES before repository edits; CHANGES findings carry into implementation. Blocked verification without explicit CI delegation selects an offline failure session before the model starts; reviewer credit exhaustion ends the turn. The factory refuses any root .github path change, including case variants, even when requested by the ticket. Edit hooks stop such changes, the diff-review hook checks changed and untracked paths, and the workflow refuses tickets requiring them before partial implementation. Diff review requires a buildable canonical candidate and checks every changed path for the protected root .github directory, including symlink and dotdot traversal; unreadable candidate construction refuses review. The selected repository binding chooses its runner image and tool manifest; optional Docker access targets a run-owned external daemon. The chart resolves standard and factory sandbox profiles. Factory-enabled sandbox egress selects factory unless an agent explicitly chooses another profile: 8Gi memory request and limit, CPU 50m request and 2 limit, ephemeral storage 10Gi request and 20Gi limit, workspace and home ceilings 15Gi each, and tmp 4Gi. Per-agent workspace overrides win over generic workspace values and profile defaults; explicit generic resource pairs use standard values for an unspecified side, and claim-time API resource overrides still win. Explicit zero requests survive, while zero volume ceilings refuse rendering. The default 8Gi memory quota permits one factory sandbox, and existing pods retain their original envelope. An explicit generic writablePathSizeLimit sets every writable path. Older computed generic values retained by --reuse-values keep the old envelope; cluster upgrade takes profile defaults while preserving explicit operator values. Factory quickstart sets max_output_tokens_per_run to 250000 through the ordinary per-agent budget command for supported forge paths and adding an agent to an existing install. A positive --output-tokens overrides it. Generic platform defaults remain 100000; the factory allowance is per run. Human and JSON ready receipts report the selected allowance, with factory-quickstart result schema v1.3. A ResultMessage does not close a turn while a tracked non-ambient SDK background task remains live. The runner continues receive_turn on the same session while accounting usage, retaining existing timeout and budget termination. An exact first-line task-notification prompt preserves the factory review-gate state. A fresh prompt captures its checkout fingerprint in at most two attempts sharing seven seconds; failure stops before plan-review spending. One advisory plan review completes on either verdict. Diff review permits five completed verdicts per loop; incomplete calls and unchanged rejected candidates spend no round, and already approved candidates cannot be reviewed again. A completed edit clears diff approval. Hook state follows the Curie session and exact checkout root across prompts, keeps separate nested checkouts, and a platform wait_ci continuation opens a new diff loop. Timing comes from the registered get_issue result: execution_deadline D and execution_seconds S. At D minus S//6, no plan review or new implementation round starts. At D minus S//12, edits, Bash and diff review stop; earlier Bash foreground timeouts are capped at the remaining wrap-up allowance. Approved candidates may publish until D. A timed-out Bash command can continue in the background until sandbox termination; an unobserved exit never proves verification. Refusal replies retain unresolved findings while pod logs expose bounded gate causes without those findings. The first-party factory runner layer now includes checksum-pinned Helm 3.16.4 for Linux amd64 and arm64, extending its existing toolchain without changing the harness or bundle format.

steps.title: Precheck an empty publication
steps.caption: When a covered call proposes no working tree change, the runner asks the scoped API route to compare the title and body with a fresh pull request read. Stale, unavailable, and unchanged proposals return nonhalting refusals with no pending approval. A changed title or body may proceed with the metadata_changed verdict when bound identity and current CI evidence pass. Local commits alone do not make a publication empty: precheck evaluates the net change from the trusted prepared head and refuses unrelated history.

steps.title: Settle publication
steps.caption: The configured automatic policy and fenced lineage create or revise one pull request, while no pull request ends in one issue comment. Canonical verification observations are required before publication. Failed, missing, or unreadable evidence refuses publication; an unavailable check requires disclosure. A refused factory publication snapshot ends with approval_create_failed and carries the existing redacted, clipped refusal detail into the issue Details line. A sanitized-base mismatch names the first 12 hexadecimal characters of both snapshot and prepared commits; repository mismatch wording and refusal behavior remain unchanged. Publication prose reports CI at pull request creation time and points to the issue status comment for subsequent results. Publication snapshots accumulate the response through EOF under the encoded and decoded size limits. Retryable read faults receive at most three reads within the remaining budget, without rerunning the model. Exhaustion names infrastructure read failure in the issue. Idempotent publication creation and execution settlement writes retry transient API faults within bounded authority; unresolved terminal reports retain heartbeat and sandbox ownership until settlement or the execution deadline. Charged publication reconciliation retries back off from fifteen seconds to five minutes. A publication attempt with no valid recorded publication reports publication_unrecorded and preserves redacted refusal detail in the issue outcome. The worker supplies its retained prepared base to the authenticated /v1/snapshot request; the body must contain exactly one full base_sha. Capture includes the net committed, staged, unstaged and nonignored untracked change from that base, so local commits cannot move publication authority. HEAD must be that base or a locally verified descendant within 256 commits and 1 MiB of commit objects. Missing authority, unrelated or unreadable history, changed HEAD or workspace observations, unsafe paths, changed symlinks or gitlinks, and patches above 900000 raw bytes refuse capture before approval creation. The worker still validates the patch against its private sanitized base.

steps.title: Observe CI and report status
steps.caption: The factory waits for CI for the configured operator wait under the execution deadline and reports the wait_ci phase itself. Failed Actions receive one rerun on the exact current head before a bounded repair round with redacted job log tails. Operator status cards and final outcomes are updated. Every declared delegated check must be observed and pass; unrelated passing checks are insufficient. Accounting separates implementer and reviewer usage, and a missing report stays unknown. When head checks fail, factory CI reads the current base branch head within the remaining observation budget. Matching failing check names or status contexts are reported as pre-existing and excluded from repair, but required Python or delegated checks failing on that base remain unverified. An unreadable base makes every head failure count as caused. Factory status synchronization owns a versioned SQL lease, releases database sessions before GitHub I/O, and runs separately from dispatch reconciliation. Late matching runtime heartbeats may renew before the execution deadline, with one heartbeat-TTL grace before owner-loss cancellation. Verification replay preserves the first observation for an unchanged command. CI reports unavailable required check names and merge_conflict explicitly instead of waiting for checks GitHub will not start. Configured metadata policy remains authoritative. Without it, metadata-only repair uses that round's Valkey-recorded failing checks and status contexts, which must freshly rerun after the edit. No fresh rerun yields checks_not_rerun; partial reruns retain failures missing at deadline, and absent or invalid records yield metadata_ci_not_configured. CI and status operations use CodeHost and MarkedComments; optional unsupported operations produce explicit capability refusals. Factory CI now defaults to 3600 seconds from push, still capped by the execution deadline and preserving explicit operator values. GitHub reads base-branch ruleset and branch-protection required-check names. A required name absent from the published head stays pending until the deadline, then ends ci_unverified and names the missing trigger without applying it. Transient rule-read failures can time out; permanent unreadability refuses immediately. Other code hosts declare required-check reads unsupported rather than simulating them. Factory status quotes now neutralize bracket links, references, images and scheme URLs as well as HTML and mentions. Only model-service causes label text Provider message; infrastructure and CI causes use Details. A failed publication warns that its branch or pull request may already exist. A no-change forge loop still persists the terminal notice.

flows.label: Declared cron turn
flows.summary: Each worker replica computes due cron slots; SQL admits one slot and the worker enqueues a normal bounded turn. A live interactive session makes the scheduled work wait for idle. An operator can test fire a declared schedule through the same admission path. Manual and scheduled admission hold current source authority; any configured policy or operation history closes the ordinary path. Scheduled and manual histories remain separate and retain terminal reasons. Hook fire succeeds only for the durable ran outcome; failed, blocked, skipped and reclaimed outcomes fail while preserving the record and reason. Open runs remain polled until settlement or a transient timeout naming the same-tier record command. Hook record reads an existing run without waiting or judging its outcome. Schedule reads separate newest scheduled and manual histories. Deploy schema v1.2 always includes cron declarations and advisory warnings from the immutable uploaded bundle; unresolved explicit targets warn after successful deployment.

steps.title: Claim one due slot
steps.caption: A unique hook run row and advisory lock prevent duplicate admissions across replicas. A dedicated source gate supplies a fresh snapshot, and configured policy or history refuses ordinary admission before the slot claim.

steps.title: Enqueue the scheduled prompt
steps.caption: The admitted slot becomes a typed cron turn on the shared runs stream. Task-owned source context must remain live before queue and failure effects.

steps.title: Run through the kernel
steps.caption: The normal consumer owns delivery bounds, session routing and the terminal hook outcome.

flows.label: Action execution + verification
flows.summary: The API persists one authorized connector action. The worker executes it without a model. A lost answer after the dispatched commit remains indeterminate and is never repeated. Policy remediation adds declared precondition reads, independent recovery samples, breakers and argument-bound approvals. Qualified protected installation authority is required separately. An executor can read connector Deployments without the reconciler.

steps.title: Persist authority and arguments
steps.caption: Store the approval or policy authority, canonical argument hash, ledger record and execution deadline.

steps.title: Claim a restricted execution sandbox
steps.caption: The target connector binding determines the runtime. Model credentials and unrelated connector secrets are removed.

steps.title: Dispatch once without a model
steps.caption: The runner loads no harness, spends a one-call grant and returns one bounded result. Uncertain dispatch ends indeterminate.

steps.title: Record recovery evidence
steps.caption: Remediation uses a separate declared read connector for verification. Failed recovery opens a breaker and may offer undo only through human approval.

adrs.title: Kubernetes Agent Sandbox as the interactive runtime substrate
adrs.summary: Kubernetes is the production runtime substrate; Docker is the parity implementation behind SandboxClient.

adrs.title: Stateless-first sessions; rehydrate on resume; no cross-hibernation cache assumption
adrs.summary: Sessions are stateless-first; a resumed thread rehydrates from externalized history, and prompt-cache warmth is assumed only within one continuous claim.

adrs.title: Langfuse as the single observability + eval backbone
adrs.summary: Self-hosted Langfuse is the single backbone for traces and eval storage, fed by OTLP over HTTP/protobuf through a thin attribute mapping layer.

adrs.title: claude-agent-sdk adapter behind a frozen ACI
adrs.summary: The outer protocol is strong; the in-runner message types and plugin format retain Claude coupling.

adrs.title: Security rails are chart defaults, not hardening backlog
adrs.summary: The chart ships per-agent ServiceAccounts, default-deny egress, scoped Secrets, hardened containers and default gVisor posture. Documented direct-install inferences may reduce gVisor isolation while preserving the other rails.

adrs.title: Adopt-not-build boundaries; build only five things
adrs.summary: Curie builds only the UI, API, dispatcher, worker and runner glue, CLI, and chart, and adopts license-clean open source for everything else.

adrs.title: Multi-tenancy: one code path, pooled RLS, hard-siloed compute
adrs.summary: Multi-tenancy uses one code path with tenant count 1..N, pooled Postgres with forced row-level security, namespace-per-tenant compute, and per-tenant planes.

adrs.title: Per-agent connector auth
adrs.summary: Connector credentials are named by the bundle and supplied per deployment, giving current MCP servers one service or bot identity rather than a human principal.

adrs.title: Approval gates and human-in-the-loop
adrs.summary: A gated turn persists a durable decision and resumes later through a new event.

adrs.title: A substrate-agnostic worker and a channel-agnostic runner (the thin-shim thesis)
adrs.summary: The worker never learns its substrate and the runner never learns its channel; SandboxClient and a Slack base URL are the two enforcing seams.

adrs.title: Concurrency and delivery: at-least-once streams with an idempotent, side-effect-aware kernel
adrs.summary: Delivery is at-least-once over Valkey Streams consumer groups, made safe by dispatcher dedupe, per-thread locks, a finish-race steer, and no retry after side effects.

adrs.title: A git push is the deploy
adrs.summary: Git flow, immutable bundles, and eval fan-out are built; a red eval does not yet universally enforce promotion.

adrs.title: The credential plane: no broker, prefix-mapped, fail-loud and fail-closed
adrs.summary: A model credential flows from a chart Secret through boot env to the runner with no broker, mapped by key prefix and failing loud and closed.

adrs.title: Swappable jobs around an opinionated core
adrs.summary: One curated default per job; a second implementation teaches the interface instead of a speculative registry.

adrs.title: Tri-language frozen contracts: Pydantic as source of truth, generate the rest, gate on drift
adrs.summary: Pydantic models are the source of truth for frozen contracts; JSON Schema, TypeScript, and Rust are generated derivatives gated on drift in CI.

adrs.title: Freeze the eval-case format: one schema, frozen in place under apps/worker
adrs.summary: The suite-with-graders eval format is canonical and frozen under apps/worker, with a committed schema, drift gate, and a byte-conformant CLI mirror.

adrs.title: Rendering-free channel interface
adrs.summary: Semantic Choice and Confirm still render in Slack and terminal. Discord and email are shipped text surfaces; capability negotiation remains open.

adrs.title: Curie is a harness for coding agents: the CLI's primary user is Claude Code
adrs.summary: The CLI's primary user is a coding agent, so commands emit structured output and semantic exit codes, run non-interactively, and the harness describes itself.

adrs.title: Eval completeness: run the same evals at every tier, grade what actually happened, and promote real traces into cases
adrs.summary: The same eval suite runs at every tier through one grader, grades the whole run, and real traces are promoted into eval cases.

adrs.title: Controller NetworkPolicy RBAC: cluster-scope read, namespace-scope mutate
adrs.summary: The controller has cluster-scope NetworkPolicy read and namespace-scope mutation authority. Preflight rejects current cluster informer refusals and observed restart growth, while namespaced refusals and historical failures remain diagnostic; recovered containers must prove current serving health.

adrs.title: `cluster deploy` reaches the platform API via the UI `/api` proxy
adrs.summary: Without an explicit API URL, cluster deploy discovers and dials the UI /api NodePort proxy instead of self-plumbing a port-forward.

adrs.title: Memory port and first loader
adrs.summary: Scoped state-backed agent memory reaches the runner as a harness-neutral boot preamble.

adrs.title: Extract the storage port now; defer the second (GCS/Azure) adapter
adrs.summary: Blob storage sits behind a structural ObjectStore Protocol with a write-once contract, and no second GCS or Azure adapter is built.

adrs.title: A thin broker port at the non-sacred seams; defer the second broker
adrs.summary: Thin StreamBroker and StreamPublisher Protocols cover the non-sacred stream seams, and no second broker is built ahead of demand.

adrs.title: The sandbox substrate is a resilience-only fallback, not a product swap axis
adrs.summary: The sandbox substrate is an internal resilience and portability seam, not a user-facing choice; Kubernetes and Docker stay maintained, no third substrate.

adrs.title: Conversation-history port and first loader
adrs.summary: A fresh or restarted sandbox rehydrates the same thread from durable transcript state, without SDK-native resume.

adrs.title: Proactive within-episode memory agent
adrs.summary: Drafts an injected within-episode memory agent; automatic generation remains absent.

adrs.title: Explicit named-provider egress, resolved at install
adrs.summary: Provider egress is opened explicitly per named provider and resolved to narrow host CIDRs; ADR-0114 later lets a credential prefix infer the provider.

adrs.title: Scoped, least-privilege sandbox state token
adrs.summary: Each turn gets an HMAC-signed sandbox token scoped to one agent's state namespace, forwarded instead of the raw platform key.

adrs.title: Approval authorizers resolve membership in the API
adrs.summary: The API resolves approver membership itself at click time, failing closed on lookup errors, with four approver sets behind one authorizer.

adrs.title: One-shot post-approval allowance at resume boot
adrs.summary: On resume, the worker injects a single-use, tool-scoped, turn-scoped grant from the durable approval record so the runner allows exactly one approved call.

adrs.title: ACI semver, reader-policy asymmetry, and a wire-lock gate that enforces it
adrs.summary: The ACI version follows its own semver with a change-class table; producers are strict, consumers tolerate unknown fields, and a wire-lock gate enforces it.

adrs.title: Bounded delivery: a delivery cap and a dead-letter graveyard
adrs.summary: A stream entry delivered max_delivery times without success is moved to a dead-letter stream and acked, bounding redelivery.

adrs.title: Every verb is answered at every tier
adrs.summary: Every CLI verb either does the work at a tier or explicitly reports the concept does not exist there, never a fabricated empty result.

adrs.title: LLM-as-a-Verifier grader and progress signal
adrs.summary: The semantic provenance grader is an accepted slot, but no verifier grader exists in Python or Rust today.

adrs.title: Converged approval gates: durable provenance, loud route resolution, and observe-only resume reconciliation
adrs.summary: Both approval paths share one lifecycle: runner-authored gate kind and granted tool are persisted, route resolution fails loud, and resume reconciliation only observes.

adrs.title: ADR-0048: Declare the model endpoint's wire protocol and credential keys
adrs.summary: CURIE_MODEL_API_BACKEND declares the model wire protocol and CURIE_MODEL_ENV_KEY the credential variable; non-Anthropic wires are rejected explicitly.

adrs.title: The boot env is a declared contract: BootEnv, producer ownership, and generated env keys
adrs.summary: The boot env is declared once as BootEnv in aci-protocol, composing SessionConfig, with env keys in the schema so codegen emits every lane's view.

adrs.title: A declared approval policy is armed exactly as declared, or the runner refuses to boot
adrs.summary: Declared approval gates must arm exactly or runner boot refuses. Unknown bare operator names and CLI aliases now fail closed; recognized canonical built-ins and resolvable declared MCP names retain their existing rules.

adrs.title: Add an expected terminal status to the frozen eval-case format
adrs.summary: Eval cases gain an optional expect_status of done or awaiting-approval, so a held approval gate can be asserted as a passing result.

adrs.title: Local Docker runner containers are hardened and network-isolated
adrs.summary: Local Docker runner containers run read-only, capability-dropped, without privilege escalation or the Docker socket, on a network with no data tier.

adrs.title: The fake model is a plumbing fixture, not a subject under test
adrs.summary: The fake model is a plumbing fixture: fake-tier eval turns must complete but are never graded, yielding a distinct plumbing_ok outcome.

adrs.title: The sandbox is a bounded resource envelope; capacity is a tenant boundary
adrs.summary: Every sandbox declares bounded resources on every dimension, bundle ingestion is size-bounded, and tenant capacity is enforced by quotas and priority classes.

adrs.title: The harness is a declared package
adrs.summary: Harness assets and selection are declared; only the built-in Claude contribution exists.

adrs.title: Out-of-process harness boundary
adrs.summary: Would make alternate harness adapters consumable out of process across an Omnigent-compatible wire.

adrs.title: Harness conformance has teeth
adrs.summary: A reusable conformance suite exists; third-party production contributions have not yet proved it.

adrs.title: Message-driven approval reply surface
adrs.summary: In zero-Slack mode, local and cluster message keep the CLI Slack stub alive through the approval window and await the resumed reply on the stream.

adrs.title: Versioned JSON Schemas for every agent-facing CLI result
adrs.summary: Every agent-facing CLI JSON result maps to a committed, versioned JSON Schema listed in an inventory that a contract test enforces.

adrs.title: Agent Proxy credential and egress boundary
adrs.summary: Accepts moving credentials and enforceable FQDN egress outside the sandbox; substrate, TLS termination, credential injection, and implementation remain follow-up work.

adrs.title: A closed, versioned attribute schema for the runner's OTel span stream
adrs.summary: The runner's OTel span attributes come from a closed, versioned key registry, so an unlisted key or wrong type is rejected at the producer.

adrs.title: Route message-driven approval cards through the connected Slack transport
adrs.summary: When a dispatcher is connected, message routes approval cards and resumed replies over the worker's real Slack transport instead of the throwaway stub.

adrs.title: Inbound triggers as a new event kind
adrs.summary: API owned HMAC hooks mint typed webhook sourced QueuedTurn records. Bespoke authenticated producers converge at the queue boundary, and declared cron schedules already ship. Deploy wiring for declared generic webhooks remains planned.

adrs.title: Console sessions and CLI-minted login codes
adrs.summary: The console authenticates with a revocable server-side session cookie obtained by exchanging a single-use login code minted by the CLI.

adrs.title: Bundles declare connectors; the platform hosts them
adrs.summary: The bundle declares MCP connectors and Curie derives their hosted runtime, secrets, policy, and MCP configuration; lifecycle portability remains intertwined with Kubernetes.

adrs.title: The API renders connector objects; the CLI applies them
adrs.summary: The API renders a version's connector Kubernetes objects as a pure function, and the CLI applies and prunes them with operator credentials.

adrs.title: Per-user delegated OAuth for MCP
adrs.summary: Defines principal-scoped OAuth, control-plane-owned grants, a token-hiding MCP gateway, and missing-auth pause and resume semantics. The service-key mode remains separate and cannot silently substitute.

adrs.title: A reconciler applies connectors, so agent repos need no CLI
adrs.summary: An in-cluster reconciler applies API-rendered connector objects to match the in-force deployment, keeping the API read-only and the CLI path available.

adrs.title: Git-flow resolves deploy targets, so one repo serves many agents
adrs.summary: Git-flow maps a pushed branch to a deploy.yaml target and its agent, so one repository can serve several agents under the same trust model.

adrs.title: A GitHub App gives the platform its own repository identity
adrs.summary: The platform authenticates to GitHub as a GitHub App with short-lived per-repository installation tokens, falling back to a configured personal access token.

adrs.title: A bundle carries its own sealed connector keys
adrs.summary: Defines the cross-language sealed-box wire and cluster-owned opening key; end-to-end production delivery is not yet fully connected.

adrs.title: Tiered memory lifecycle
adrs.summary: Defines agent and channel memory tiers, lifecycle turns, trust, and bootstrap/update obligations.

adrs.title: Port adapters are deployed services
adrs.summary: First-party Discord and email adapters are deployed services on the shipped HTTP edge. The generic third-party adapter kit remains unbuilt.

adrs.title: Hooks are bundle-declared turns
adrs.summary: Drafts scheduled and webhook turns with authorization, silence, concurrency, and test-fire semantics.

adrs.title: Agents search their own surface through the channel port
adrs.summary: Proposes a spike before committing channel search verbs; intentionally not current behavior.

adrs.title: External native session checkpoints
adrs.summary: Makes provider-native checkpoints an optional harness capability while retaining portable projection.

adrs.title: An approver is an authenticated principal
adrs.summary: Approval resolution derives authenticated chat, Console, or operator principals from credentials; membership, not requester inequality, decides authority, and the platform key alone cannot resolve.

adrs.title: An agent reads its own runs
adrs.summary: Proposes a first-party scoped runs MCP surface with structured attribution and fail-closed identity.

adrs.title: Deploy targets carry environment values
adrs.summary: Moves environment-specific non-secret values onto deploy targets while preserving connector declaration shape.

adrs.title: Retention, capacity, and back pressure are one policy
adrs.summary: Accepted. When the deployment publishes CURIE_SANDBOX_ADMISSION, the worker admits a sandbox claim against that quota envelope and live headroom before creating it. The rest of the decision's queue and retention policy is not newly settled by this release.

adrs.title: Deterministic security posture classification
adrs.summary: Computes posture from shipped layers and operator gates instead of trusting a configured label.

adrs.title: Default memory compaction algorithm
adrs.summary: Drafts opt-in, from-source compaction with validation, scope defaults, and an auditable write path.

adrs.title: Bundles declare connector build inputs and tiers deliver pinned images
adrs.summary: Bundles list external MCP servers in .mcp.json and hosted connectors in connectors.yaml, where a build form is built and run as a pinned digest.

adrs.title: Session identity arrives over the ACI so a sandbox can be pre-bound
adrs.summary: The claim path can bind a warm sandbox before the turn by passing session identity over the ACI, without changing isolation rails.

adrs.title: A tool that changes the world reports what it changed
adrs.summary: The action ledger records mutations with conditional SQL completion and undo acquisition. A redacted result keeps neither prior nor post state and cannot promise undo. Restore remains a connector owned verb under accepted ADRs 0121 and 0124, and an acquired undo is not proof its restore ran. ADR 0203 requires approval for undo of a policy-executed remediation.

adrs.title: Binding cardinality is the multi-surface opt-in
adrs.summary: One agent may bind several (kind, address) surfaces. Adding Discord or email does not clone the bot identity.

adrs.title: Durable first-party email state
adrs.summary: The mail adapter keeps ingress and reply ownership in local SQLite with one serialized writer, not in-process maps.

adrs.title: A restore is the connector's own verb, run under the same pinned connector
adrs.summary: The connector-owned restore executor is accepted, with execution under the original pinned connector. The executor is not implemented.

adrs.title: A pending approval's approver set does not follow its route binding
adrs.summary: The allowed approver set is captured when the approval is created and does not track a later binding change.

adrs.title: A snapshot is sealed to the connector that wrote it
adrs.summary: Connector-sealed snapshots are accepted; sealing and the restore executor remain planned.

adrs.title: Managed repository workspaces and approval-gated publication
adrs.summary: The platform clones and publishes through its own GitHub identity. Write credentials do not remain inside the sandbox. First publication can replay the approved patch on a descendant base tip, with API ancestry proof and fenced actual-parent persistence.

adrs.title: Runtime repository selection is sticky authorized thread state
adrs.summary: The selected repository sticks on the thread as authorized state rather than being re-derived from the prompt.

adrs.title: One release owns a cluster's shared singletons; every other release declares what it needs from them
adrs.summary: One release owns cluster singletons; other releases use them without creating or deleting them.

adrs.title: Deliberate progress is bounded durable channel state
adrs.summary: Progress is durable channel state with a bound, not a substitute for streaming the final answer.

adrs.title: A delivery has one deadline and one renewable fenced owner
adrs.summary: Stream delivery ownership is a renewable fence with one deadline. A second replica cannot steal a live delivery.

adrs.title: A hook shares one thread per partition
adrs.summary: Drafts per-delivery conversation identity for hooks so concurrent firings do not share one thread by default.

adrs.title: A late workspace handoff replaces the sandbox at a fenced turn boundary
adrs.summary: A workspace-capable thread may begin generically, prepare a replacement from durable scoped state, and compare-and-set swap its route only at a turn boundary while retaining prior history and keeping credentials outside the sandbox.

adrs.title: Coding tools are built in and an initial repository URL selects the workspace
adrs.summary: Coding tools and publication are platform session capabilities. An initial allowed repository URL can establish scoped workspace state, while the legacy deployment bit is not the runtime coding gate and late replacement follows ADR 0136.

adrs.title: Curie supports one model harness until a second one exists
adrs.summary: Would retain only the production-read Claude contribution fields and stop speculative multi-harness work until a real second engine can teach the contract; as a Draft it authorizes nothing.

adrs.title: Database compatibility is a release contract; migrations run in one upgrade phase
adrs.summary: Each API image publishes a machine-readable serving window, the target chart is validated before mutation, contract or irreversible migrations require explicit forward-only admission, and one chart phase owns schema migration.

adrs.title: A coding thread owns one fenced pull request lineage
adrs.summary: One scoped server thread and repository own at most one active pull request lineage. Review work starts from the exact verified head, every revision needs fresh approval, and publication compare-and-set advances the same pull request while stale or terminal authority is refused. For a first publication, the writer fetches the API-authoritative base branch and, if its tip advanced, replays the approved patch onto that descendant tip. Conflict, empty replay, unrelated history and replay failure stop publication. The API verifies the revision marker and one parent, proves the approved base is an ancestor of that parent and the parent is an ancestor of the current base tip, with one is_ancestor request per relation. GitHub answers from the status of one three-dot compare. Equal shas count as ancestors, and a forge that cannot answer leaves the publication unproved. The immutable approval base stays unchanged; lineage settlement records the actual first parent under publication, lease and lineage fences. Later revisions still require the exact prior published head. Rejected-Job and ambiguous open-request recovery require exact quiescence before settlement; this does not implement database-loss adoption.

adrs.title: The cluster lifecycle admits before it mutates, and its pause authority is installation-scoped
adrs.summary: Records the shipped v0.8.x lifecycle gates: installation and revision scoped quiesce authority, namespace admission before Helm, schema admission before rollback, and clean retry after a never-good install. Draft status records built behavior without accepting the decision. Under ADR 0209, a clean drain leaves a 300 second handoff lease, attest and migration renew existing authority, and the final hold hook extends it to the configured roll hold.

adrs.title: A channel port turn carries its attachments
adrs.summary: Channel HTTP ingress now accepts opaque attachment references and copies them onto QueuedTurn. The worker selects Slack or generic binding endpoint transport and uses the adapter egress credential for the latter. Discord and mail still emit no references, so their producing half remains unproved.

adrs.title: A channel adapter is a principal, and its credential is scoped to what an adapter does
adrs.summary: A deployed channel adapter receives a bounded adp credential with only channel token rotation, approval listing, and approval resolution scopes for the binding rows it serves. It enters the shared ApprovalPrincipal boundary without presenting the platform key.

adrs.title: Tenant boundary and principal identity land together
adrs.summary: The accepted identity model adds tenant, human principal, provider installation, durable bot identity, shareable agent release, and agent installation concepts in ordered additive stages. None of those schema or enforcement stages is implemented at this pin.

adrs.title: A custom connector is a bundle built HTTP MCP server that holds its own credential
adrs.summary: The draft proposes an authoring contract for bundle-built HTTP MCP servers whose provider credential stays outside the runner sandbox. Historical spike evidence proves the core hosted connector loop, but the draft authorizes no new platform surface.

adrs.title: A long scheduled sweep stays on one sandbox
adrs.summary: A scheduled sweep claims one cron slot and runs through one sandbox on the shared bounded stream.

adrs.title: Signed GitHub issue events admit one WorkItem
adrs.summary: Signed GitHub issue events admit one canonical WorkItem after installation, repository and sender checks.

adrs.title: WorkItems own durable execution identity
adrs.summary: Durable WorkItems and ExecutionRequests own factory execution identity, admission, cancellation and recovery.

adrs.title: The tracker owns dependencies and Curie admits ready work
adrs.summary: The draft would let tracker dependencies gate factory admission; no dependency enforcement is shipped.

adrs.title: Tenant boundary and principal identity land together
adrs.summary: Tenant schema groundwork is present; broader principal and installation boundaries remain unfinished.

adrs.title: Agent and channel memory are written by the agent, guided by editable guidance
adrs.summary: Agents load attributed agent and channel facts and write through bounded memory tools when the operator enables writes.

adrs.title: One installation hosts several bot identities
adrs.summary: One installation hosts several declared Slack identities. The relay separates reply delivery from binding identity, and durable approvals and publications preserve that selector across pauses, resolution and publication admission.

adrs.title: A mean tester tests an agent the way a person does, from any installation
adrs.summary: The mean tester probes an agent through ordinary surfaces and reports observations.

adrs.title: Conversation transcripts live in their own per-thread table
adrs.summary: Conversation transcripts moved to a capped per thread table with terminal and idle expiry.

adrs.title: A factory run may take three hours and is bounded by time, not turns
adrs.summary: The turn budget and the rule that a request deadline is fixed at start still stand. ADR 0249 raises the per-agent deadline ceiling, the worker delivery budget ceiling, and the runner request ceiling from 10800 seconds to 43200 seconds. Shipped chart defaults stay at 10800 seconds and the default agent deadline stays 1800 seconds.

adrs.title: The mean tester is one bundle on off-the-shelf MCP servers, and it only reports
adrs.summary: The shipped mean tester uses existing MCP servers and reports observations. ADR 0181 limits every probe to reading or asking, including on test installations.

adrs.title: A bundle may layer its own runner image on the platform's
adrs.summary: Bundle layered runner images are built and selected for deployments with platform base validation. Releases publish the first party factory runner layer, and rendering records layer and platform base digest locks.

adrs.title: Publication prechecks use an execution scoped capability
adrs.summary: Covered factory execute and CI turns carry an optional versioned ACI publication context with a signed ppc capability scoped only to publication.precheck. The runner shares one decision across the stream observer, PreToolUse hook, and can_use_tool, and compares an empty workspace snapshot against a fresh API side pull request read, returning nonhalting refusals without pending approval state. It amends ADR 0143 so this one comparison route accepts the scoped credential. Metadata only publication can revise the bound pull request under current identity and CI evidence, and admission still checks independently.

adrs.title: A bot may limit who can talk to it
adrs.summary: A binding caller list refuses an unapproved speaker before a turn or placeholder is created.

adrs.title: A factory run may test end to end in a namespace it owns on a separate cluster
adrs.summary: Factory test policy permits a named isolated namespace on a separate test cluster.

adrs.title: An approval is answered where it was asked, including by email
adrs.summary: Approval route selection, email card egress and scoped authorization are implemented. Current AgentMail replies cannot establish verifiable sender authentication, so the adapter refuses them before resolving approvals; existing accepted delivery replies remain available. Accepted ADR 0220 partially supersedes amendment A1 to A3 for agents that name an approver team. That team check is implemented: membership replaces the route default, a declared route set only narrows it, and agents without an approver team keep their existing route behavior, including email lists. Card location is unchanged.
